# Changelog

## DMAR 1.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-11-15

### Breaking Changes in 1.1.0

DMAR 1.1.0 names the total sample size, the number of predictors, a
planner’s planning value, and the desired width one way, and names an
argument for the quantity it holds rather than for a symbol. The DMAR
1.0.x names listed here are not accepted: a call that gives one stops
with R’s “unused argument” error. The exceptions, all of them, are
listed under Old Names That R Still Matches, after the table. There is
no deprecation period and no function that maps an old name to a new
one. Change the call. Three functions are removed, with no alias; the
call that replaces each is given under One Function for Each ANOVA
Effect Size.

#### The Count in the Partial and Semipartial Correlation Functions Changed Meaning

[`var_partial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_partial_r.md),
[`var_semipartial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_semipartial_r.md),
[`expected_partial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/expected_partial_r.md),
[`ss_aipe_partial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_partial_r.md),
[`ss_aipe_semipartial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_semipartial_r.md),
[`ss_aipe_partial_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_partial_r_sensitivity.md),
and
[`ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity.md)
took `J`, the number of variables partialed out. They take `p`, the
total number of predictors in the regression of Y on X and the variables
partialed out, in the place `J` held, and `p = J + 1`. **A DMAR 1.0.x
call that gave the count by position still runs, and now describes one
fewer variable partialed out.** `var_partial_r(.3, 100, 2)` was a
partial correlation given two other variables and is now a partial
correlation given one; `ss_aipe_partial_r(.3, 2, .2)` planned for two
variables partialed out and now plans for one. Add 1 to the count in
every such call: `var_partial_r(.3, 100, 3)`,
`ss_aipe_partial_r(.3, 3, .2)`. A call that named the count (`J = 2`)
stops with “unused argument” and becomes `p = 3`. `p` must be a whole
number of at least 2; with nothing partialed out the correlation is the
simple correlation, which
[`var_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_r.md),
[`expected_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/expected_r.md),
[`ss_aipe_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_r.md),
and
[`ss_aipe_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_r_sensitivity.md)
cover.

#### One Function for Each ANOVA Effect Size

- **`eta_squared_partial()`, `omega_squared_partial()`, and
  `ci_eta_squared_partial()` are removed.**
  [`eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/eta_squared.md),
  [`omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/omega_squared.md),
  [`ci_eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_eta_squared.md),
  and
  [`ci_omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_omega_squared.md)
  take `estimand = c("all", "total", "partial")` and report the total
  and the partial value of each effect in columns of their own (see
  Total and Partial Eta Squared and Omega Squared). There is no alias.
  Replace

  | DMAR 1.0.x call | DMAR 1.1.0 call |
  |----|----|
  | `eta_squared_partial(fit)` | `eta_squared(fit, estimand = "partial")` |
  | `eta_squared_partial(F_value = , df_effect = , df_error = )` | `eta_squared(F_value = , df_effect = , df_error = )` (the partial value; `estimand = "partial"` leaves out the `NA` total column) |
  | `omega_squared_partial(fit)` | `omega_squared(fit, estimand = "partial")` |
  | `omega_squared_partial(F_value = , df_effect = , df_error = , N = )` | `omega_squared(F_value = , df_effect = , df_error = , N = , estimand = "partial")` |
  | `ci_eta_squared_partial(fit)` | `ci_eta_squared(fit, estimand = "partial")` |
  | `ci_eta_squared_partial(F_value = , df_effect = , df_error = , N = )` | `ci_eta_squared(F_value = , df_effect = , df_error = , N = , estimand = "partial")` |

- **The columns of the four tables are named for the estimand.** A
  script that read `$eta_squared`, `$omega_squared`, `$ci_lower`, or
  `$ci_upper` from these tables reads the new name. The values under the
  old names were the partial values, and the new argument does not
  change them.

  | function | DMAR 1.0.x column | DMAR 1.1.0 column |
  |----|----|----|
  | [`eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/eta_squared.md) | `eta_squared` | `eta_squared_partial` |
  | [`omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/omega_squared.md) | `omega_squared` | `omega_squared_partial` |
  | [`ci_eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_eta_squared.md) | `eta_squared`, `ci_lower`, `ci_upper` | `eta_squared_partial`, `eta_squared_partial_ci_lower`, `eta_squared_partial_ci_upper` |
  | [`ci_omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_omega_squared.md) | `omega_squared`, `ci_lower`, `ci_upper` | `omega_squared_partial`, `omega_squared_partial_ci_lower`, `omega_squared_partial_ci_upper` |

  With `estimand = "all"`, the default, the columns of the total
  (`eta_squared_total`, `omega_squared_total`, and for the intervals
  `eta_squared_total_ci_lower` and so on) come before those of the
  partial value; `estimand = "partial"` gives the table of 1.0.x with
  the new names. The `effect`, `stratum`, `F_value`, `df_effect`,
  `df_error`, and `N` columns are unchanged.

- **`estimand` is the second argument** of
  [`eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/eta_squared.md),
  [`omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/omega_squared.md),
  [`ci_eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_eta_squared.md),
  and
  [`ci_omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_omega_squared.md),
  after `object`. A call that gave `F_value` by position (as the second
  argument) stops; name it.

- **`tidy()` of these tables gives one row per effect and estimand**,
  the rows of the total before those of the partial value, with `term`
  naming the estimand (`"eta_squared_total"`, `"eta_squared_partial"`)
  where it named `"eta_squared"`. `glance()` of a table with more than
  one row of `tidy()` gives the estimands in `term`, separated by a
  comma.

#### Renamed Arguments

An argument is named for the quantity it holds and for the role of the
value. A population value that a planner or a sensitivity function takes
begins with `true_`, as do those of the analysis of variance, analysis
of covariance, and regression data generators; the value a sensitivity
function plans the design from begins with `supposed_` (`estimated_` or
`est_` in DMAR 1.0.x, which suggested an estimate from data, where the
value is a planning assumption); and a null value begins with `null_`.
The quantity is named in words: a correlation is `cor` (`true_cor`,
`true_cor_YX`, `cor_lower`), a contrast `contrast` and a standardized
one `std_contrast`, a regression coefficient `reg_coef` and a
standardized one `std_reg_coef`, a squared multiple correlation `R2`, a
mean `mean`, a standard deviation `sd` (`true_sd`, and `true_sd_X` and
`true_sd_Y` when the variable is named), a population variance
`true_var_` followed by what it is the variance of (`true_var_within`,
`true_var_error`, `true_var_trend`), a covariance matrix `cov_matrix`, a
factor loading `factor_loading`, and a residual variance `residual_var`.
A function that computes the same quantity from population values or
from estimates
([`cohen_f()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cohen_f.md),
[`ci_srsnr()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_srsnr.md),
[`covmat_from_cfa()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/covmat_from_cfa.md),
[`var_ete()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_ete.md),
[`var_indirect_effect()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_indirect_effect.md))
names its arguments without a role. A sample size given so that the
power or the precision at that size is returned is `specified_N` (the
total, or the one group) or `specified_n_per_group`. The table gives the
name each argument had in DMAR 1.0.x.

#### Old Names That R Still Matches

R matches an argument name by its leading characters, and a function
that passes `...` to another program does not refuse a name itself. The
table lists 602 old names, a name counted once for each function that
had it. Of these, 536 stop with “unused argument”. These 66 do not:

- **The same quantity under its new name; the call runs as before.**
  `w =` in
  [`ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity.md)
  and
  [`design_consequences()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/design_consequences.md)
  (matched to `width`); `df_res =` in
  [`ss_power_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_sem.md)
  (`df_restricted`); `n =` in
  [`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md),
  [`ci_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova.md),
  [`ci_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc_ancova.md),
  [`equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_c.md),
  [`cohen_f()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cohen_f.md),
  [`is_orthogonal_set()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/is_orthogonal_set.md),
  [`variance_components_mls()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/variance_components_mls.md),
  [`simulate_anova_data()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/simulate_anova_data.md),
  [`simulate_ancova_data()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/simulate_ancova_data.md),
  [`ss_seq_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_seq_c.md),
  [`mr_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_smd.md),
  and
  [`power_equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/power_equivalence_c.md)
  (matched to `n_per_group`, the per-group size it always was; in the
  five power planners that took `n` and take `specified_n_per_group`,
  [`ss_power_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c.md),
  [`ss_power_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_sc.md),
  [`ss_power_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c_ancova.md),
  [`ss_power_split_plot_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_split_plot_anova.md),
  and
  [`ss_power_composite_ancova_2group()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_ancova_2group.md),
  `n =` now stops with “unused argument”); and `n =` in
  [`power_equivalence_md()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/power_equivalence_md.md),
  [`power_density_equivalence_md()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/power_density_equivalence_md.md),
  and
  [`power_equivalence_md_plot()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/power_equivalence_md_plot.md)
  (matched to `n_per_treatment`, the same quantity, now that the degrees
  of freedom are `df_error` and no other argument begins with `n`: a
  1.0.x call that gave the degrees of freedom by position runs, and one
  that named `nu` stops for `nu`). Write the full name: the match is
  R’s, it is not a name these functions have, and it ends the day one of
  them gains another argument that begins with the same letters.
- **Another argument; the call stops, with a message about something
  else.** `es =` in the six `ss_aipe_crd_es_*()` functions is matched to
  `es_type` when `es_type` is left out, and the call stops where the
  effect size is needed, with a message about `es_type` or about the
  missing effect size; a fixed-budget call that does not ask for the
  expected width never used the effect size and still runs. `a =` in
  [`ss_power_indirect_effect()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_indirect_effect.md)
  is matched to `alpha_level`, so a 1.0.x call stops for the unused `b`.
  `n =` in
  [`ecvi()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ecvi.md) is
  matched to `npar` when `npar` is left out, and the call stops for the
  missing `multiplier`; a call that also names `npar` stops with “unused
  argument”. `f =` in
  [`ss_power_factorial_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_factorial_anova.md)
  and
  [`ss_power_factorial_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_factorial_ancova.md)
  is matched to `factor_levels` when the levels are given by position,
  and the call stops because a value of Cohen’s *f* is not a vector of
  levels; a call that names `factor_levels` stops with “unused
  argument”.
- **More than one argument; the call stops.** `w =` in
  [`ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity.md),
  [`ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.md)
  stops with “argument matches multiple formal arguments”
  (`which_predictor`, `width`), as does `n =` in
  [`ci_c_ancova_bp()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova_bp.md)
  (`n_per_group`, `n_covariates`), in the five
  `simulate_longitudinal_*()` functions (`n_per_group`, `n_occasions`),
  in [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md)
  (`n_per_group`, `ncp`), and in
  [`simulate_ancova_factorial_data()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/simulate_ancova_factorial_data.md)
  (`n_per_cell`, `n_covariates`). `d =` in
  [`ss_power_mixed_effects()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_mixed_effects.md)
  stops with the same message when `desired_power` and `directional` are
  both left out; when one of them is named, `d` is matched to the other
  and the call stops for the missing `true_smd`.
- **Another argument, or `...`; the function reads the name and stops.**
  `n =` in
  [`var_icc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_icc.md)
  would be matched to `n_raters`, and in
  [`var_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_alpha.md)
  to `n_items`, so a call that named only the sample size and gave the
  count by position, `var_alpha(.80, n = 100, 10)` or
  `var_icc(.60, n = 30, 4)`, would run with the two values exchanged:
  100 items and 10 respondents, or 30 raters and 4 subjects. `n =` in
  [`bayes_one_sample_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bayes_one_sample_t.md)
  would be matched to `null_mean`, so a call that named the sample size
  `n` would take it as the comparison value for the mean. The three
  functions read the names in the call and refuse `n` with a condition
  of class `dmar_argument_invalid` that says to write `N =`. A 1.0.x
  call of
  [`var_icc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_icc.md)
  or
  [`var_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_alpha.md)
  that named every argument also named `k` or `p_items` (and `rho` in
  [`var_icc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_icc.md))
  and stops with “unused argument”; `n =` in
  [`bayes_paired_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bayes_paired_t.md),
  which has no argument that begins with `n`, stops with “unused
  argument” too. Four names would reach a `...`: `t_value =` in
  [`ci_nc_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_nc_t.md),
  which was a second name for `ncp`, would pass to the root finder;
  `mu_0 =` in
  [`ci_mahalanobis()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_mahalanobis.md)
  would reach the root search of
  [`ci_nc_F()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_nc_F.md);
  `psi =` in
  [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md) would
  reach
  [`ci_nc_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_nc_t.md)
  and stop inside its root finder; and `psi =` in
  [`ci_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova.md)
  would be dropped without a word under `procedure = "t"` and passed to
  [`ci_c_ancova_bp()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova_bp.md)
  under `"bryant_paulson"`. Each function refuses the name with the same
  class and says to write `ncp =`, `null_mean =`, or `contrast =`.
- **Given to a function that passes `...` to lavaan, beside the new
  arguments; the function reads the name and stops.** `Sigma =`,
  `pop_model =`, `mu =`, `desired_width =`, and `N =` in
  [`ss_aipe_composite_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_composite_sem.md);
  `Sigma =`, `pop_model =`, `mu =`, and `N =` in
  [`ss_power_composite_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_sem.md);
  `Sigma =` and `N =` in
  [`ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity.md);
  `Sigma =` and `desired_width =` in
  [`ss_aipe_sem_path()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sem_path.md);
  and `est_Sigma =`, `true_Sigma =`, `desired_width =`, and `N =` in
  [`ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity.md)
  (`true_Sigma` was that function’s 1.0.x name for the generating
  matrix, now `true_cov_matrix`). Each of the five functions checks the
  names in `...` against the arguments and options of lavaan before
  anything is fitted, and a name that is neither is refused with a
  condition of class `dmar_argument_invalid` that gives the name as it
  was typed and points to the function’s Renamed arguments section.
- **Given to a function that takes `...` for its root search; the call
  stops, but not with “unused argument”.** `chi_square =` in
  [`ci_nc_chisq()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_nc_chisq.md)
  goes to `...`, and the call stops at once because `chisq` is missing
  (class `dmar_argument_invalid`). `sigma_squared =` in
  [`ci_srsnr()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_srsnr.md)
  with `means` stops the same way because `var_within` is missing; with
  `F_value`, it reaches the noncentral *F* search, which stops with
  “unused argument (sigma_squared = …)” inside a condition of class
  `dmar_computation_failed`.

[`ci_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_cv.md),
[`ss_aipe_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c.md),
[`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md),
[`ss_aipe_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2.md),
[`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md),
[`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md),
[`ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity.md),
[`ss_aipe_sm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sm.md),
and
[`ss_power_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2.md)
took `...` and used it for nothing, so a name they did not have was
dropped without a word and the call ran on the default of the argument
that was meant: `ss_power_R2(true_R2 = .3, p = 3, N = 50)` planned for
the default power and returned 36. They no longer take `...`, and any
name they do not have, old or misspelled, is an “unused argument”. The
two counts of the simulation that `ss_aipe_R2(verify_ss = TRUE)` runs,
which were read from `...` as `g` and `G`, are the arguments `G_initial`
(the replications for each candidate *N* of the coarse search) and `G`
(the replications of the final pass); `g` and `G` differed only in case.
[`ci_c_ancova_bp()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova_bp.md)
and the three Bryant-Paulson distribution functions took a `...` they
did not use and no longer take it, for the same reason:
`ci_c_ancova_bp(num_covariates = 2)` would otherwise have been computed
for the default of one covariate without a word. So did
[`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md),
[`ci_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_reg_coef.md),
[`plot_randomization_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_randomization_test.md),
and
[`R2_mixed_effects()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/R2_mixed_effects.md),
and [`ci_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_rc.md) and
[`ci_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_src.md),
which passed theirs to
[`ci_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_reg_coef.md),
where nothing read it; none of the six takes `...` now. No exported
function is left with a `...` that its body does not use.
[`covmat_from_cfa()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/covmat_from_cfa.md)
read only `tol_det` from its `...`, so a misspelled name, or a third
value given by position, was dropped without a word; `tol_det` is now an
argument of its own, after `factor_loading` and `residual_var`, and the
function takes no `...`.

In
[`ss_power_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_r.md)
the name `N` is gone and no other argument took it:
`ss_power_r(true_cor = .3, N = 50)` stops, and the call is
`ss_power_r(true_cor = .3, specified_N = 50)`. The null value was
`rho_0` and is `null_cor`, as the other null values are `null_R2` and
`null_rmsea`; the 1.0.x planning value `rho` then matches nothing and
stops.

[`ss_aipe_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c.md)
takes the error variance one way, as `true_var_error`, the name in
[`ss_aipe_c_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_sensitivity.md)
and
[`ss_power_contrast()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_contrast.md).
`MSwithin` was a second name for it and `SD` was its square root; both
are gone, with the three checks that the values agreed, so a 1.0.x call
that gave `SD = s` gives `true_var_error = s^2`. A population contrast
is `true_contrast` in every planner and an observed one `contrast`; the
standardized contrast is `true_std_contrast`, where the two standardized
contrast sensitivity functions called it `true_psi`, the 1.0.x name of
the unstandardized contrast elsewhere.

In the planners for the analysis of variance, Cohen’s *f* is a planning
value and is `true_f`, beside `true_eta_squared` and
`true_eta_squared_partial`, in
[`ss_power_one_way_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_one_way_anova.md),
[`ss_power_rm_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_rm_anova.md),
[`ss_power_split_plot_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_split_plot_anova.md),
[`ss_power_factorial_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_factorial_anova.md),
and
[`ss_power_factorial_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_factorial_ancova.md);
the row of
[`ss_power_contrast()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_contrast.md)
that holds the *f* of the contrast is `true_f` too (`effect_size_f`).
Cohen’s *f* squared is `true_f2` in
[`ss_power_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2.md),
[`ss_power_R2_change()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2_change.md),
[`ss_power_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_reg_coef.md),
and
[`ss_power_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_rc.md),
the argument and the row. The correlation among the repeated measures
and the sphericity value of
[`ss_power_rm_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_rm_anova.md)
and
[`ss_power_split_plot_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_split_plot_anova.md)
are `true_cor` and `true_epsilon`, and the proportion of within-cell
variance the covariates explain in
[`ss_power_factorial_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_factorial_ancova.md)
is `true_covariate_R2`. The five planners report the noncentrality
parameter in the row `noncentral_f_parm`, the name in
[`ss_power_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2.md),
and the degrees of freedom in `df_effect` and `df_error`, the names in
[`ss_aipe_omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_omega_squared.md)
and
[`ci_eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_eta_squared.md).
The number of subjects of
[`ss_power_rm_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_rm_anova.md),
each measured on every occasion, is the total sample size, so it is
`specified_N` when given and the row `necessary_N` when planned.

[`cohen_f()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cohen_f.md),
[`ci_srsnr()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_srsnr.md),
and
[`covmat_from_cfa()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/covmat_from_cfa.md)
are calculators, not planners: each computes the same quantity from
population values or from sample summaries and estimates, so their
arguments carry plain quantity names without `true_`.
[`cohen_f()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cohen_f.md)
takes `means`, `var_within`, `n_per_group`, `eta_squared`, `sd_means`,
and `sd_within` (`mu`, `sigma_squared`, `n`, `sigma_m`, `sigma`); given
population values it returns the population *f*, and given sample
summaries it returns the plug-in value from the same calculation, which
is not an unbiased estimate of *f*.
[`ci_srsnr()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_srsnr.md)
takes the observed group means, `var_within` (the pooled within-group
mean square; `sigma_squared`), and `n_per_group` as an alternative to
`F_value`; with population values in their place, the interval is a
hypothetical one, not an interval from observed data and not the
expected interval of a planned study.
[`covmat_from_cfa()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/covmat_from_cfa.md)
takes the factor loadings and residual variances, population values or
estimates from a fitted model, as `factor_loading` and `residual_var`
(`lambda`, `psi_squared`), and returns its matrix as the element
`model_implied_cov` (`population_cov`): the matrix is unchanged, and the
new name says what it is whether the loadings and residual variances are
population values or estimates.
`covmat_from_cfa(lambda = l, psi_squared = p)$population_cov` is
`covmat_from_cfa(factor_loading = l, residual_var = p)$model_implied_cov`.

The planners for composite power in the analysis of variance and
covariance
([`ss_power_composite_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_anova.md),
[`ss_power_composite_factorial_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_factorial_anova.md),
[`ss_power_composite_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_ancova.md),
[`ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova.md),
[`ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova_het()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova_het.md),
and
[`ss_power_composite_ancova_2group()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_ancova_2group.md))
name their population values as the single-effect planners do:
`true_means`, `true_sd`, `true_cor` (the covariate correlations,
`correlations`), `true_covariate_R2`, and `true_sd_X`, the standard
deviation of the covariate (`sd_cov`), which is the name the two ANCOVA
contrast sensitivity functions give the same quantity. **The fields of
each element of `effects` are renamed too: Cohen’s *f* is `true_f` and
partial eta squared is `true_eta_squared_partial`** (`f`,
`partial_eta_squared`), so `list(factors = 1, f = 0.25)` becomes
`list(factors = 1, true_f = 0.25)`. A field is not an argument and R
does not check it, so the planners now do: an element of `effects` with
a field they do not read is refused (see Calls That Are Now Refused).
The rows follow: `true_f_<label>`, `noncentral_f_parm_<label>`, and
`df_error`, the names the single-effect planners use. The total sample
size beside the per-cell or per-group answer is the row `total_N` in
both branches, the rule for an implied total everywhere else in the
package (it was `necessary_N` beside a planned size and `specified_N`
beside a size that was given); when the correlations differ in absolute
value and the size was planned, it is `approximate_total_N` beside
`approximate_n_per_cell` or `approximate_n_per_group` (`approximate_N`).
The attributes the
[`plot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/graphics/plot.default.html) method reads
from the tables of
[`ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova_het()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova_het.md)
and of `ss_power_composite_ancova(slopes = "heterogeneous")` (`means`,
`correlations`, `sigma`, `sd_cov`) are renamed with the arguments:
`true_means`, `true_cor`, `true_sd`, and `true_sd_X`.
[`ss_power_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c_ancova.md)
takes `true_sd` and `specified_n_per_group` (`sigma`, `n`), as
[`ss_power_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c.md)
does.

A size per group is `n_per_group` and a size per cell is `n_per_cell`,
in the estimators as in the planners:
[`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md),
[`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md),
[`ci_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova.md),
[`ci_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc_ancova.md),
[`equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_c.md),
[`cohen_f()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cohen_f.md),
[`is_orthogonal_set()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/is_orthogonal_set.md),
[`variance_components_mls()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/variance_components_mls.md),
[`ss_seq_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_seq_c.md),
[`mr_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_smd.md),
[`simulate_anova_data()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/simulate_anova_data.md),
and
[`simulate_ancova_data()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/simulate_ancova_data.md)
took `n` and take `n_per_group` (one number for equal groups, or one per
group where the function allowed it);
[`ss_power_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c.md),
[`ss_power_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_sc.md),
and
[`ss_power_split_plot_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_split_plot_anova.md),
where the size is given so that the power at that size is returned, took
`n` and take `specified_n_per_group`;
[`simulate_ancova_factorial_data()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/simulate_ancova_factorial_data.md)
takes `n_per_cell`.
[`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md) and
[`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md) had `n`
and `N`, a per-group size and the total, apart only by the case of one
letter. In
[`power_equivalence_md()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/power_equivalence_md.md),
[`power_density_equivalence_md()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/power_density_equivalence_md.md),
and
[`power_equivalence_md_plot()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/power_equivalence_md_plot.md)
the size is `n_per_treatment`: the number of subjects who receive each
treatment, which is the size of each group in a parallel design and
every subject in a crossover, the n of the standard error sigma \*
sqrt(2 / n) in both. The three functions take the equivalence bounds as
`lower_bound` and `upper_bound`, the true difference or ratio as
`true_effect`, and the error degrees of freedom as `df_error`
(`ltheta1`, `ltheta2`, and `ldiff` in
[`power_equivalence_md()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/power_equivalence_md.md),
`theta1`, `theta2`, and `diff` in the other two, and `nu` in all three).
The grid attached to the plot keeps its column labels (`n=24`); its
first column, `diff`, is `true_effect`.
[`power_equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/power_equivalence_c.md)
takes `n_per_group` for independent groups; the number of units of a
paired design, new in this release, is `N` (see Equivalence and
Noninferiority of a Contrast).

The contrast planners name their population values as the sensitivity
functions do. The error standard deviation is `true_sd` in
[`ss_power_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c.md),
[`ss_power_equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_equivalence_c.md),
and
[`power_equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/power_equivalence_c.md)
(`sigma`), as in
[`ss_seq_c_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_seq_c_sensitivity.md);
[`ss_power_contrast()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_contrast.md)
takes `true_means` and `true_var_error` (`mu`, `sigma_squared`);
[`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md)
takes `true_sd_anova`, `true_sd_ancova`, and `true_sd_ratio` (`ratio`
alone is an allocation ratio elsewhere); and the values the two ANCOVA
contrast sensitivity functions generate their data from are
`true_mean_Y`, `true_sd_Y`, `true_mean_X`, and `true_sd_X`. The data
generators for the analysis of variance and covariance and for
regression name their population values the same way:
[`simulate_anova_data()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/simulate_anova_data.md)
takes `true_mean` and `true_sd` (`mu`, `sigma`);
[`simulate_ancova_data()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/simulate_ancova_data.md)
takes `true_mean_Y`, `true_mean_X`, `true_sd_Y`, `true_sd_X`, and
`true_cor` (`mu_y`, `mu_x`, `sigma_y`, `sigma_x`, `rho`), and
[`simulate_ancova_factorial_data()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/simulate_ancova_factorial_data.md)
the same with `true_cor_YX` and `true_cor_XX` (`rho_y_x`, `rho_x_x`);
and
[`simulate_regression_data()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/simulate_regression_data.md)
takes `true_cor_YX`, `true_cor_XX`, `true_mean_Y`, `true_mean_X`,
`true_sd_Y`, and `true_sd_X` (`rho_YX`, `rho_XX`, `mu_Y`, `mu_X`,
`sigma_Y`, `sigma_X`).
[`mr_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_smd.md) and
[`mr_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_cv.md) keep
the symbols of the published procedure (`A`, `epsilon`, `gamma`, `m0`);
their rows now name the sizes they hold: `n_1` and `n_2` and
`pilot_n_per_group` in
[`mr_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_smd.md), `N`
and `pilot_N` in
[`mr_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_cv.md).
[`var_omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_omega_squared.md)
takes the value its formula is evaluated at as `true_omega_squared`
(`population_omega_squared`), the name in
[`ss_aipe_omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_omega_squared.md).
In the six `ss_aipe_crd_es_*()` functions write `true_es =`, and in
[`ss_power_mixed_effects()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_mixed_effects.md)
`true_smd =`; what R does with `es =` and `d =` is under Old Names That
R Still Matches.

[`ss_power_pcm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_pcm.md)
and
[`ss_aipe_pcm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_pcm.md)
give the variance of the individuals’ change coefficients and the level
one error variance the same names, `true_var_trend` and `true_var_error`
(`tau` and `level_1_variance` in
[`ss_power_pcm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_pcm.md),
`variance_trend` and `error_variance` in
[`ss_aipe_pcm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_pcm.md)),
and
[`ss_aipe_pcm_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_pcm_sensitivity.md)
plans from `supposed_var_trend` and `supposed_var_error`.
[`ss_aipe_pcm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_pcm.md)
takes the sampling-error variance of one individual’s estimated change
coefficient (Kelley & Rausch, 2011, Equation 19) as
`true_var_trend_error` (`variance_true_minus_estimated_trend`), and
[`ss_power_pcm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_pcm.md)
reports the same quantity in the row of that name
(`error_var_of_slopes`).
[`ss_power_pcm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_pcm.md)
took the group difference in the change coefficient as `beta` and a
flag, `standardized`, that said whether `beta` was divided by the
between-subject standard deviation of the change coefficient. It takes
the difference under the name of its scale: `true_std_reg_coef` for the
standardized difference (`beta` under the 1.0.x default) and
`true_reg_coef` for the difference in the units of the change
coefficient (`beta` with `standardized = FALSE`). Exactly one is given;
both or neither is refused with a condition of class
`dmar_argument_invalid`.
`ss_power_pcm(beta = -.4, tau = .003, level_1_variance = .0262, frequency = 1, duration = 4, N = 238)`
is
`ss_power_pcm(true_std_reg_coef = -.4, true_var_trend = .003, true_var_error = .0262, frequency = 1, duration = 4, specified_n_per_group = 119)`.
The two come first among the arguments, so a 1.0.x call that gave
`beta`, `tau`, and `level_1_variance` by position gives both and is
refused rather than read on the other scale. The table reports the
difference on both scales, in the rows `true_reg_coef` and
`true_std_reg_coef` (`unstd_coefficient`, `std_coefficient`), whichever
was given, and the power is unchanged. The help of
[`ss_power_pcm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_pcm.md)
keeps the symbols of Raudenbush and Liu (2001) in its formulas and says
which argument each one is.

In the planners for an indirect effect each path is a standardized
regression coefficient of the population the plan is made for, so the
paths are `true_std_reg_coef_a`, `true_std_reg_coef_b`, and
`true_std_reg_coef_direct`, and the product of the two paths is the row
`true_std_indirect_effect`. The power of the indirect effect in
[`ss_power_indirect_effect()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_indirect_effect.md)
is the row `power_ab` (`actual_power`), followed by `power_a` and
`power_b`, and `tidy()` and `glance()` read it as the power of the
design.
[`var_indirect_effect()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_indirect_effect.md)
computes the same variances from population values or from estimates,
raw or standardized, so its arguments carry neither `true_` nor `std_`;
[`mediate()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediate.md)
keeps its rows `a` and `b`, which are estimates.

In the planners for structural equation models a population covariance
matrix is `true_cov_matrix` and the matrix a sensitivity study is
planned from is `supposed_cov_matrix`; the rows of
[`ss_power_composite_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_sem.md)
that echo the population value of each parameter are `true_<label>`, as
in
[`ss_aipe_composite_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_composite_sem.md).
In
[`ss_power_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_sem.md)
`df` and `df_full` keep their names.

In the functions for one sample and for paired data, the size of the one
sample, the number of pairs, and the number of trials are each the total
sample size, so
[`bayes_one_sample_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bayes_one_sample_t.md),
[`bayes_paired_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bayes_paired_t.md),
[`ci_proportion()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_proportion.md),
and
[`ci_eigenvalue()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_eigenvalue.md)
take `N`; a call that gave the size by position
(`ci_proportion(17, 50)`) is unchanged. The eigenvalue that
[`ci_eigenvalue()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_eigenvalue.md)
brackets was chosen with `k` and is chosen with `which_eigenvalue`, as
`which_predictor` and `which_path` choose theirs. The per-group sizes of
[`bayes_independent_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bayes_independent_t.md),
[`ci_ratio_of_means()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_ratio_of_means.md),
and
[`design_consequences()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/design_consequences.md)
keep `n_1` and `n_2`. In
[`ss_aipe_cliff_delta()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cliff_delta.md)
`ratio` keeps its name (the allocation ratio is a constant of the
design, not a planning value).

A null value is `null_` followed by the quantity.
[`bayes_one_sample_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bayes_one_sample_t.md)
and
[`ci_mahalanobis()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_mahalanobis.md)
take the comparison value of the mean as `null_mean` (`mu_0`), and
[`welch_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/welch_t.md) and
[`summary_t_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/summary_t_test.md)
take the null value of the difference between the means as
`null_mean_diff` (`mu`), beside `null_cor` in
[`ss_power_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_r.md),
`null_R2` in
[`ss_power_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2.md),
and `null_rmsea` in
[`ss_power_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_sem.md).

The proportion of intervals no wider than the desired width is the row
`pct_ci_less_width` in every sensitivity function and in
[`design_consequences()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/design_consequences.md)
(`pct_ci_less_w`; every other name in the package spells the width out),
and the rows of
[`ss_aipe_composite_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_composite_sem.md)
that hold the same proportion for each parameter are
`pct_ci_less_width_<label>` (`width_within_desired_<label>`).

A count is `n_<things>`. The number of groups is `n_groups` in
[`cv_tukey_hsd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cv_tukey_hsd.md),
[`cv_bryant_paulson()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cv_bryant_paulson.md),
and the three Bryant-Paulson distribution functions (`groups`,
`num_groups`), and the number of random covariates is `n_covariates`
there and in
[`ci_c_ancova_bp()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova_bp.md)
(`covariates`, `num_covariates`); `covariates` in
[`ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ancova.md) and
[`mediate()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediate.md)
names columns and keeps its name. The per-group size of
[`ci_c_ancova_bp()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova_bp.md)
is `n_per_group`. The number of random permutations of
[`procrustes_phi()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/procrustes_phi.md)
is `n_resamples`, the name in
[`randomization_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/randomization_test.md),
[`randomization_test_paired()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/randomization_test_paired.md),
and
[`vargha_delaney_A()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/vargha_delaney_A.md).
The five `simulate_longitudinal_*()` functions take `n_per_group`, the
number of units in each population (one number, or one per population;
never a total), and `n_occasions`, the number of measurement occasions
per unit. In
[`ecvi()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ecvi.md) the
divisor is `multiplier`: it is the multiplier with which the chi square
was formed from the fit function, the total sample size under the normal
likelihood and the total less the number of groups under the Wishart
likelihood, so `n` named it for one case only.

The number of items is `n_items`, the number of raters `n_raters`, the
number of clusters `n_clusters`, and the number of level one units in a
cluster `cluster_size`, in every function that takes or reports one.
[`ss_aipe_reliability()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reliability.md)
and
[`ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity.md)
took the number of items as `i` and
[`var_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_alpha.md)
as `p_items`; the row of
[`reliability()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability.md),
[`reliability_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_alpha.md),
[`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md),
[`reliability_omega_categorical()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega_categorical.md),
and
[`reliability_kr20()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_kr20.md)
that holds it was `J` and is `n_items`, the name `glance()` already gave
it, and the row of
[`ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity.md)
was `items`.
[`ss_aipe_icc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_icc.md),
[`ss_aipe_icc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_icc_sensitivity.md),
and [`var_icc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_icc.md)
took the number of raters as `k`; the help keeps *k* in the formulas and
in the names of the forms (`"ICC(1,k)"`).
[`ss_power_mixed_effects()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_mixed_effects.md)
took `n`, `rho`, and `J` and takes `cluster_size`, `true_icc`, and
`specified_n_clusters_per_arm`: the number of clusters in each arm, not
the total `n_clusters`, so its rows are `necessary_n_clusters_per_arm`
and `specified_n_clusters_per_arm`, and its noncentrality parameter is
in the row `noncentral_t_parm`, as in
[`ss_power_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c.md)
and
[`ss_power_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_smd.md).
`cluster_size` has no default and is checked first.

An intraclass correlation that a planner takes as a planning value is
`true_icc`: in
[`ss_aipe_icc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_icc.md)
(`rho`) and
[`ss_aipe_icc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_icc_sensitivity.md)
(`true_rho`; a correlation is `true_cor` everywhere else, and the value
the sensitivity study is planned from is `supposed_icc`, which was
`estimated_rho`), in
[`ss_power_mixed_effects()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_mixed_effects.md)
(`rho`), in the twelve `ss_aipe_crd_*()` functions (`icc_Y`), and in
[`ss_aipe_mixed_effects()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_mixed_effects.md)
(`icc`).
[`var_icc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_icc.md)
takes the intraclass correlation its variance is evaluated at as `icc`,
as in
[`design_effect()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/design_effect.md).

The total variance of the outcome in a two-level plan is
`true_total_var`: in
[`ss_aipe_mixed_effects()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_mixed_effects.md)
(`sigma2_y`) and
[`ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity.md)
(`true_sigma2_y`, with `supposed_total_var` for `estimated_sigma2_y`),
and in the `ss_aipe_crd_*()` functions (`total_var`), where
`true_var_within` is the within-cluster variance alone. Two names that
differed by one capital no longer hold two quantities. The sensitivity
function also plans from `supposed_var_X` and `supposed_icc`
(`estimated_sigma2_x`, `estimated_icc`) and takes the population slope
as `true_reg_coef` (`true_beta`), whose simulated summaries are the rows
`mean_reg_coef`, `median_reg_coef`, and `sd_reg_coef`.

The twelve planners for a cluster randomized design name every
population value with `true_`: `true_var_between`, `true_var_within`,
`true_total_var`, `true_icc`, `true_R2_between`, and `true_R2_within`,
and in the six for the standardized effect size `true_icc_covariate`
(`icc_Z`) beside `true_es`. The number of covariates beside the
treatment indicator is `n_covariates` (`num_predictors`; the value is
unchanged, and the total number of predictors is
`p = n_covariates + 1`). The number of individuals in a cluster is the
argument `cluster_size` of the four functions that take it
(`n_individuals`); the functions that solve for it report it in the row
`necessary_cluster_size`, beside `necessary_n_clusters` in the two that
solve for both, and a size that was given is not repeated in the table.
The function names keep `n_individuals`. The four functions that plan
from a width echo it in the row `width`, as the other AIPE planners do,
and the `width` column of `tidy()` and `glance()` is that desired width
for every AIPE planner (`NA` for a plan made from a budget and for a
planner that does not echo the request); the expected or assured width
is the `glance()` column of that name. The number of processes of the
six `ss_aipe_crd_es_*()` functions is `ncpus` (`multicore`, `num_proc`),
the name in the bootstrap functions. The two costs are `cluster_cost`
and `individual_cost`, and the number of simulated data sets of the six
`ss_aipe_crd_es_*()` functions is `G`, as in every other function that
simulates (`nrep`). The row that reports the width no longer carries the
effect or the assurance in its name: it is `expected_width` without an
assurance and `assured_width` with one, and the assurance is in a row of
its own, `assurance`. In 1.0.x the row was, for example,
`width_of_unstd_conditions_diff_with_0.8_assurance`, a name that changed
with the value asked for.

[`ss_aipe_reliability()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reliability.md)
names its population as a planner does: `true_cov_matrix` (`S`, which is
a sample covariance matrix in the estimators), `true_factor_loading`
(`lambda`), `true_residual_var` (`psi_square`), and
`true_item_covariance` (`cor_est`: the help defines it as the common
covariance of every pair of items, which is their correlation only for
standardized items, and it is a planning value, not an estimate). The
replications of the two stages of its assurance search are `G_initial`
and `G` (`initial_iter`, `final_iter`), the names in
[`ss_aipe_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2.md),
and an assurance plan reports the rows `assurance`,
`assurance_attained`, and `G` (`specified_assurance`,
`empirical_assurance`, `final_iter`), the names in
[`ss_aipe_partial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_partial_r.md)
and
[`ss_aipe_semipartial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_semipartial_r.md).
The estimators
([`reliability_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_alpha.md)
and the rest) keep `S`, `data`, and `items`. The reliability
[`ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity.md)
plans from is `supposed_reliability` (`estimated_reliability`): a
planning assumption, not an estimate from data.

The measurement model and item response functions name their parameters
for what they are (see the table).
[`irt_information()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/irt_information.md)
reports the grid in the column `trait_value` and carries the attributes
`discrimination`, `threshold`, and `trait_value_max_information`; the
columns `a` and `b` of an
[`irt_grm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/irt_grm.md)
table keep their names, and the help of
[`irt_grm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/irt_grm.md) and
[`irt_information()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/irt_information.md)
says what they are. A call of
[`irt_information()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/irt_information.md)
that gives the values by position is unaffected.

Every population value a planner for a regression coefficient takes
carries `true_` and is named for its quantity: the coefficient is
`true_reg_coef_j` in the units of the data and `true_std_reg_coef_j`
when it is standardized (DMAR 1.0.x used `b_j` for the first and
`beta_j` for both), a squared multiple correlation is `true_R2_`
followed by its variables, and the standard deviations and correlations
are `true_sd_Y`, `true_sd_X`, `true_cor_XX`, and `true_cor_YX`. The
estimators name what they are given the same way, without `true_`
(`reg_coef_j`, `se_reg_coef_j`, `sd_Y`, `sd_X`, `std_reg_coef_j`).

The regression coefficient sensitivity functions lost `standardize`: the
name of the function says the scale.
[`ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity.md),
[`ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity.md),
and
[`ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity.md)
report the unstandardized coefficient, as their 1.0.x default did, and
[`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.md)
reports the standardized one, as its 1.0.x default did. A call that gave
`standardize` stops with “unused argument”. The default of `noncentral`
is `TRUE` in
[`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.md)
and `FALSE` in the other two, as in DMAR 1.0.x, so the call that
replaces `ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity(standardize = TRUE)` or
`ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity(standardize = TRUE)` is
`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity(noncentral = FALSE)`, and the call that
replaces
`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity(standardize = FALSE, noncentral = FALSE)` is
[`ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity.md).
`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity(standardize = FALSE)`, with its default
`noncentral = TRUE`, becomes
`ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity(noncentral = TRUE)`, which is refused when the
sample size is planned from supposed variances that are not 1 (see Calls
That Are Now Refused). With `standardize = TRUE`,
[`ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity.md)
gave the same power (the *t* statistic does not depend on the scale), so
such a call drops the argument.

One name has one meaning, and the bounds of an equivalence region are
named for the quantity they bound: `smd_lower` and `smd_upper`,
`contrast_lower` and `contrast_upper`, `cor_lower` and `cor_upper`, and
`prop_diff_lower` and `prop_diff_upper` in
[`equivalence_proportion_paired()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_proportion_paired.md),
which is new;
[`plot_equivalence()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_equivalence.md),
which draws whatever estimates it is given, takes `effect_lower` and
`effect_upper`.
[`cles()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cles.md),
[`nnt_from_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/nnt_from_smd.md),
and
[`proportion_of_superiority()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/proportion_of_superiority.md)
used `smd_lower` and `smd_upper` for confidence limits on *d*, as
arguments and as rows; those are now `smd_ci_lower` and `smd_ci_upper`,
the names DMAR gives the limits of an interval named for its estimate,
so `cles(smd = .5, smd_lower = .2, smd_upper = .8)` stops with “unused
argument”.
[`convert_delta_lambda()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/convert_t_smd.md)
takes `smd`, and
[`convert_lambda_delta()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/convert_t_smd.md)
and
[`convert_lambda_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/convert_R2.md)
take `ncp`; the function names keep their symbols.

#### Renamed Output Rows and Columns

A row or column that echoes a renamed argument is renamed with it, a row
that summarizes simulated estimates is named for the quantity
(`mean_reg_coef_j`, `mean_contrast`, `mean_std_contrast`), and the
columns of the per-replication files that the sensitivity functions
write with `filename` follow the rows they summarize. Code that looks a
row or column up by its 1.0.x name must be changed, because an old name
matches nothing and gives no error: `x$value[x$term == "rho"]` returns
`numeric(0)`. The columns of
[`eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/eta_squared.md),
[`omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/omega_squared.md),
[`ci_eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_eta_squared.md),
and
[`ci_omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_omega_squared.md)
are under One Function for Each ANOVA Effect Size.

**The limits of every confidence interval are `ci_lower` and
`ci_upper`.** DMAR 1.0.x named them `lower_limit` and `upper_limit` in
most functions and `ci_lower` and `ci_upper` in the coefficient tables
and the `tidy()` results. One pair is now used everywhere, as a row of a
long table, a column of a wide one, and a suffix of a limit named for
its estimate (`rmsea_ci_lower`, `cles_ci_lower`).
`x$value[x$term == "lower_limit"]` becomes
`x$value[x$term == "ci_lower"]`, and `x$lower_limit` becomes
`x$ci_lower`.

| function | DMAR 1.0.x | now |
|----|----|----|
| every function that reports a confidence interval | rows or columns `lower_limit`, `upper_limit` | `ci_lower`, `ci_upper` |
| every function whose limits are named for their estimate | `<estimate>_lower_limit`, `<estimate>_upper_limit` (for example `cles_lower_limit`, `smd_upper_limit`, `shift_lower_limit`, `loa_upper_lower_limit`, `mean_lower_limit`) or `<estimate>_lower`, `<estimate>_upper` (for example `tau2_lower`, `indirect_upper`, `sigma2_b_lower`, `eta_squared_partial_upper`) | `<estimate>_ci_lower`, `<estimate>_ci_upper` (`cles_ci_lower`, `smd_ci_upper`, `shift_ci_lower`, `loa_upper_ci_lower`, `mean_ci_lower`, `tau2_ci_lower`, `indirect_effect_ci_upper`, `sigma2_between_ci_lower`, `eta_squared_partial_ci_upper`) |
| [`combine_p()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/combine_p.md) | row `k` | row `n_studies` |
| [`welch_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/welch_t.md), [`summary_t_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/summary_t_test.md) | row `t_statistic` | row `t_value` |
| [`pairwise_within()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/pairwise_within.md), [`ci_dunnett()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_dunnett.md), [`ci_dunnett_t3()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_dunnett_t3.md) | column `t_statistic` | column `t_value` |
| [`contrast_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_test.md) | column `t` | column `t_value` |
| [`contrast_adjusted()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_adjusted.md), [`bayes_one_sample_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bayes_one_sample_t.md), [`bayes_paired_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bayes_paired_t.md), [`bayes_independent_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bayes_independent_t.md) | row `t` | row `t_value` |
| [`ci_scheffe()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_scheffe.md) | columns `contrast_value`, `F_statistic` | columns `estimate`, `F_value` |
| [`ci_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova.md) | row `psi` | row `contrast`, as in [`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md) |
| [`ci_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc_ancova.md) | row `psi` | row `std_contrast`, as in [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md) |
| [`equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_c.md) | rows `psi_hat`, `delta_lower`, `delta_upper` | rows `contrast`, `contrast_lower`, `contrast_upper` (the lower bound is still signed); [`plot_equivalence()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_equivalence.md) reads them |
| [`ci_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_rc.md) | rows `lower_limit`, `upper_limit` only | rows `ci_lower`, `reg_coef`, `ci_upper`: the coefficient sits between its limits, as in [`ci_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_reg_coef.md) and [`ci_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_src.md) |
| [`var_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_r.md) | row `var_r_bonett_wright` | removed with `kurtosis_x` and `kurtosis_y` (see Calls That Are Now Refused) |
| [`ss_aipe_partial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_partial_r.md), [`ss_aipe_semipartial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_semipartial_r.md), [`ss_aipe_partial_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_partial_r_sensitivity.md), [`ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity.md) | row `J` | row `p`, holding `p` |
| [`expected_partial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/expected_partial_r.md) | columns `n`, `J`, `rho` | columns `N`, `p`, `true_cor` |
| [`expected_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/expected_r.md) | columns `n`, `rho` | columns `N`, `true_cor` |
| [`equivalence_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_r.md) | rows `n`, `rho_lower`, `rho_upper` | rows `N`, `cor_lower`, `cor_upper` (the lower one still holds the negative bound) |
| [`ss_aipe_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_r.md), [`ss_power_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_r.md), [`ss_aipe_partial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_partial_r.md) | row `rho` | row `true_cor` |
| [`ss_power_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_r.md) | row `rho_0` | row `null_cor` |
| [`ss_aipe_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_r_sensitivity.md), [`ss_aipe_partial_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_partial_r_sensitivity.md) | rows `true_rho`, `estimated_rho` | rows `true_cor`, `supposed_cor` |
| [`ss_aipe_semipartial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_semipartial_r.md) | row `r_sp` | row `true_r_sp` |
| [`ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity.md) | row `estimated_r_sp` | row `supposed_r_sp` (beside the new rows `true_R2_full` and `supposed_R2_full`) |
| [`ss_aipe_equivalence_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_equivalence_r.md) | row `population_r` | row `true_cor` |
| [`ss_aipe_equivalence_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_equivalence_r_sensitivity.md) | rows `true_r`, `estimated_r`, `rho_lower`, `rho_upper` | rows `true_cor`, `supposed_cor`, `cor_lower`, `cor_upper` |
| [`ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity.md), [`ss_power_R2_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2_sensitivity.md) | row `estimated_R2` | row `supposed_R2` |
| [`ss_power_R2_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2_sensitivity.md) | rows `mean_F`, `median_F`, `sd_F` | rows `mean_F_value`, `median_F_value`, `sd_F_value` |
| [`expected_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/expected_R2.md) | row `expected_value_population_R2` | row `expected_R2`, as [`var_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_R2.md) reports `var_R2` (the value is unchanged) |
| [`ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity.md), [`ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity.md) | rows `mean_b_j`, `median_b_j`, `sd_b_j`, `true_b_j`, `estimated_b_j` | rows `mean_reg_coef_j`, `median_reg_coef_j`, `sd_reg_coef_j`, `true_reg_coef_j`, `supposed_reg_coef_j` |
| [`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.md) | rows `mean_b_j`, `median_b_j`, `sd_b_j`, `true_b_j`, `estimated_b_j` | rows `mean_std_reg_coef_j`, `median_std_reg_coef_j`, `sd_std_reg_coef_j`, `true_std_reg_coef_j`, `supposed_std_reg_coef_j` (the standardized coefficient, as `true_std_reg_coef_j` in [`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md)) |
| [`ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity.md) | rows `mean_b_j`, `median_b_j`, `sd_b_j`, `mean_se_b_j`, `median_se_b_j`, `sd_se_b_j`, `true_b_j`, `estimated_b_j`, `mean_t`, `median_t`, `sd_t` | rows `mean_reg_coef_j`, `median_reg_coef_j`, `sd_reg_coef_j`, `mean_se_reg_coef_j`, `median_se_reg_coef_j`, `sd_se_reg_coef_j`, `true_reg_coef_j`, `supposed_reg_coef_j`, `mean_t_value`, `median_t_value`, `sd_t_value` |
| [`ci_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_cv.md) | rows `c_of_v`, `c_of_v_unbiased` | rows `cv`, `cv_unbiased` |
| [`ss_aipe_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_smd.md), [`ss_power_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_smd.md), [`ss_power_composite_ancova_2group()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_ancova_2group.md) | row `supposed_smd` | row `true_smd` |

| [`ss_aipe_equivalence_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_equivalence_smd.md) | row `population_smd` | row `true_smd` |
| [`ss_aipe_smd_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_smd_sensitivity.md) | rows `true_delta`, `estimated_delta` | rows `true_smd`, `supposed_smd` |
| [`ss_aipe_equivalence_smd_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_equivalence_smd_sensitivity.md) | rows `estimated_smd`, `delta_lower`, `delta_upper` | rows `supposed_smd`, `smd_lower`, `smd_upper` |

| [`ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity.md), [`ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity.md) | columns `b_j`, `ll_ci_beta_j`, `ul_ci_beta_j`, `r_2`, `se_b_j`, `t_for_b_j` of the per-replication file written with `filename` | columns `reg_coef_j`, `ci_lower`, `ci_upper`, `R2`, `se_reg_coef_j`, `t_value` |
| [`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.md) | the same six columns of its file | columns `std_reg_coef_j`, `ci_lower`, `ci_upper`, `R2`, `se_std_reg_coef_j`, `t_value` |
| [`ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_reg_coef_sensitivity.md) | columns `b_j`, `se_b_j`, `t_stat`, `r_2` of its file | columns `reg_coef_j`, `se_reg_coef_j`, `t_value`, `R2` |
| [`ss_power_R2_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2_sensitivity.md) | columns `r2`, `f_stat` of its file | columns `R2`, `F_value` |
| [`ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity.md) | columns `r2`, `lower_width_ci`, `upper_width_ci`, `width_ci` of its file | columns `R2`, `ci_width_lower`, `ci_width_upper`, `ci_width`, the names of the rows that summarize them |
| [`ss_aipe_c_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_sensitivity.md) | column `psi_hat` of its file | column `contrast` |
| [`ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity.md) | columns `psi_obs`, `se_psi`, `se_psi_restricted` of its file | columns `contrast`, `se_contrast`, `se_contrast_restricted` |
| [`ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity.md), [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity.md) | column `psi_obs` of the file | column `std_contrast` |
| [`ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity.md), [`ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity.md) | columns `ci_low`, `ci_up` of the file | columns `ci_lower`, `ci_upper`; a file begun by DMAR 1.0.x keeps its header when a run appends to it |
| [`var_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_cv.md) | rows `var_cv_mckay`, `var_cv_vangel` | row `var_cv_normal`, which holds the value that `var_cv_mckay` held; `var_cv_vangel` is removed (see Changes to Earlier Results) |

The reasons for each name are in One Notation for the Regression and
Correlation Functions, below.

The removed rows `suc_rep` and `num_probs_with_cis` held counts of
replications, which every sensitivity function now reports one way, in
the `simulation` attribute of its table (see Changes to Earlier
Results): `suc_rep` was the number of replications that gave an
interval, and `num_probs_with_cis` the number that did not.
[`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md)
returns the same table for every kind of input; the table of DMAR 1.0.0
is not returned for any call, and there is no warning period (see
Coefficient H From a Fitted Model).

The column that holds a test statistic is `test_statistic` wherever the
reference distribution depends on an option: under `test = "t"` in
[`vargha_delaney_A()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/vargha_delaney_A.md),
and under a finite `wald_df` in the multilevel and confirmatory factor
analysis tables, the statistic is referred to Student’s *t*, so
`z_value` named it wrongly. The meta-analysis functions named their
statistic `t` under `hartung_knapp = TRUE` and `z` without it (`z` in
[`meta_contrast()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/meta_contrast.md));
it is `test_statistic` in all four, with the reference distribution in
the attributes `test_distribution` and `test_df` and in a line under the
printed table, and the table of
[`meta_contrast()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/meta_contrast.md)
now has the class `dmar_meta_contrast`, a `dmar_tbl`. Otherwise a column
whose name is always true keeps it (`z_value` in
[`cohen_kappa()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cohen_kappa.md)
and
[`fleiss_kappa()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fleiss_kappa.md),
`t_value` in
[`welch_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/welch_t.md) and
its relatives).

The common language effect size is the row `cles` wherever it is
reported: [`cles()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cles.md)
named it `cl`, as
[`randomization_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/randomization_test.md)
did not, and
[`results_sentence()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/dmar_output_helpers.md)
on a [`cles()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cles.md)
table begins “cles =” where it began “cl =”.

[`ss_power_R2_change()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2_change.md)
is new in this release, so its rows `true_f2` and `true_partial_R2` have
no 1.0.x names; they are named as planning values like every other row
that holds one. The same holds for the other functions new in this
release:
[`ss_aipe_two_phase()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_two_phase.md),
[`ss_aipe_two_phase_cost()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_two_phase_cost.md),
and
[`ss_aipe_two_phase_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_two_phase_sensitivity.md)
echo `true_cor`, and the sensitivity function `supposed_sd_Y` and
`supposed_cor`;
[`equivalence_proportion_paired()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_proportion_paired.md)
reports its bounds in the rows `prop_diff_lower` and `prop_diff_upper`;
[`ss_aipe_mean_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_mean_sensitivity.md)
echoes `supposed_sd`;
[`ss_aipe_crossed_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crossed_sensitivity.md)
echoes `supposed_var_unit`, `supposed_var_rater`, and
`supposed_var_residual`; and
[`ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity.md)
echoes `supposed_icc_X`.

#### Calls That Are Now Refused

- **[`var_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_r.md) no
  longer takes `kurtosis_x` and `kurtosis_y`.** DMAR 1.0.x returned a
  row `var_r_bonett_wright`, the normal-theory variance times 1 + rho^2
  (kurtosis_x + kurtosis_y) / 4, and credited it to Bonett and Wright
  (2000). That article has no such formula, no other source for it was
  found, and the help’s statement that it is exact for elliptical
  distributions was wrong: there the variance is the normal-theory
  variance times one factor that does not depend on the correlation. The
  large-sample variance under non-normality depends on every
  fourth-order cumulant of the joint distribution (Duncan & Layard,
  1973, Equation 1.1), which two marginal kurtoses do not supply. A call
  that gives either argument stops with “unused argument”.

- **`desired_power` must be strictly between 0 and 1 in every power
  planner.**
  [`ss_power_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2.md)
  accepted 0 and 1 (and returned a sample size for a power of 1);
  [`ss_power_pcm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_pcm.md)
  made no check. Every `ss_power_*` function now applies one rule and
  gives one refusal, of class `dmar_desired_power_invalid`, that carries
  the value given.

- **The unbiased standardized mean difference on one degree of freedom
  is refused.** `smd(unbiased = TRUE)` with `n_1 + n_2 = 3` and
  `smd_c(unbiased = TRUE)` with `n_C = 2` returned 0, because the
  correction factor of Hedges (1981) is 0 at one degree of freedom
  whatever the data. They now stop with a refusal of class
  `dmar_hedges_correction_undefined` that says why and what to do
  (`unbiased = FALSE`, or more observations). On no degrees of freedom
  ([`smd_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/smd_c.md) from
  summary statistics with `n_C = 1`, which returned `Inf`, or `NaN` when
  the means were equal;
  [`smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/smd.md) with one
  standard deviation and `n_1 + n_2 = 2`) the refusal has the same class
  and states its own reason: the correction factor is not defined there,
  because there is no standard deviation.

- **`desired_power` is checked when a sample size is given too.** A
  power planner that is given a sample size computes the power and does
  not use `desired_power`; a value outside (0, 1) given with it was
  accepted without a word
  (`ss_power_r(true_cor = .3, specified_N = 60, desired_power = 1)`
  returned a table) and is now refused with
  `dmar_desired_power_invalid`.

- **[`smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/smd.md) from
  summary statistics refuses a group of one that has its own standard
  deviation.** With `s_1` and `s_2`, `n_1 = 1` and `n_2 = 2` returned a
  number and two groups of one returned `NaN`, where raw data with a
  group of one were already refused. Each size must be at least 2; the
  refusal has class `dmar_argument_invalid`.

- **`conf_level`, `alpha_level`, `width`, and `assurance` are checked on
  entry, one way.** `conf_level` and `alpha_level` are each a single
  number strictly between 0 and 1; `width` is a single positive finite
  number; `assurance` is `NULL` or a single number strictly between 0
  and

  1.  A value that is not (a negative or zero width, a level of 0, 1, or
      -1, `NA`, a logical, a character string, a vector of two) reached
      the computation in many functions. Fifteen planners searched
      without end for a width of 0 or below
      (`ss_aipe_sm(true_sm = 10, width = -1)`,
      `ss_aipe_R2(true_R2 = .5, p = 5, width = -1)`); others returned a
      number for it
      ([`ss_aipe_rmsea()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea.md)
      20,000,
      [`ss_aipe_reliability()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reliability.md)
      `Inf`);
      [`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md)
      returned limits of `Inf` and `-Inf` for `conf_level = -1`; and
      [`ss_power_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_reg_coef.md)
      did not return for `alpha_level = 0`. Each is now refused at the
      first line of the function with a condition of class
      `dmar_argument_invalid` (`dmar_assurance_invalid` for `assurance`)
      that names the argument, carries the value given, and says what to
      give. The check is at the head of the 166 functions in which a
      degenerate value was found to run or to stop with R’s own message;
      a function with a narrower range of its own (a width below 2 for a
      correlation, a level below .5 for an equivalence test, an
      assurance above .5) applies it after. An argument with no default
      is checked when it is given.

- **A number that is missing, empty, or not a number is refused by
  name.** An argument that holds one number and was given as `NA`,
  `NaN`, a character string, a list, or a vector of length 0 stopped
  inside the computation with R’s message (“missing value where
  TRUE/FALSE needed”, “non-numeric argument to binary operator”,
  “argument is of length zero”), which names neither the argument nor
  the function. In 79 functions those arguments are now checked on
  entry: `ci_smd(smd = .5, n_1 = NA, n_2 = 10)` stops with “‘n_1’ must
  be a number that is not missing; NA was given”, class
  `dmar_argument_invalid`. No call that returned a result is affected.

- **The interval functions check `conf_level` before the tail areas are
  derived from it.**
  [`ci_pvaf()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_pvaf.md),
  [`ci_snr()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_snr.md),
  [`ci_srsnr()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_srsnr.md),
  [`ci_eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_eta_squared.md),
  [`ci_omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_omega_squared.md),
  and [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md)
  refused `conf_level = 1.2` with a message about `alpha_lower`, an
  argument the call did not give. The refusal now names `conf_level`.
  [`ss_aipe_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2.md),
  [`ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity.md),
  and
  [`plot_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_R2.md)
  gave an empty message for `conf_level = NULL`; they give the same
  refusal.

- **[`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md)
  refuses one tail area given without the other.**
  `ci_c(means = c(1, 0), s_anova = 1, c_weights = c(1, -1), n_per_group = c(20, 20), conf_level = NULL, alpha_upper = .025)`
  (`n` in 1.0.0) stopped in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of
  1.1.0 with R’s own message, “Non-numeric argument to mathematical
  function”, and with only `alpha_lower` given, “arguments imply
  differing number of rows: 3, 2”. It is now refused with class
  `dmar_argument_invalid`, `arg` `c("alpha_lower", "alpha_upper")`:
  “Only ‘alpha_upper’ was given. ‘alpha_lower’ and ‘alpha_upper’ go
  together: each is the tail area beyond one limit, so the interval
  needs both. Give both (for example alpha_lower = .025 and alpha_upper
  = .025, or 0 for a one-sided interval), or neither and a
  ‘conf_level’.”

- **[`ss_power_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c.md)
  and
  [`ss_power_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_sc.md)
