  refuse a contrast of 0 when a sample size is to be found.** A
  population contrast of 0 is the null hypothesis; the power is
  `alpha_level` at every sample size. The two functions searched a
  million sample sizes and stopped with “Failed to converge within
  reasonable sample size.” They now stop at once with a refusal of class
  `dmar_argument_invalid` that says so. With a sample size given they
  return the power at 0, as before. The nine power planners that had
  that message for a search that reaches its limit
  ([`ss_power_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c.md),
  [`ss_power_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_sc.md),
  [`ss_power_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c_ancova.md),
  [`ss_power_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_smd.md),
  [`ss_power_one_way_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_one_way_anova.md),
  [`ss_power_factorial_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_factorial_anova.md),
  [`ss_power_rm_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_rm_anova.md),
  [`ss_power_split_plot_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_split_plot_anova.md),
  [`ss_power_mixed_effects()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_mixed_effects.md))
  now say what it means (the effect at the planning values is too small
  for the power asked for at any size up to 1,000,000) and what to
  check; the class is `dmar_computation_failed`, as before.

- **[`ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity.md)
  refuses `supposed_R2` together with `specified_N`.** It ran the
  simulation at the sample size planned from the supposed value and
  ignored `specified_N` (a call with `specified_N = 6` reported
  `total_N` 34). The coefficient of variation, Cliff’s delta, and
  reliability siblings refused the pair already; all four refusals now
  have class `dmar_argument_invalid`.

- **[`ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity.md)
  asks for `width` when it plans.** With `supposed_std_contrast` and no
  `width` the call stopped inside the planner with “argument is of
  length zero”; it now stops with a refusal of class
  `dmar_argument_invalid` that names `width`.

- **[`ss_aipe_reliability()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reliability.md)
  checks its two counts of replications.** `G_initial` and `G`
  (`initial_iter` and `final_iter` in 1.0.x) each must be a single whole
  number of at least 1; a fractional number, 0, a negative number, `NA`,
  or more than one value reached the search unchecked and is now an
  error of class `dmar_count_invalid`, as for every other `G`.

- **[`ss_power_mixed_effects()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_mixed_effects.md)
  refuses a missing or inadmissible `cluster_size`, `true_icc`, or
  `specified_n_clusters_per_arm` by class.** Each refusal has class
  `dmar_argument_invalid`, carries the name of the argument, and says
  what the value must be and why. A cluster size or a number of clusters
  that is not finite was not refused in 1.0.x.

- **An element of `effects` with a field the composite planners do not
  read is refused.** Each element of `effects` in
  [`ss_power_composite_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_anova.md),
  [`ss_power_composite_factorial_anova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_factorial_anova.md),
  [`ss_power_composite_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_ancova.md),
  [`ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova.md),
  and
  [`ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova_het()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_factorial_ancova_het.md)
  is a list of `factors`, `true_f` or `true_eta_squared_partial`, and
  `label` (and `type` under heterogeneous slopes). A field under any
  other name, the `f` and `partial_eta_squared` of 1.0.x among them, or
  an element with no name, was not looked at: with the sizes read from
  `true_means` it was dropped without a word. It is now an error of
  class `dmar_argument_invalid` that names the effect and the field and
  gives the fields that are read.

- **[`ss_power_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c_ancova.md)
  refuses an `n_per_group` that is not a single finite number of at
  least 2 by class** (`dmar_argument_invalid`). A size below 2 was a
  plain error in 1.0.x, and a size that is not finite was not refused.

- **An argument a function does not have is an error in 20 more
  functions.** See the paragraph on `...` under Old Names That R Still
  Matches.

- **[`bifactor_indices()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bifactor_indices.md)
  refuses a fit with one group factor.** A general factor beside a
  single group factor is not a bifactor model with subscales: its
  indices divide the common variance between those two factors alone,
  every item belongs to the one subscale, and PUC is 0. DMAR 1.0.0
  refused only a fit with no group factor and described a fit with one
  when every item was listed under that factor (some of them with
  loadings fixed at zero). Such a fit now stops with a message that
  names the group factor and says what to fit instead, as it does in
  [`fa_bifactor()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_bifactor.md)
  and
  [`ci_bifactor_indices()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_bifactor_indices.md),
  which are new in this release.

- **The six `ss_aipe_crd_es_*()` planners refuse a width asked for
  without the effect size.** The width of the interval is read from data
  simulated at `true_es`. Without `true_es` the four planners that take
  or return a width stopped with a message that did not name the cause
  ([`ss_aipe_crd_es_n_individuals_fixed_width()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
  said that the width seemed impossible to reach with the number of
  clusters); they now stop at once with a refusal of class
  `dmar_argument_invalid` that says why the effect size is needed and
  what to give. In
  [`ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_crd_es_n_individuals_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
  the expected width is asked for by supplying `G`: with `G` and without
  `true_es` the call stopped with “arguments imply differing number of
  rows: 660, 0”, and with `G` and without `pr_treat` or `true_icc` it
  returned the table without the width and without a word. Both are now
  refused with the same class, in a message that names every population
  value that is missing and says that `G = NULL` returns the size the
  budget buys without a width. A `true_es` that is not a single finite
  number is refused the same way. With one covariate
  (`n_covariates = 1`) the same two functions had no default for
  `true_R2_within` and `true_R2_between`, where the four planners that
  take a width have 0, and did not use `true_icc` for a missing
  `true_icc_covariate` as the help says: a call with `G` and a covariate
  and without all three stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE
  needed” or “arguments imply differing number of rows”. The two
  proportions now default to 0 in all six functions, a missing
  `true_icc_covariate` is `true_icc`, and a value of any of the three
  that is not a single number in range is refused with class
  `dmar_argument_invalid`, by name.

- **The twelve cluster randomized planners (`ss_aipe_crd_*()` and
  `ss_aipe_crd_es_*()`) check their sizes, proportions, and allocation
  on entry.** `n_covariates` must be a whole number of 0 or more,
  `cluster_size` a whole number of at least 2 (the cluster size searches
  start at 2), `n_clusters` a whole number of at least
  `3 + n_covariates` (the interval has `n_clusters - 2 - n_covariates`
  degrees of freedom), `pr_treat` strictly between 0 and 1, and
  `true_R2_between` and `true_R2_within` in \[0, 1), as the two
  standardized budget planners already required of a covariate. Each
  refusal has class `dmar_argument_invalid` and names the argument as
  `arg`. DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of 1.1.0 planned with
  whatever they were given (the calls are written with the 1.1.0 names;
  1.0.0 gave the same results under its own):
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 1, cluster_size = 20, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8)`
  returned 17.5 clusters with `n_covariates = .5`, 5 with
  `true_R2_between = 1.1`, and 19 with `true_R2_within = -.5`.
  Fractional sizes were planned for and are now refused:
  `cluster_size = 20.5` gave 62 clusters at `width = .5`, and
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_width(width = .5, n_clusters = 60.5, ...)`
  a cluster size of 23; so is `cluster_size = 1`, which gave 249
  clusters. `n_clusters = 2` stopped with “missing value where
  TRUE/FALSE needed”
  ([`ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_width()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd.md))
  or returned an expected width of `NaN`
  ([`ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd.md)),
  and `pr_treat = 0` or `1` searched without end. A fixed number of
  clusters that leaves a condition without a cluster is refused,
  wherever a width is computed, with `reason` `"arm_without_clusters"`
  and the fewest clusters that would do (`fewest`):
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, n_clusters = 5, pr_treat = .1, ...)`
  returned a cluster size of 200 with an expected width of `Inf`, since
  round(5 \* .1) = 0 clusters are treated, and is refused with
  `fewest = 6`.
  [`ss_aipe_crd_es_n_individuals_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
  makes the check only when `G` asks for the width, since without `G` it
  does not use `pr_treat`: with
  `cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 1, G = 2, true_icc = .2, true_es = .5`
  the same design returned a cluster size of 200 with an expected width
  of `NaN` in DMAR 1.0.0 and stopped with class
  `dmar_computation_failed` after simulating it in the development
  versions, and without `G` it still returns 200.

- **Costs and budgets in the cluster randomized planners must be single
  finite numbers of 0 or more, and costs of 0 are refused where they
  decide the design.** Costs that are both 0 are refused (`reason`
  `"costs_all_zero"`) in the budget planners and the `both` planners,
  and `individual_cost = 0` (`reason` `"individual_cost_zero"`) where
  the costs choose the cluster size:
  [`ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd.md),
  [`ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd.md),
  [`ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd.md),
  and their `ss_aipe_crd_es_*()` counterparts. Each class is
  `dmar_argument_invalid`, and each message says what to give. A search
  over designs that all cost the same has no end. In DMAR 1.0.0 and the
  development versions of 1.1.0 all six budget planners searched without
  end with both costs 0 (none returned within 4 seconds), among them
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, cluster_size = 20, cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 0)`;
  so did, with `cluster_cost = 10` and `individual_cost = 0`,
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, n_clusters = 20, ...)`,
  [`ss_aipe_crd_es_n_individuals_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
  with the same arguments,
  `ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_budget(budget = 10000, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8, ...)`,
  and
  `ss_aipe_crd_es_both_fixed_budget(budget = 10000, true_es = .5, true_icc = .2, pr_treat = .5, G = 2, seed = 113, ...)`,
  which with a budget of 1000 stopped instead with “‘from’ must be a
  finite number”. With the same costs
  `ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width(width = .5, ...)` returned a table of
  `NA` with a character `value` column, and
  [`ss_aipe_crd_es_both_fixed_width()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
  stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”. Clusters of a
  fixed size cost only their clusters, so
  [`ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd.md)
  with `individual_cost = 0` and a positive `cluster_cost` still plans
  (100 clusters for a budget of 1000 at `cluster_cost = 10`). In the
  four planners that plan from a width and a fixed size the costs only
  price the plan, and costs of 0 still give a budget of 0. A negative
  cost, a vector of costs, and a negative budget were used, and are
  refused:
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = .5, cluster_size = 20, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8, cluster_cost = -1, individual_cost = 1)`
  reported a budget of 1178 (62 clusters at 19 each),
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, cluster_size = 20, individual_cost = c(1, 2))`
  stopped with “arguments imply differing number of rows”, and
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = -5, cluster_size = 20)`
  returned `NA`, in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions.

- **A budget that does not buy the smallest design a cluster randomized
  planner can return is refused with the cost of that design.** The
  refusal has class `dmar_argument_invalid`, `arg` `"budget"`, `reason`
  `"budget_infeasible"`, and `min_cost`, and the budget it names buys a
  design the planner returns:
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 1, cluster_size = 10, cluster_cost = 10, individual_cost = 1)`
  (4 clusters of 10 cost 80) and
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget(budget = 1, n_clusters = 10, cluster_cost = 10, individual_cost = 1)`
  (10 clusters of 2 cost

  120. returned a table whose size and budget were `NA` in DMAR 1.0.0
       and the development versions of 1.1.0, as did their
       `ss_aipe_crd_es_*()` counterparts;
       `ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_budget(budget = 1, cluster_cost = 10, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .5, ...)`
       and
       [`ss_aipe_crd_es_both_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
       with the same budget stopped with “invalid ‘type’ (list) of
       argument” (4 clusters of 2 cost 48). When the width is asked for
       (`pr_treat`, or `G` in the standardized planner), the smallest
       design
       [`ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd.md)
       can return has a cluster in each condition and a degree of
       freedom:
       `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 60, cluster_size = 20, cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .1, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8)`
       returned a table of `NA` in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development
       versions, and is refused with the cost of 6 clusters, 120 (with
       `n_covariates = 2` and `pr_treat = .5`, 5 clusters, 100);
       [`ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
       with the same budget and `G = 2, true_icc = .2, true_es = .5`
       stopped with “NA/NaN argument” in both.

- **A budget that buys clusters of a fixed size with no finite width is
  refused when `pr_treat` asks for the width.**
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 100, cluster_size = 20, cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .1, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8)`
  returned 5 clusters, none of them treated, with an `expected_width` of
  `Inf` in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of 1.1.0. It is
  refused (class `dmar_argument_invalid`, `reason`
  `"arm_without_clusters"`) with the budget, the design it buys, and the
  cheapest design that puts a cluster in each condition (6 clusters,
  cost 120); a design with no degrees of freedom (4 clusters with
  `n_covariates = 2`) is refused with `reason` `"too_few_clusters"`.
  [`ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
  makes the same check before it simulates a width.

- **The six unstandardized cluster randomized planners refuse a
  negative, missing, or contradictory variance before searching.** Any
  two of `true_var_between`, `true_var_within`, `true_total_var`, and
  `true_icc` determine the model. Each one given must be a single finite
  number (`reason` `"variance_input_invalid"`); a variance must be 0 or
  more, the total positive, whether it is given or is the sum of the two
  variances, and the intraclass correlation in \[0, 1\] (`reason`
  `"variance_out_of_range"`); fewer than two inputs, or a between
  variance of 0 with an intraclass correlation of 0, is refused with
  `reason` `"underidentified_variances"`; and a third or fourth input
  that disagrees with the two that determine the model by more than 64
  machine epsilons of its scale is refused with `reason`
  `"inconsistent_variances"`, with the value they imply in the message.
  With `diff_size` a within-cluster variance of 0 is refused (`reason`
  `"within_variance_zero"`), where the budget planners reported a width
  of `NaN` and the others stopped with an error from R. Each refusal has
  class `dmar_argument_invalid`, carries the four inputs as given in
  `supplied`, and says what to give. In DMAR 1.0.0 and the development
  versions of 1.1.0
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 1, cluster_size = 20, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = -.2, true_var_within = .8)`
  stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” after ten
  warnings, as did `true_total_var = 1, true_icc = NA` without the
  warnings; `true_var_between = 0, true_var_within = 0` returned 3
  clusters with an expected width of 0; and
  `true_total_var = 1, true_icc = .2, true_var_between = .5` planned 36
  clusters with a between variance of .5 and a within variance of .8,
  where the pair (total 1, ICC .2) gives 18; it is now refused with
  “true_total_var = 1 and true_icc = 0.2 imply true_var_between = 0.2,
  but 0.5 was given”. A rounded redundant value is refused the same way:
  `true_var_between = 1, true_var_within = 2, true_icc = .333`, which
  DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions planned from the two variances
  (71 clusters), says that the variances imply
  `true_icc = 0.333333333333333`; give two of the four.

- **`G` above 999,999 is refused by the six `ss_aipe_crd_es_*()`
  planners.** Each simulated data set takes its own seed, drawn without
  replacement from 1 to 999,999.
  `ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, cluster_size = 10, cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 1, G = 1000000, pr_treat = .5, true_icc = .2, true_es = .5)`
  stopped with “cannot take a sample larger than the population when
  ‘replace = FALSE’” in DMAR 1.0.0 (`nrep`) and the development versions
  of 1.1.0; it is refused on entry with class `dmar_count_invalid`,
  `max` 999999, and a message that says why. The draw of seeds is
  unchanged, so every `G` that was accepted gives the same seeds and the
  same result.

- **The cluster randomized planners check `assurance`, and the
  standardized ones `width`, `conf_level`, and the covariate’s
  intraclass correlation, on entry.**
  [`ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_width()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_crd_es_both_fixed_width()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
  check `width`, `conf_level`, and `assurance` as the other planners do:
  `ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = -1, cluster_size = 20, true_es = .5, true_icc = .2, pr_treat = .5, G = 2)`
  searched without end in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of
  1.1.0.
  [`ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd.md),
  [`ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_crd_es_n_individuals_fixed_budget()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
  refuse an `assurance` that is not `NULL` or a single number strictly
  between 0 and 1 (class `dmar_assurance_invalid`), whether or not a
  width is computed, as the other planners do. In DMAR 1.0.0 and the
  development versions
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, cluster_size = 20, cluster_cost = 10, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8, assurance = 1.5)`
  returned 33 clusters with an assured width of `NaN`, and without the
  population values and with `assurance = 2` 33 clusters and a budget of
  990; the two standardized planners with `G = 2` and `assurance = 2`
  stopped with “‘probs’ outside \[0,1\]”, and without `G` returned the
  size the budget buys (50 clusters of 10 at `cluster_cost = 10`). The
  four standardized planners that take a width or search over both sizes
  check `true_icc_covariate` (a single number in \[0, 1\]) on entry, as
  the two budget planners already did with `G`:
  `ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 1, cluster_size = 20, true_es = .5, true_icc = .2, pr_treat = .5, n_covariates = 1, true_icc_covariate = 1.5, true_R2_within = .1, true_R2_between = .1, G = 2, seed = 113)`
  stopped with “‘data’ must be of a vector type, was ‘NULL’” in DMAR
  1.0.0 and, after simulating three designs, with class
  `dmar_computation_failed` (`reason` `"no_finite_width"`) in the
  development versions; it is refused with class `dmar_argument_invalid`
  and `arg` `"true_icc_covariate"`.

- **The cluster randomized planners refuse a `diff_size`, `true_icc`, or
  `es_type` that makes the width not a number, and a target that no
  design of up to 1,000,000 clusters meets.** `diff_size` must be `NULL`
  or a vector of one or more finite numbers, in all twelve planners.
  Wherever a width is simulated, the six `ss_aipe_crd_es_*()` planners
  check `es_type` (0, 1, or 2) and `true_icc`, a single number in \[0,
  1), and above 0 with `es_type = 2`: at 1 no variance lies within
  clusters and the model fitted to each simulated data set has none to
  estimate, and with `es_type = 2` an intraclass correlation of 0 leaves
  the effect without a scale. Each refusal has class
  `dmar_argument_invalid`. In DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of
  1.1.0
  `ss_aipe_crd_es_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 1, cluster_size = 20, true_es = .5, true_icc = 1, pr_treat = .5, G = 2, seed = 113)`
  stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”, as it did with
  `true_icc = 1.5`, `true_icc = -.2`, and `true_icc = 0, es_type = 2`;
  with `true_icc = 1, es_type = 0` it stopped with that message in
  1.0.0, and the development versions simulated three designs at which
  every fit failed and stopped with class `dmar_computation_failed`.
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 1, cluster_size = 20, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8)`
  stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” with
  `diff_size = numeric(0)`, `c(Inf, 0)`, or `NA`, and with “non-numeric
  argument to mathematical function” with `diff_size = "a"`. The
  searches over the number of clusters consider at most 1,000,000
  clusters, the bound the power planners use for a sample size, and a
  target that no design within it meets is refused with `arg` `"width"`,
  `reason` `"n_clusters_beyond_reach"`, and the width at the bound as
  `width_at_max`: in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions the same
  call searched without end with `width = 1e-300` and returned 1,639,025
  clusters with `width = .003`, and
  `ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width(width = .003, cluster_cost = 10, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8)`
  returned 1,391,996 clusters of 209. A target met within the bound is
  planned as before (`width = .004`: 921,953 clusters). The standardized
  planners start from this search and refuse such a target before
  anything is simulated. A width that is not a number at a design a
  search compares stops it with class `dmar_computation_failed` and
  `reason` `"width_not_a_number"`; the checks on entry leave no call
  that reaches it.

- **The twelve cluster randomized planners refuse a nonzero
  `true_R2_between` with `n_covariates = 0`.** `true_R2_between` is the
  share of the between-cluster variance of the outcome that the
  cluster-level covariates explain, and `n_covariates = 0` says there
  are none. Such a call is refused on entry, before any search or
  simulation, in all twelve planners, including the budget planners that
  compute no width. The refusal has class `dmar_argument_invalid`, `arg`
  `"true_R2_between"`, and `reason` `"R2_between_without_covariates"`,
  and its message asks for `n_covariates` or `true_R2_between = 0`.
  `true_R2_within` may still be nonzero without a cluster-level
  covariate. The plans these calls returned are under Changes to Earlier
  Results.

- **Summary statistics given with a fitted model are refused.** Through
  1.0.x `eta_squared(fit, F_value = 3)` and
  `ci_eta_squared(fit, N = 50)` ignored the summary statistics;
  [`eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/eta_squared.md),
  [`omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/omega_squared.md),
  [`ci_eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_eta_squared.md),
  and
  [`ci_omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_omega_squared.md)
  now stop and say that a fitted model and summary statistics were both
  given. An infinite `F_value` is refused on entry by all four;
  [`ci_eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_eta_squared.md)
  and
  [`ci_omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_omega_squared.md)
  let it reach the noncentral root search, which failed.

- **[`ci_mahalanobis()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_mahalanobis.md)
  refuses a name in `...` that its root search does not take.** `tol`,
  `maxiter`, `check.conv`, and `trace` are passed to the search of
  [`ci_nc_F()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_nc_F.md);
  any other name, and an argument with no name, is refused before
  anything is computed, with a condition of class
  `dmar_argument_invalid` whose `arg` names it. DMAR 1.0.x passed every
  name on, so most stopped inside the search with a message about the
  search, and [`uniroot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/uniroot.html)’s
  `lower`, `upper`, `f.lower`, and `f.upper` replaced the bracket the
  search had set.

- **[`ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity.md)
  refuse `noncentral = TRUE` when the sample size is planned from the
  supposed values and the supposed variances of *Y* and of the targeted
  predictor are not both 1**, with a condition of class
  `dmar_argument_invalid` whose message names
  [`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.md):
  the noncentral plan of
  [`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md)
  is for a standardized coefficient, and these two report the
  unstandardized one. With unit variances, or with `specified_N`, the
  call runs.

- **[`bifactor_indices()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bifactor_indices.md)
  refuses a multiple-group fit,** with the error
  [`average_variance_extracted()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/average_variance_extracted.md)
  gives such a fit (class `dmar_argument_invalid`, the groups carried as
  `groups`): the factors have indices in each group, those of the model
  fitted to that group’s data alone.
  [`ci_bifactor_indices()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_bifactor_indices.md)
  already refused such a fit.

- **[`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  refuses a plan that cannot exist.** With `alpha_upper = 0` the
  interval is a lower confidence bound whose upper limit is infinite at
  every sample size; in DMAR 1.0.0 the search ran its cap of 100,000
  steps (about a minute) before stopping with the error “The sample size
  search did not converge within 100000 iterations”. Such a call is now
  refused at once with a condition of class `dmar_argument_invalid`
  naming `alpha_upper`. With `alpha_lower = 0`, an upper confidence
  bound, DMAR 1.0.0 returned no plan for any width:
  [`ci_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_cv.md) gave
  that interval a lower limit of `-Inf`, so its width was infinite at
  every sample size and the search stopped at the same cap. The lower
  limit is now 0, and the width is the upper bound itself. With
  `alpha_upper` below .5 the bound stays above `true_cv` at every sample
  size the search can reach, so a `width` at or below `true_cv` is
  refused the same way, naming `width` and `alpha_lower`. A wider target
  is planned without `assurance` (`true_cv = .2`, `width = .25`,
  `conf_level = NULL`, `alpha_lower = 0`, and `alpha_upper = .05`
  give 37) and is refused with it (see the entry below on `assurance`
  together with `alpha_lower = 0`).

- **[`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity.md)
  take the contrast weights
  [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md)
  takes:** weights that sum to zero and whose positive values sum to 1,
  with
  [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md)’s
  messages and class `dmar_argument_invalid`.
  `ss_aipe_sc(true_std_contrast = .5, c_weights = c(.25, .25, -.5), width = .4)`
  returned 41 for a contrast
  [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md)
  refuses to estimate. Integer weights such as `-1:1` are accepted, as
  before.

- **[`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md)
  refuses unequal `alpha_lower` and `alpha_upper`** (class
  `dmar_argument_invalid`, naming both). It plans for the interval of
  [`ci_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc_ancova.md),
  which has equal tails only, and with unequal tails planned for an
  interval no DMAR function reports (`alpha_lower = .01` and
  `alpha_upper = .04` returned 215 at `true_std_contrast = .5`,
  `c_weights = c(1, -1)`, and `width = .4`).

- **`ss_aipe_sc_ancova(divisor = "s_anova")` refuses a ratio of the
  ANCOVA to the ANOVA error standard deviation outside (0, 1\]**, which
  no population has (class `dmar_argument_invalid`): `true_cor = 1`
  stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”, and
  `true_sd_anova = 1` with `true_sd_ancova = 2` returned 508 at
  `true_contrast = 1` and `width = .5`.

- **Every function that takes contrast weights refuses weights that are
  all zero** (class `dmar_argument_invalid`; `arg` is `"c_weights"`, or
  the name the function gives the weights: `"contrast"` in
  [`contrast_adjusted()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_adjusted.md),
  `"weights"` in
  [`meta_contrast()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/meta_contrast.md),
  and `"contrasts"` in
  [`ci_scheffe()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_scheffe.md),
  [`contrast_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_test.md),
  and
  [`is_orthogonal_set()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/is_orthogonal_set.md)).
  Such weights pass the rules that the weights sum to zero and that the
  positive ones sum to at most 1, and they define no contrast. The
  message is “‘c_weights’ has no nonzero weight, so it defines no
  contrast; give weights such as c(1, -1) or c(1/2, 1/2, -1).”, with the
  function’s own name for the weights in place of ‘c_weights’
  (“‘contrast’ has no nonzero weight, …” in
  [`contrast_adjusted()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_adjusted.md)).
  Where the weights are a set of contrasts (the rows of a matrix
  `c_weights` in
  [`ci_c_ancova_bp()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova_bp.md),
  the rows of `contrasts` in
  [`contrast_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_test.md),
  the columns of `contrasts` in
  [`ci_scheffe()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_scheffe.md)
  and
  [`is_orthogonal_set()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/is_orthogonal_set.md)),
  a set with one such contrast is refused, and the message names it
  (“Row 2 of ‘c_weights’ has no nonzero weight”, “The contrast ‘none’ in
  ‘contrasts’ has no nonzero weight”). The functions are
  [`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md),
  [`ci_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova.md),
  [`ci_c_ancova_bp()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova_bp.md),
  [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md),
  [`ci_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc_ancova.md),
  [`ci_scheffe()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_scheffe.md),
  [`contrast_adjusted()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_adjusted.md),
  [`contrast_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_test.md),
  [`equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_c.md),
  [`is_orthogonal_set()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/is_orthogonal_set.md),
  [`meta_contrast()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/meta_contrast.md),
  [`power_equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/power_equivalence_c.md),
  [`ss_aipe_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c.md),
  [`ss_aipe_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_ancova.md),
  [`ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity.md),
  [`ss_aipe_c_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_sensitivity.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity.md),
  [`ss_power_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c.md),
  [`ss_power_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c_ancova.md),
  [`ss_power_contrast()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_contrast.md),
  [`ss_power_equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_equivalence_c.md),
  [`ss_power_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_sc.md),
  [`ss_seq_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_seq_c.md),
  and
  [`ss_seq_c_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_seq_c_sensitivity.md).
  With `c_weights = c(0, 0)` (or three zeros where the design has three
  groups), DMAR 1.0.0:

  - returned the interval \[0, 0\] from
    `ci_c(means = c(1, 2), s_anova = 1, c_weights = c(0, 0), n_per_group = c(20, 20))`,
    from
    [`ci_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova.md)
    with either procedure, from
    [`ci_c_ancova_bp()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova_bp.md),
    and from
    [`contrast_adjusted()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_adjusted.md),
    [`ci_scheffe()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_scheffe.md),
    and
    [`contrast_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_test.md),
    and \[.5, .5\] from
    `ci_c(contrast = .5, s_anova = 1, c_weights = c(0, 0), n_per_group = c(20, 20))`
    and from
    [`ci_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova.md)
    with `contrast = .5`;
    [`ci_scheffe()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_scheffe.md)
    and
    [`contrast_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_test.md)
    reported a standard error of 0 beside the interval, and
    [`contrast_adjusted()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_adjusted.md),
    [`ci_scheffe()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_scheffe.md),
    and
    [`contrast_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_test.md)
    a test statistic and *p*-value of `NaN`;
  - returned a plan of 2 per group from
    `ss_aipe_c(true_var_error = 1, c_weights = c(0, 0), width = .5)`,
    with or without `assurance = .9`, and from
    [`ss_aipe_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_ancova.md),
    and a summary of zeros (every simulated contrast and width 0,
    `pct_ci_less_width` 1) from
    [`ss_aipe_c_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_sensitivity.md)
    and
    [`ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity.md);
  - returned 2 per group, a power of 1, and a noncentrality parameter of
    `Inf` from
    `ss_power_c(true_contrast = .5, c_weights = c(0, 0), true_sd = 1)`,
    [`ss_power_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c_ancova.md),
    and
    [`ss_power_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_sc.md),
    and a power of 1 with `specified_n_per_group = 10`;
  - reported `all_orthogonal` 1 from
    `is_orthogonal_set(cbind(c(1, -1, 0), c(0, 0, 0)))`;
  - stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” in
    [`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md),
    [`ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity.md),
    [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md),
    [`ci_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc_ancova.md),
    and
    [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity.md)
    with `supposed_std_contrast`, and with “object ‘k’ not found” in
    [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity.md)
    with `specified_n_per_group`;
  - stopped with an unclassed message about the positive weights in
    [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md)
    (“Please use fractions to specify the contrast weights”),
    [`ss_power_contrast()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_contrast.md),
    [`equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_c.md),
    [`power_equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/power_equivalence_c.md),
    [`ss_power_equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_equivalence_c.md),
    [`ss_seq_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_seq_c.md),
    and
    [`ss_seq_c_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_seq_c_sensitivity.md),
    and with “All contrast weights are zero after centering.” in
    [`meta_contrast()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/meta_contrast.md).

  Empty weights, `c_weights = numeric(0)`, have no nonzero weight
  either, and they get the same refusal wherever no earlier check of
  their length refuses them. DMAR 1.0.0 returned the limits `NaN` around
  the contrast .5 from
  `ci_c(contrast = .5, s_anova = 1, c_weights = numeric(0), n_per_group = 20)`
  and from
  `ci_c_ancova(contrast = .5, s_ancova = .8, c_weights = numeric(0), n_per_group = 20, cov_means = numeric(0), SSwithin_x = 40)`,
  the limits `NaN` around a contrast of 0 with `means = numeric(0)` or
  `adj_means = numeric(0)` in place of `contrast`, and \[.5, .5\] from
  [`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md) with
  `N = 40` added. It stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE
  needed” in
  `ss_aipe_c(true_var_error = 1, c_weights = numeric(0), width = .5)`,
  [`ss_aipe_c_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_ancova.md),
  [`ss_aipe_c_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_sensitivity.md),
  [`ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_ancova_sensitivity.md)
  (with empty `true_mean_Y`),
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova_sensitivity.md),
  and a matrix that holds no contrast stopped with a message from R
  (“arguments imply differing number of rows: 1, 0” from
  `ci_c_ancova_bp(adj_means = c(1, 2), s_ancova = .8, c_weights = matrix(numeric(0), 0, 2), n_per_group = 20)`,
  and “length of ‘dimnames’ \[2\] not equal to array extent” from
  [`ci_scheffe()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_scheffe.md)
  with `contrasts = matrix(numeric(0), 3, 0)`), as did a set that holds
  no contrast in
  [`contrast_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_test.md)
  (“length of ‘dimnames’ \[1\] not equal to array extent” with
  `contrasts = matrix(numeric(0), 0, 3)`, and “argument must be
  coercible to non-negative integer” with `contrasts = list()`). In the
  other functions DMAR 1.0.0 stopped on empty weights with a message
  about the length or form of the weights, the number of groups or
  contrasts, the positive weights, or the degrees of freedom; where a
  check of the length comes first (as in
  [`ss_power_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_c.md),
  whose weights must have length 2 or more), DMAR 1.1.0 refuses them
  with that check’s message.

  Logical weights that are all `FALSE`, which are zeros when R computes
  with them, are refused too: with the message above, or, in the
  functions that require numeric weights, with that rule’s message.
  Those functions refused them with the same message in DMAR 1.0.0,
  without a class, except
  [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity.md),
  which require numeric weights from this release on: there DMAR 1.0.0
  stopped with “Please use fractions to specify the contrast weights”
  ([`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md)) and
  “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” (the two planners). DMAR 1.0.0
  returned \[0, 0\] from
  `ci_c(means = c(1, 2), s_anova = 1, c_weights = c(FALSE, FALSE), n_per_group = 20)`
  and a plan of 2 per group from
  `ss_aipe_c(true_var_error = 1, c_weights = c(FALSE, FALSE), width = .5)`.

  Weights in which every contrast has a nonzero value are accepted or
  refused as before, and the results for them are unchanged.

- **[`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md)
  refuse a `width` that needs more than 2^53 per group** (about 9.0e15,
  the largest number up to which R holds every whole number exactly;
  class `dmar_argument_invalid`, naming `width`). Past it neighboring
  sample sizes can be the same number in R, so no size there is the
  smallest that reaches `width`. DMAR 1.0.0 returned such numbers at a
  standardized contrast of 0:
  `ss_aipe_sc(true_std_contrast = 0, c_weights = c(1, -1), width = 5e-8)`
  (`psi_standardized` in 1.0.x) gave 12,292,668,226,221,188, and
  `width = 1e-9` gave 30,731,670,565,552,979,968. Those calls are now
  refused, both when the start of the search is past 2^53 and when the
  search passes it (as at `true_std_contrast = .1` with a start of
  9,006,298,534,815,513 per group). Below the limit the plans are
  returned at every contrast:
  `ss_aipe_sc(true_std_contrast = 2, c_weights = c(1, -1), width = 1e-6)`
  gives 46,097,505,846,480, and `true_std_contrast = .1` with
  `width = 5.9e-8` gives 8,839,438,422,537,546; DMAR 1.0.0 raised the
  sample size by one from a start about a third below the first and did
  not return either within 60 seconds. Past about 1e11 per group the
  plans rest on the precision of doubles (Details of
  [`?ss_aipe_sc`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md)
  and
  [`?ss_aipe_sc_ancova`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md)
  give the sizes). The smallest sample sizes here are for `width` and
  the tail areas as R holds them; with the default `conf_level = .95`
  each tail area, (1 - .95) / 2, is 0.025000000000000022 in doubles. At
  a contrast of 0, where the width is computed from the normal
  quantiles, `width = 6e-7` gives 85,365,751,570,981, the smallest
  sample size that reaches it, where DMAR 1.0.0 gave 85,365,751,570,976;
  `width = 1e-6` gives 30,731,670,565,553, also the smallest, where DMAR
  1.0.0 gave 30,731,670,565,548; and `width = 1e-7` gives
  3,073,167,056,555,298, 2 below the smallest, where DMAR 1.0.0 gave
  3,073,167,056,555,294. At other contrasts the width is the difference
  of two limits near the noncentrality: the plan above at a contrast of
  2 and `width = 1e-6` is 1,850 below the smallest, 46,097,505,848,330
  (see Bug Fixes for the search, and Changes to Earlier Results for the
  noncentral *t* distribution at many degrees of freedom).

- **[`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md),
  [`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md)
  refuse a tail probability of 0 or above .5, and two tails of .5,**
  with a condition of class `dmar_argument_invalid` naming `alpha_lower`
  and `alpha_upper`. With a tail of 0 the interval has a limit at
  infinity and is never as narrow as `width`, and
  [`ci_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_reg_coef.md),
  which reports the interval, takes no tail above .5. DMAR 1.0.x planned
  such a call as if both tails were their average: for two predictors
  correlated .3, correlated .4 and .3 with *Y*, and a width of .3,
  `alpha_lower = 0` with `alpha_upper = .05` gave 157, the plan for
  tails of .025, and the noncentral search (`noncentral = TRUE`, the
  default of
  [`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md))
  did not end; `alpha_lower = .6` with `alpha_upper = .01` gave 14; and
  two tails of .5 gave 5 (2*p* + 1), or 3 with `assurance = .9`, which
  leaves no residual degrees of freedom.

- **A nonzero tail area below 1e-9 is refused by
  [`ci_nc_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_nc_t.md)
  and by the intervals and plans of a regression coefficient, a
  contrast, and a correlation.**
  [`ci_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_reg_coef.md),
  [`ci_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_rc.md),
  [`ci_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_src.md),
  [`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md),
  [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md),
  [`ci_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc_ancova.md),
  [`ci_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_correlation.md),
  [`ci_sm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sm.md),
  [`ci_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_cv.md),
  [`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md),
  [`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md),
  [`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md),
  [`ss_aipe_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md),
  [`ss_aipe_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_r.md),
  [`ss_aipe_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_r_sensitivity.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  check the floor once their tails are resolved, and
  [`ci_nc_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_nc_t.md)
  checks it for every interval and plan whose limits come from it, among
  them
  [`ci_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_smd.md),
  [`ci_smd_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_smd_c.md),
  [`smd_trimmed()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/smd_trimmed.md),
  [`ss_aipe_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_smd.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sm.md),
  and the sensitivity functions of these planners. Functions that form
  one of these intervals at their own `conf_level` refuse the same
  levels:
  [`cles()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cles.md),
  [`proportion_of_superiority()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/proportion_of_superiority.md),
  [`nnt_from_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/nnt_from_smd.md),
  and
  [`plot_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_smd.md)
  through
  [`ci_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_smd.md),
  [`ss_aipe_c_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c_sensitivity.md)
  through
  [`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md), and
  [`ss_aipe_equivalence_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_equivalence_r_sensitivity.md)
  through
  [`ci_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_correlation.md).
  A tail of 0, a one-sided interval, is accepted wherever it was. Below
  1e-9 the noncentral *t* limits lose accuracy: the tail probability a
  limit is found from carries an absolute error of up to about 1e-12, a
  growing share of a smaller tail. The central intervals of a contrast,
  a correlation, and a regression coefficient and the plans for them
  keep the same floor, so that an interval and the plan for it accept
  the same tail areas. DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of 1.1.0
  returned what they computed.
  `ci_reg_coef(reg_coef_j = .5, se_reg_coef_j = .1, N = 50, p = 2, conf_level = NULL, alpha_lower = .025, alpha_upper = 1e-20, noncentral = TRUE)`
  (`b_j` and `SE_b_j` in 1.0.0) gave an upper limit of 1.549 in 1.0.0
  and 1.435 in the development versions, where the limit is 1.554. With
  `noncentral = FALSE` the upper limit was `Inf`, as it was for
  `ci_c(means = c(1, 0), s_anova = 1, c_weights = c(1, -1), n_per_group = c(20, 20), conf_level = NULL, alpha_lower = .025, alpha_upper = 1e-20)`
  (`n` in 1.0.0).
  `ci_r(r = .3, N = 50, conf_level = NULL, alpha_lower = .025, alpha_upper = 1e-20)`
  (`n` in 1.0.0) gave an upper limit of 1, and -1 for the lower limit
  with the tails exchanged.
  [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md) with
  the means and tails of that
  [`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md) call
  gave an upper limit of 4.126 in 1.0.0 and 3.782 in the development
  versions.
  `ss_aipe_reg_coef(true_R2_Y_X = .1, true_R2_j_X_without_j = .2, p = 2, true_reg_coef_j = .1, width = .4, conf_level = NULL, alpha_lower = 1e-20, alpha_upper = .05)`
  (`rho2_Y_X`, `rho2_j_X_without_j`, and `b_j` in 1.0.0) returned 114 in
  1.0.0, the plan for two tails of .025, and stopped in the development
  versions with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”.
  `ss_aipe_sc(true_std_contrast = .5, c_weights = c(1, -1), width = .5, conf_level = NULL, alpha_lower = 1e-20, alpha_upper = .025)`,
  and
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md)
  with the same contrast and width and both tails 1e-20
  (`psi_standardized` in 1.0.0 for both), stopped with the same message
  in 1.0.0 and refused ‘width’ (“needs more than 2^53 per group”) in the
  development versions. A level is held to the floor through its tails,
  (1 - conf_level) / 2 each, so `conf_level = 1 - 1e-12` is refused by
  every function above, and .999999998 is the largest level accepted. At
  `conf_level = 1 - 1e-12`,
  [`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md)
  with the planning values above returned 1,459 in 1.0.0 and the
  development versions,
  `ss_aipe_c(true_var_error = 1, c_weights = c(1, -1), width = .5)`
  (`error_variance` in 1.0.0) returned 1,640,
  `ss_aipe_r(true_cor = .3, width = .2)` (`rho` in 1.0.0) returned
  4,189, and `ci_smd(smd = .5, n_1 = 50, n_2 = 50)` returned \[-0.953,
  1.948\]. At .999999998 the floor leaves these plans as they were;
  [`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md)
  gives 1,032, where 1.0.0 gave 1,033, through the change in its plans
  without `assurance` (see Changes to Earlier Results). The refusal has
  class `dmar_argument_invalid`, `reason` `"tail_below_floor"`, `arg`
  naming the tail or tails below the floor (`conf_level` when the tails
  came from it), `value`, and `floor` (1e-9). Its message reads, for
  example, “‘alpha_upper’ is 1e-20, a tail area above 0 and below 1e-9,
  the smallest nonzero tail area accepted. Below 1e-9 the noncentral t
  limits lose accuracy (…), so a limit or a sample size could be off
  without notice. The central intervals of a contrast, a correlation,
  and a regression coefficient, and their plans, keep the same floor, so
  that an interval and the plan for it accept the same tail areas. Give
  a tail area of at least 1e-9, or 0 for a one-sided interval.” In
  [`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md),
  which refuse a tail of 0, and
  [`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md),
  which refuses one as `alpha_upper`, it ends “Give a tail area of at
  least 1e-9.” For a level the message reads “‘conf_level’ of
  0.999999999999 leaves a tail area of 5e-13 on each side, below 1e-9, …
  Give a conf_level of at most 0.999999998.” At the floor, the
  noncentral limits in six cases (*t* from -3 to 10, 10 to 1,000 degrees
  of freedom) at 66 tail areas from 1e-6 down to 1e-9 were within 1.4e-4
  of the exact ones (6.0e-6 of the width of the interval). “Small tail
  areas” in
  [`?ci_nc_t`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_nc_t.md)
  gives the numbers.

- **An assurance above .999999998 is refused by
  [`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sm.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_smd.md),
  and by their sensitivity functions when they plan with it.** The
  published assurance step with which DMAR 1.0.x planned them finds
  noncentral *t* limits with tail areas of (1 - assurance) / 2 and 1 -
  assurance (in
  [`ss_aipe_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_smd.md)
  through
  [`ci_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_smd.md)),
  which then fall below the floor of 1e-9 of the entry above.
  `ss_aipe_sc(true_std_contrast = .5, c_weights = c(1, -1), width = .5, assurance = 1 - 1e-10)`
  (`psi_standardized` in 1.0.0) returned 151 per group in DMAR 1.0.0 and
  the development versions of 1.1.0, as did
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md)
  at the same values and
  `ss_aipe_smd(true_smd = .5, width = .5, assurance = 1 - 1e-10)`
  (`delta` in 1.0.0), and
  `ss_aipe_sm(true_sm = .5, width = .5, assurance = 1 - 1e-10)` (`sm` in
  1.0.0) returned 116. Each came from limits below the floor. The
  refusal names `assurance`, not the tails of the step, which the caller
  did not give (class `dmar_argument_invalid`, `reason`
  `"tail_below_floor"`): “‘assurance’ of 0.9999999999 is too close to 1:
  the published assurance step, with which DMAR 1.0.x planned, finds
  noncentral t limits with tail areas of (1 - assurance) / 2 and 1 -
  assurance, and (1 - assurance) / 2 is below 1e-9, the smallest nonzero
  tail area accepted, below which those limits lose accuracy. Give an
  assurance of at most 0.999999998.” The check is made whatever
  `assurance_method` is, so whether a call is refused does not depend on
  it.

- **[`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md),
  [`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md)
  refuse an abbreviation of `"Lower"` or `"Upper"`, as they refuse those
  values.** They plan only for the full width, but DMAR 1.0.0 checked
  `which_width` with
  [`char.expand()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/char.expand.html) and then
  tested the value as given, so `"L"`, `"Lo"`, `"U"`, `"Up"`, and `""`
  were planned for the full width. In DMAR 1.0.0,
  `ss_aipe_reg_coef(true_R2_Y_X = .3, true_R2_j_X_without_j = .2, p = 5, true_reg_coef_j = .25, width = .15, which_width = "L")`
  (`rho2_Y_X`, `rho2_j_X_without_j`, and `b_j` in 1.0.x) and
  [`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md)
  with the same arguments returned 607, the plan of `"Full"`, and
  `ss_aipe_src(true_R2_Y_X = .3, true_R2_j_X_without_j = .2, p = 5, true_std_reg_coef_j = .25, width = .15, which_width = "L")`
  (`Rho2_j_X_without_j` and `beta_j` in 1.0.x) returned 626, also the
  plan of `"Full"`. These three calls now stop with a refusal of class
  `dmar_argument_invalid` (`arg = "which_width"`) whose message says
  that `"L"` stands for `"Lower"`. `"F"` and `"Fu"` still give the plan
  of `"Full"`: 606 from
  [`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md),
  625 from
  [`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md)
  (a case below 1.0.0; see Changes to Earlier Results).
  `ss_aipe_R2(true_R2 = .5, width = .15, which_width = "", p = 5, random_predictors = FALSE)`
  is refused the same way; DMAR 1.0.0 returned `NULL` for it
  (`population_R2` in 1.0.x).

- **[`mr_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_cv.md) and
  [`mr_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_smd.md)
  check every argument.** Each refusal names the argument and has class
  `dmar_argument_invalid`, or `dmar_count_invalid` for `m0` and
  `n_per_group`. In DMAR 1.0.x:

  - [`mr_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_cv.md)
    given scores with a negative mean returned the risk and the decision
    of the same scores with their signs reversed, beside a negative
    coefficient of variation; a data frame stopped with “is.atomic(x) is
    not TRUE”; and three observations returned a risk of `NaN` and a
    decision of `NA`. `data` must be a numeric vector of at least 4
    finite observations with a positive mean.
  - A `sampling_cost` of -75 gave a negative criterion and a stopping
    rule that was met, and a `sampling_cost` of 0, an `epsilon` of 0, or
    a `gamma` of -1 gave a pilot sample size of `Inf`. `sampling_cost`,
    `A`, `structural_cost`, and `epsilon` must each be a single positive
    finite number, and a call without `sampling_cost` is refused by
    name.
  - `gamma = .5` was accepted. `gamma` must be strictly between 0 and
    1/2, the interval on which the stopping rule is defined
    (Chattopadhyay & Kelley, 2016, Equation 23).
  - [`mr_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_cv.md)
    returned an `m0` of 4.5 or of 2 as the pilot sample size. `m0` must
    be a whole number of at least 4 in both functions.
  - `pilot = 1` and `pilot = 0` were read as `TRUE` and `FALSE`, and
    `pilot = "yes"` stopped with “object ‘Outcome’ not found”. `pilot`
    and `verbose` must be `TRUE` or `FALSE`.
  - [`mr_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_smd.md)
    given a sample size per group of -5 (`n` in 1.0.x) returned a
    negative risk and a decision of `NA`, accepted 74.5, and stopped
    with “arguments imply differing number of rows” for a vector there
    or in `d`. `d` must be a single finite number and `n_per_group` a
    whole number of at least 2.
  - `mr_cv(pilot = TRUE, A = 1e300, sampling_cost = 1e-10)` returned a
    pilot sample size of `Inf`. `A` divided by `sampling_cost` must be a
    finite number in both functions.

- **[`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  refuses `assurance` together with `alpha_lower = 0`,** a one-sided
  upper confidence bound, with a condition of class
  `dmar_argument_invalid` that names both arguments and advises planning
  without `assurance`. The assurance step of Kelley (2007) was written
  for a two-sided interval and does not give the requested probability
  for a bound; the numbers are on
  [`?ss_aipe_cv`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  under “Edge cases”. DMAR 1.0.0 returned no plan for a call with
  `alpha_lower = 0` (see the entry above on a plan that cannot exist).

- **[`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  refuses a planning value or a tail area that is not one admissible
  number, each by name** (class `dmar_argument_invalid`). With
  `conf_level = NULL`, a tail area that is left out, `NA`, or a vector
  stopped in DMAR 1.0.0 with an error of R’s own (“missing value where
  TRUE/FALSE needed” for a tail left out or `NA`); the refusal now says
  that each of `alpha_lower` and `alpha_upper` is a single number at
  least 0 and below 1. A vector `true_cv` (`C_of_V` in 1.0.x) stopped
  with “the condition has length \> 1”. `true_mean` and `true_sd` (`mu`
  and `sigma` in 1.0.x) must each be positive: DMAR 1.0.0 planned a
  negative mean with a negative standard deviation as their positive
  ratio.

- **[`ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity.md)
  checks every input that defines its simulation.** DMAR 1.0.0 refused a
  `true_cv` that was left out or not positive and an `estimated_cv` (now
  `supposed_cv`) that was not positive. It did not check that either was
  one finite number, and it did not check `mean` (now `true_mean`) or,
  when `specified_N` was given, `specified_N`, `width`, or `assurance`.
  `true_cv`, `supposed_cv`, and `true_mean` are now each a single finite
  positive number; `specified_N` is a whole number of at least 4, the
  smallest sample size
  [`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  plans (class `dmar_count_invalid`), so that a character string does
  not turn the `value` column into text and a fraction is not echoed as
  a sample size; `width`, when given, is a single finite positive
  number, also with `specified_N`; and `assurance` is checked on entry
  (class `dmar_assurance_invalid`), also with `specified_N`, where it is
  only echoed.

- **[`var_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_cv.md)
  refuses an `NA` or infinite `true_cv` or `N`.** In DMAR 1.0.x, where
  the arguments were `cv` and `n`, a numeric `NA` in either (`NA_real_`,
  as a computation returns it) stopped with R’s “missing value where
  TRUE/FALSE needed”, an infinite coefficient returned `Inf` in both
  rows, and an infinite sample size returned 0 and `NaN`. Each of these
  calls now stops with a refusal of class `dmar_argument_invalid` that
  names the argument and states the value given.

- **[`ss_aipe_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2.md)
  refuses `assurance` with a half-width.** With `which_width = "Lower"`
  or `"Upper"` the function plans for the distance from the expected
  sample value to one limit, and `assurance` given with either stops
  with a refusal of class `dmar_argument_invalid`
  (`arg = c("assurance", "which_width")`). In DMAR 1.0.0 every such call
  with `"Upper"` stopped with the R error “unused argument
  (random_predictors = random_predictors)”, and with `"Lower"` the
  function returned a sample size that did not deliver the probability
  asked for.
  `ss_aipe_R2(true_R2 = .30, width = .10, p = 3, which_width = "Lower", assurance = .99)`
  (`population_R2` in 1.0.x) returned 253, the plan without `assurance`,
  and at 253 the distance from the sample squared multiple correlation
  to its lower limit was no larger than .10 in 52 percent of 20,000
  simulated samples. With `true_R2 = .10` and `width = .05` it returned
  486 for an assurance of .80, again the plan without `assurance` (52
  percent), and 637 for .99 (95 percent); with `true_R2 = .70` and
  `width = .10` it returned 153 for .80 (72 percent).

- **[`ss_aipe_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity.md)
  refuse a call without `width`.** `ss_aipe_R2(true_R2 = .5, p = 5)`
  (`population_R2` in 1.0.x) stopped in DMAR 1.0.0 with R’s “missing
  value where TRUE/FALSE needed” and now stops with a refusal of class
  `dmar_argument_invalid` that names `width` (`arg = "width"`), as a
  call without `p` or `true_R2` is refused in the name of the argument
  left out.
  [`ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2_sensitivity.md)
  (where `width` was `w` in 1.0.x) stopped with the same error of R’s
  when `w` or `true_R2` was left out, and with “invalid ‘times’
  argument” when `p` was left out beside `specified_N`. Each of
  `true_R2`, `width`, and `p` left out is now refused in its name, with
  `supposed_R2` and with `specified_N`.

#### Conditions That Gained a Class

A condition with a class can be caught or muffled by name, whatever its
wording. **Every error and every warning DMAR signals on purpose now has
a class.** Every error is a `dmar_refusal` and carries a `code`, so
`tryCatch(expr, dmar_refusal = function(e) ...)` catches whatever DMAR
refused, and an error without that class came from R, from another
package, or from [`match.arg()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/match.arg.html).
The check of an argument (its type, length, or range, arguments that
cannot be given together, a column that is not in the data, a model the
function does not cover) is a `dmar_argument_invalid`, which carries the
names of the arguments at issue as `arg` (`NULL` where the refusal is
not about a named argument, and in some checks whose message names the
argument only in running text). Three more general classes cover the
errors that have no class of their own: `dmar_package_required` (a
package the analysis needs is not installed; field `package`),
`dmar_computation_failed` (the arguments were accepted and a search, a
fit, a refit, or a bootstrap made with them gave no result), and
`dmar_internal_error` (a state DMAR’s own code should not reach). Two
cover the warnings that have none: `dmar_result_qualified` (the result
is returned with something to know before using it) and
`dmar_argument_ignored` (an argument given has no effect on the call).
The more specific classes (`dmar_not_converged`, `dmar_no_maximum`,
`dmar_lavaan_error`, `dmar_inadmissible`, and the others the sections
below name) are `dmar_refusal`s as well; `dmar_bootstrap_cancelled` and
`dmar_progress_error`, which come from the caller’s `progress` function,
are not. In 1.0.0 nearly every error was a plain error and no error was
a `dmar_refusal`. Messages are worded as before, except that some of the
oldest checks now name the argument and state the rule (for example
“‘c_weights’ must sum to zero.” in place of “The sum of the coefficients
must be zero”). The help of
[`dmar_metadata()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/dmar_metadata.md)
lists the classes.

[`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
and
[`ss_aipe_sm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sm.md)
refuse an `assurance` that is not `NULL` or a single number strictly
between 0 and 1 with `dmar_assurance_invalid` (the condition carries the
value given; the message says why neither end is accepted).
`dmar_argument_invalid`, which carries the name or names at issue as
`arg`, is the class of the refusals of
[`ss_power_R2_change()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2_change.md)
for a `p_restricted` not below `p_full`, for squared multiple
correlations that cannot belong to nested models, and for an effect
stated in more than one way; of the partial and semipartial correlation
functions for a `p` below 2; and of
[`smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/smd.md) and
[`smd_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/smd_c.md) for
`unbiased = TRUE` without the sample sizes. One warning joins a class
its siblings already gave:
[`ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity.md)
reports replications without an interval with
`dmar_replications_without_interval` (fields `n_without_interval` and
`G`). The count of noncentral *F* lower-limit clamps that
[`ss_aipe_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2.md)
reports after its search has the new class `dmar_nc_F_clamp_search`,
with the field `n_evaluations`. The wording of each message is
unchanged, except that the refusals of
[`smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/smd.md) and
[`smd_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/smd_c.md) now
also say why the sizes are needed. The warnings about the accurate range
of the noncentral *t* distribution that
[`ci_nc_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_nc_t.md) and
the searches built on it gave in DMAR 1.0.x are gone, since every limit
is now computed exactly (see Exact Noncentral *t* and Studentized Range
Distributions).

- **A `which_width` that is not a single character string is refused
  with a class.** In DMAR 1.0.0,
  [`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md),
  [`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md),
  [`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2.md)
  with `which_width = 1` stopped with the error of base R “‘input’ and
  ‘target’ must be character vectors”, and with
  `which_width = c("Full", "Lower")` with “‘input’ must have length 1”.
  They now stop with `dmar_argument_invalid` (`arg = "which_width"`).

Where a check’s message opens with the name of the argument and the
check did not store it, `arg` is read from the message, so
`tryCatch(bayes_one_sample_t(mean = .5, sd = 1, N = 30, prior_location = NULL), dmar_refusal = function(e) e$arg)`
returns `"prior_location"` where it returned `NULL`.

### A Two-Level Planner and a Sensitivity Function That Describe One Design

- **[`ss_aipe_mixed_effects()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_mixed_effects.md)
  plans for a predictor at either level and for three ways of centering
  it, and
  [`ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_mixed_effects_sensitivity.md)
  simulates what it plans.** In DMAR 1.0.x the planner was for an
  individual-level (i.e., Level 1) predictor centered at its cluster
  mean, and the sensitivity function generated a cluster-level (i.e.,
  Level 2) predictor, whose slope has a far larger variance; its
  intervals were much wider than the plan and the comparison tested
  nothing. Both functions now take `predictor_level` (1, the default, or
  2), `centering` (`"cluster_mean"`, the default; `"grand_mean"`;
  `"none"`), and the intraclass correlation of an individual-level
  predictor (`true_icc_X`, with `supposed_icc_X` for the planning value
  in the sensitivity function), share one set of expressions, and form
  one interval, the estimate plus and minus a *t* quantile times its
  standard error, on K(m - 1) - 1 degrees of freedom for an
  individual-level predictor and K - 2 for a cluster-level one.
  - The planner’s default call returns the same number of clusters as
    before or more (19 against 18 for `true_total_var = 1`,
    `true_var_X = 1`, `true_icc = .10`, `width = .20`, and clusters of
    20; 88 against 70 with clusters of 5), because it uses the *t*
    quantile and the expected standard error of the interval computed
    from data, where 1.0.x used the normal quantile and the total sample
    size.
  - A cluster-level predictor centered at its cluster mean is refused
    (it is 0 for every individual), as is `true_icc_X` given for one.
  - Centering at the grand mean and not centering give the same slope
    and the same plan; both are accepted so that a call can say what the
    analysis does.
  - The sensitivity function computes the two cases with a closed form
    directly (the within-cluster regression, and the regression of
    cluster means) and fits the pooled case with lme4, which it asks for
    only then. It evaluates as few as 2 clusters for an individual-level
    predictor and 3 for a cluster-level one, where it refused fewer than
    5, and reports `expected_width`, `predictor_level`, `true_icc_X`,
    and `supposed_icc_X` rows.
  - In 4,000 simulated data sets for each of six designs the mean width
    was within 0.3 percent of the planned width in the four designs with
    an exact expression, and 0.5 and 1.3 percent narrower in the two
    with a pooled slope.

### Overview

A minor release, and a large one. DMAR 1.0.1 was prepared but never
submitted to CRAN; its changes are part of this release, and its section
below is kept as the record of them.

Factor analysis gets its own names and new models.
[`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
is the 1.0.0
[`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
and
[`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
its new exploratory partner, with
[`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
and
[`plot_cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_fa_confirmatory.md)
kept as aliases,
[`efa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
a new alias of
[`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md),
and the 1.0.0 result class kept after the new one;
[`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
fits incomplete items by FIML, gives rotation-aware intervals, and
rotates to a target;
[`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md)
and
[`parallel_analysis()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/parallel_analysis.md)
compare numbers of factors;
[`fa_bifactor()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_bifactor.md)
and
[`fa_second_order()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_second_order.md)
fit the bifactor and second-order models, with delta method intervals
for their indices;
[`factor_scores()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_scores.md)
gives per-case standard errors and the determinacy of each factor,
beside 2 rho^2 - 1, the lowest correlation two equally consistent sets
of scores can have; and
[`factor_congruence()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_congruence.md)
gives Tucker’s congruence between two solutions. Structural equation
models get measures of fit, precision, and comparison
([`sem_fit_measures()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_fit_measures.md),
[`sem_residual_fit()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_residual_fit.md),
[`sem_information_criteria()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_information_criteria.md),
[`sem_exact_fit_bootstrap()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_exact_fit_bootstrap.md),
[`equivalence_rmsea()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_rmsea.md),
[`compare_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/compare_sem.md))
and
[`sem_sam()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_sam.md),
which estimates the structural relations after the measurement models.

A missing data family states what the missing values cost: the fraction
of missing information for every parameter of a FIML fit, the patterns
and coverage behind it, the maximum likelihood covariance matrix of
incomplete data, and small-sample degrees of freedom with a t reference
distribution for Wald intervals, taught in a new vignette. Two-stage
maximum likelihood is a missing data option for the CFA family,
measurement invariance, and coefficients alpha and omega, and sample
size planning for a reliability coefficient can allow for the missing
values it will be estimated from. The omega of
[`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md),
[`reliability_omega_categorical()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega_categorical.md),
and
[`bifactor_indices()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bifactor_indices.md)
can take either the observed or the model implied variance as its
denominator and says which it used; categorical omega no longer needs
mvtnorm, no longer drops a correlation the data do not determine, and
takes incomplete items; coefficient H is computed from a fitted model;
the bifactor indices get bootstrap intervals; and the reliability
bootstrap counts the fate of every replication, runs on several
processes, refuses a solution that leaves no coefficient, and takes a
progress callback that can cancel it.

New intervals, tests, and plans: Dunnett’s T3
([`ci_dunnett_t3()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_dunnett_t3.md));
the difference between two proportions measured on the same units, with
tests of noninferiority and equivalence
([`ci_proportion_paired()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_proportion_paired.md),
[`equivalence_proportion_paired()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_proportion_paired.md));
Fieller’s confidence set for the ratio of two means
([`ci_ratio_of_means()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_ratio_of_means.md),
[`ci_ratio_of_means_paired()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_ratio_of_means_paired.md));
nonsuperiority in
[`equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_c.md);
the marker variable adjustment for common method variance with its
interval and test
([`common_method_adjusted_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/common_method_adjusted_r.md));
planning the interval for a single mean
([`ss_aipe_mean()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_mean.md))
and the assurance of a contrast’s interval when the errors are not
normal (`true_kurtosis` in
