[`ss_aipe_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_c.md));
a crossed design of units and raters
([`ci_crossed()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_crossed.md),
[`ss_aipe_crossed()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crossed.md));
and two-phase sampling, a costly measurement with an inexpensive proxy
([`ci_two_phase()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_two_phase.md),
[`ss_aipe_two_phase()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_two_phase.md),
[`ss_aipe_two_phase_cost()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_two_phase_cost.md),
[`ss_seq_two_phase()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_seq_two_phase.md)).
A new vignette fits classical tests as path models in lavaan, and a
knitted result table now carries every line the console prints under it.
A result table prints its numbers to three decimal places, where 1.0.x
printed three significant figures (see Changes to Earlier Results).
[`eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/eta_squared.md),
[`omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/omega_squared.md),
and their intervals report the total and the partial value of each
effect and take sums of squares from a published table;
[`ss_aipe_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_smd.md),
[`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md),
[`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md),
[`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md),
[`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md),
and
[`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md)
can find the sample size for `assurance` from the probability that the
interval is no wider than asked for, computed exactly or simulated from
the exact sampling distribution;
[`ss_power_indirect_effect()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_indirect_effect.md)
takes its power from the joint sampling distribution of the two path
tests, with the predictor measured or fixed by design; and the
noncentral *t* distribution and the studentized range are computed
exactly wherever R’s [`pt()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/TDist.html),
[`qt()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/TDist.html),
[`dt()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/TDist.html),
[`qtukey()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/Tukey.html), and
[`ptukey()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/Tukey.html) are not accurate.

Some defaults change results. DMAR 1.1.0 gives no warning when a result
or a default differs from 1.0.x; these notes describe every such change.
The changed defaults are described under Changes to Earlier Results,
each with the argument that restores the 1.0.x analysis where there is
one;
[`ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity.md)
also corrects how it forms its intervals, which no argument restores.
[`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
(with its alias
[`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
and with
[`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md) and
[`cfa_2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_2.md)) fits
raw data by full information maximum likelihood and takes the standard
errors that match the estimator (Huber-White under MLR, where 1.0.x took
the standard ones), and
[`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md),
[`reliability_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_alpha.md),
and
[`measurement_invariance()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_invariance.md)
fit incomplete data that way (as does
[`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md),
which takes `data` for the first time in this release);
[`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md)
forms the default interval of the model implied omega on the logit
scale; and
[`ci_rmsea()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_rmsea.md),
[`ss_aipe_rmsea()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea.md),
and
[`ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity.md)
form and plan a 90 percent RMSEA interval by default, where 1.0.x used
95 percent.
[`ss_aipe_semipartial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_semipartial_r.md)
without the new `true_R2_full` plans for the largest variance over every
full-model R2, which raises the sample size when `true_r_sp` squared is
above 1/2 (`true_R2_full = true_r_sp^2` restores the 1.0.x plan), and
[`ss_aipe_partial_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_partial_r_sensitivity.md)
and
[`ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_semipartial_r_sensitivity.md)
simulate one more variable partialed out than 1.0.x did for the same
model, which no argument restores.
[`ss_aipe_partial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_partial_r.md)
and
[`ss_aipe_semipartial_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_semipartial_r.md)
find the sample size for `assurance` from the sampling distribution of
the estimate, where 1.0.x multiplied by a chi square factor that does
not apply to these intervals, and
[`ss_aipe_partial_r_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_partial_r_sensitivity.md)
simulates the raw-scale interval it plans, where 1.0.x simulated
Fisher’s *Z* interval; no argument restores the first, and
`fisher_z = TRUE` gives the Fisher interval, planned and simulated, for
the second. Every function names the total sample size `N`, the number
of predictors `p`, a planner’s planning value `true_X`, a sensitivity
function’s planning value `supposed_X`, and the desired width `width`,
and names an argument for the quantity it holds (`true_cor`,
`true_contrast`, `true_reg_coef_j`, `true_cov_matrix`) rather than for a
symbol; the 1.0.x names are not accepted, `eta_squared_partial()`,
`omega_squared_partial()`, and `ci_eta_squared_partial()` are removed,
and the count of the partial and semipartial correlation functions is
the number of predictors, one more than the 1.0.x count of variables
partialed out (see Breaking Changes in 1.1.0).
[`vargha_delaney_A()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/vargha_delaney_A.md)
refers its test statistic to Student’s *t* with Satterthwaite degrees of
freedom, which gives a larger *p*-value than the standard normal
reference of 1.0.x (`test = "z"` restores it). With `assurance`,
[`ss_aipe_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_smd.md),
[`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md),
[`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md),
[`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md)
with its default `noncentral = FALSE`, and their sensitivity functions
return the smallest sample size, not below the plan without `assurance`,
at which the exact probability that the interval is no wider than
`width` reaches the request (the new argument `assurance_method`,
`"analytic"` by default), where DMAR 1.0.x returned published
approximations that could attain more or less than the request.
[`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md),
[`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md)
with `noncentral = TRUE`,
[`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md),
and their sensitivity functions return the published approximations by
default, and `assurance_method = "simulation"` returns the smallest
sample size at which a simulated estimate of that probability reaches
the request. The four regression and ANCOVA planners without `assurance`
return the smallest sample size that meets the width, where 1.0.x could
return a case or more above it (a few more per group in
[`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md)),
and the approximations, which start from that plan, move with it. No
argument restores the plans of
[`ss_aipe_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_r.md),
[`ss_aipe_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_smd.md),
and
[`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md)
with `assurance`, the central plans of
[`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md)
and
[`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md)
with `assurance` or with unequal tails, the plans without `assurance` of
[`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md),
[`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md),
[`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md),
and
[`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md),
which can be a case or more smaller, and the approximations that start
from them, the plans and true values of
[`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.md)
when the variances of *Y* and of the targeted predictor differ, the
plans of
[`ss_aipe_equivalence_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_equivalence_smd.md)
and its sensitivity function and of the standardized cluster randomized
planners, the power and plans of
[`ss_power_indirect_effect()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_indirect_effect.md),
the rows of
[`var_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_alpha.md),
or the simulated contrasts of
[`ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity.md),
each corrected in this release.
[`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
on complete data gives the same estimates as 1.0.x, but under ML its
standard errors come from the observed information, the item intercepts
join the table, and AIC and BIC count them; and its omega, average
variance extracted, and H rows get limits formed on the logit scale, as
[`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md)’s
already were, as described under Exploratory Models and Structural
Relations. Its RMSEA interval stays at the 90 percent of 1.0.0, now with
an argument of its own, `rmsea_conf_level`: every RMSEA interval in the
package, and the SRMR interval of
[`sem_residual_fit()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_residual_fit.md),
defaults to 90 percent, whose limits decide the tests of close and not
close fit at .05, while the other intervals keep 95 percent (see Every
RMSEA Interval at 90 Percent by Default).

### Every RMSEA Interval at 90 Percent by Default

- **RMSEA and SRMR intervals default to 90 percent, and every output
  states the level.** A 100(1 - 2 alpha) percent interval for the RMSEA
  decides the one-sided tests of close and not close fit at level alpha
  (MacCallum, Browne, & Sugawara, 1996, p. 136), and its lower limit is
  0 exactly when the test of exact fit does not reject at alpha, so the
  limits of a 90 percent interval decide those tests at .05, the level
  conventionally used with them and the default at which
  [`ss_power_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_sem.md)
  plans them;
  [`sem_fit_measures()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_fit_measures.md)
  reports the tests’ p-values beside the interval, and the 90 percent
  limits agree with those p-values compared with .05. A 95 percent
  interval decides them at .025. Every RMSEA interval in the package
  therefore defaults to 90 percent, as lavaan’s does, and so does the
  SRMR interval of
  [`sem_residual_fit()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_residual_fit.md),
  whose test of close fit pairs with its interval in the same way; the
  package’s other intervals keep 95 percent. Where a function reports
  both kinds, the RMSEA interval has an argument of its own. The
  functions and their arguments:

  - [`ci_rmsea()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_rmsea.md),
    [`ss_aipe_rmsea()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea.md),
    and
    [`ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity.md):
    `conf_level = 0.90`, where 1.0.x defaulted to 0.95.
    `conf_level = 0.95` restores the 1.0.x result of
    [`ci_rmsea()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_rmsea.md)
    and
    [`ss_aipe_rmsea()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea.md),
    and the 1.0.x level of
    [`ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity.md),
    whose intervals were also corrected, with no argument to restore
    them (see Changes to Earlier Results).
  - [`sem_fit_measures()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_fit_measures.md):
    `conf_level = 0.90`, which also sets the gamma hat and adjusted
    gamma hat intervals, mapped from the same noncentrality limits.
  - [`sem_residual_fit()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_residual_fit.md):
    `conf_level = 0.90` for the interval of the unbiased SRMR, lavaan’s
    default too.
  - [`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md):
    `conf_level = 0.90`, the level of its RMSEA intervals and of nothing
    else; the Monte Carlo limits of the parallel analysis reference in
    its `parallel_analysis` attribute keep the 95 percent of
    [`parallel_analysis()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/parallel_analysis.md).
  - [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
    (and
    [`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)),
    [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md),
    [`cfa_2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_2.md),
    [`fa_bifactor()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_bifactor.md),
    and
    [`fa_second_order()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_second_order.md):
    the new `rmsea_conf_level = 0.90` sets the RMSEA interval of the fit
    rows, which the `rmsea_ci_level` row and the `glance()` column of
    that name record, while `conf_level = 0.95` sets the intervals of
    the parameters and indices and no longer reaches the RMSEA interval.
    [`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
    [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md),
    and [`cfa_2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_2.md)
    thereby report the RMSEA interval of DMAR 1.0.0, which took lavaan’s
    90 percent whatever `conf_level` was; a development version of 1.1.0
    made it follow `conf_level`, and that change is withdrawn. In
    [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
    (and so
    [`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)),
    [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md),
    and
    [`cfa_2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_2.md),
    whose arguments DMAR 1.0.0 fixed in order, `rmsea_conf_level` comes
    after `...`, beside `wald_df`, so a 1.0.0 call that gives its
    arguments by position works as before and the new argument is given
    by name.
  - [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
    (and
    [`efa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)):
    the new `rmsea_conf_level = 0.90` sets the RMSEA interval of the fit
    line and of the `fit_measures` attribute, while `conf_level` sets
    the intervals of the solution.
    [`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md)
    passes its `conf_level` to it.
  - [`irt_grm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/irt_grm.md):
    the new `rmsea_conf_level = 0.90`, passed to lavaan, sets the RMSEA
    interval of the `fit_measures` attribute, which held lavaan’s 90
    percent interval before with no way to choose it, and is recorded as
    the `rmsea_conf_level` attribute.
  - [`equivalence_rmsea()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_rmsea.md)
    keeps `alpha_level`, whose 1 - 2 alpha interval is 90 percent at its
    default of .05.

  For 95 percent intervals pass `conf_level = 0.95` to
  [`ci_rmsea()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_rmsea.md),
  [`ss_aipe_rmsea()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea.md),
  [`ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity.md),
  [`sem_fit_measures()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_fit_measures.md),
  [`sem_residual_fit()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_residual_fit.md),
  and
  [`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md),
  and `rmsea_conf_level = 0.95` to the factor analysis functions and
  [`irt_grm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/irt_grm.md).
  The level is stated wherever such an interval is shown: the line
  beneath a printed table (“Confidence level: 90%”, and for the factor
  analysis tables, whose parameter intervals are at another level,
  “Confidence level: 95% (90% for the RMSEA interval)”), the fit line of
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  (“RMSEA with 90% interval”), the line beneath
  [`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md)’s
  table,
  [`results_sentence()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/dmar_output_helpers.md),
  the `conf_level` column `tidy()` puts on the RMSEA rows of
  [`sem_fit_measures()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_fit_measures.md)
  and beside the RMSEA columns of
  [`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md),
  and a new `rmsea_conf_level` field of
  [`dmar_metadata()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/dmar_metadata.md),
  which holds the level of a table’s RMSEA interval beside `conf_level`.

- The help of `rmsea_conf_level` in
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
  [`fa_bifactor()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_bifactor.md),
  and
  [`fa_second_order()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_second_order.md)
  (and so in
  [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md) and
  [`cfa_2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_2.md),
  which inherit it) now says where the argument reaches: the table DMAR
  returns and its `glance()`. `output = "summary"` returns the lavaan
  summary, which shows lavaan’s 90 percent interval whatever the
  argument is.

### Exploratory Models and Structural Relations

- [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  and
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
  name the exploratory and the confirmatory factor analysis.
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
  is the function DMAR 1.0.0 released as
  [`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md);
  [`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
  remains as an alias, as
  [`plot_cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_fa_confirmatory.md)
  does for
  [`plot_fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_fa_confirmatory.md),
  and its results keep the 1.0.0 class `dmar_cfa_k` after
  `dmar_fa_confirmatory`, so code written for 1.0.0 still runs, though
  on incomplete items its default analysis has changed (FIML in place of
  listwise deletion; see Changes to Earlier Results).
  [`efa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  is the alias of
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md),
  whose name is DMAR’s own so that attaching lavaan, whose `efa()` it
  calls, masks nothing.
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  fits common-factor ML or MLR models directly to incomplete raw
  observations with FIML, or explicitly requested WLSMV models to
  ordered items. Rotated loadings, factor correlations, and
  communalities carry rotation-aware confidence intervals. The
  estimator, missing-data method, and selected rotation travel with the
  result. The factor count and rotation are conditioned on, not treated
  as known without qualification. `estimator = "ULS"` adds the minimum
  residual (minres) solution of Harman and Jones (1966): unweighted
  least squares fitted to the correlation matrix (lavaan’s
  `correlation = TRUE`), whose loadings and communalities equal those of
  `psych::fa(fm = "minres")` and of a direct minimization of the squared
  off-diagonal residuals. With raw data the standard errors are lavaan’s
  normal theory sandwich for a least squares estimator
  (`robust.sem.nt`); from a supplied matrix they are `NA`, since the
  sandwich needs the raw data. ULS has no likelihood, so incomplete data
  are refused under the default `missing = "fiml"` rather than deleted
  or imputed silently: `missing = "listwise"` fits the complete cases,
  and `S` takes a correlation matrix estimated from every case (for
  example
  [`cov_fiml()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cov_fiml.md)’s).
  The ULS statistic, N - 1 times the ULS discrepancy of the
  correlations, has no reference distribution, so in the `fit_measures`
  attribute the `chi_square` row holds it without a p-value, the RMSEA
  rows and the CFI, TLI, RNI, and IFI are `NA`, and the NFI and the SRMR
  are reported;
  [`sem_fit_measures()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_fit_measures.md)
  says why in the terms of a correlation structure, in a warning of
  class `dmar_uls_standard_statistic` that
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  reads by class. `glance()` carries the fitted structure
  (`"correlation"` or `"covariance"`).

- **[`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  prints the solution, not the parameter list.** One row per item with
  its standardized pattern loading on each factor and the loading’s
  interval, its communality with its interval, and Hofmann’s (1978)
  complexity; above the table the sample, estimator, missing data
  method, rotation and its form, and standard error method; beneath it
  the variance each factor accounts for (the diagonal of Phi Lambda’
  Lambda, as a sum of squared loadings and as proportions of the total
  and of the common variance, in the new `variance_accounted`
  attribute), the factor correlations with their intervals, and a fit
  line read from the `fit_measures` attribute with its version lines.
  `knit_print()` and
  [`as_kable()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/dmar_output_helpers.md)
  show the same display. The table keeps every parameter in both metrics
  for `tidy()`, now with the complexity rows (op `"complexity"`), and a
  subset of it prints as an ordinary table. The rotation list opens from
  three criteria to ten, each applied in the form the help names and
  refused if lavaan applied it otherwise: oblique oblimin, quartimin,
  geomin, simplimax, oblimax, infomax, and Bentler; orthogonal varimax
  and quartimax; and the unrotated solution. The result carries the
  class `dmar_fa_exploratory` in front of `dmar_factor_analysis`, and
  the help states the covariance-first rule (Cudeck, 1989) with its two
  correlation-structure exceptions, minres and ordered items.

- **[`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  reports each factor’s determinacy and coefficient H.** The determinacy
  is the correlation of the regression factor score with its factor, the
  multiple correlation of the factor with the items (Grice, 2001; the
  factor determinacy index of Ferrando & Lorenzo-Seva, 2018), whose
  square is the factor’s maximal reliability under the model; H is
  Hancock and Mueller’s (2001) closed form on the factor’s standardized
  loadings alone, as Rodriguez, Reise, and Haviland (2016) apply it to
  one factor of a multidimensional solution. Each carries a delta method
  standard error over lavaan’s covariance matrix of the standardized
  estimates and Wald limits formed on the logit scale (Browne, 1982), as
  [`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md)
  forms them by default. They are rows of the table (ops `"determinacy"`
  and `"H"`), the new `factor_quality` attribute, and a block of the
  display under the factor correlations. With one factor H is the
  squared determinacy, and its standard error is the one
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)’s
  H row carries for the same model fitted the same way. Beside each
  determinacy rho the display and the attribute give 2 rho^2 - 1, the
  lowest correlation two sets of factor scores equally consistent with
  the model can have (Guttman, 1955, as Grice, 2001, presents it), with
  its delta method standard error and the determinacy’s limits mapped
  through it; it is zero when rho^2 is .5 and negative below, and no
  line is drawn.

- **[`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)’s
  omega, average variance extracted, and H rows take one interval
  form.** Each keeps lavaan’s delta method standard error, and its
  limits are formed on the logit scale and transformed back to the scale
  of the coefficient (Browne, 1982; Kelley, 2007), as
  [`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md)
  and
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  form H’s, so they lie within (0, 1) and are asymmetric near one; for H
  with one factor the three functions give the same interval for the
  same fit. A finite `wald_df` puts its t quantile on the logit scale;
  under `wald_df = "missing_information"` these rows keep the normal
  reference, as
  [`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md)’s
  logistic intervals do, and only the loadings take the t reference.
  Through this change the limits were the estimate plus or minus the
  normal quantile times the standard error, which can exceed one.

- **[`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  rotates to a partially specified target.** `rotation = "target"`
  (oblique; Browne, 1972b) and `rotation = "target_orthogonal"` (Browne,
  1972a) take the target in the new `target` argument, either as
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)’s
  named list of item keys, which targets each item at zero on every
  factor it is not keyed to, or as a matrix of items by factors with
  `NA` for each unspecified loading; with no `items`, the items the
  target names are analyzed, from raw data or from `S` alike, and the
  number of factors is read from the target. lavaan’s rotation checks
  neither the target nor whether it identifies the rotation (an
  unidentified one comes back with finite standard errors and no
  warning), so DMAR checks the identification counts before fitting and
  the rank condition on the standardized unrotated loadings (Algina,
  1980; Browne, 2001), and refuses a target that fails with an error of
  class `dmar_target_unidentified` (a target it cannot read, with
  `dmar_target_invalid`; both inherit `dmar_refusal`). The target’s mask
  is passed explicitly, so nonzero target values are kept, and no row
  weights are applied. lavaan reflects all the factors or none, so when
  any specified value is nonzero no factor is reflected: a factor with a
  nonzero value takes its sign from the target, and one whose specified
  values are all zero takes the sign of the random start that reached
  the minimum, which `seed` fixes (the help says so). Loadings the
  rotation attains exactly, which lavaan reports with a standard error
  of zero and a meaningless test, are shown as fixed by the target, at
  the target value and without a standard error; when every specified
  loading is attained the solution is the confirmatory model with those
  loadings fixed, and the tests check it against
  [`lavaan::cfa()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/lavaan/man/cfa.html). The
  rotation line of the display counts the specified loadings, the target
  prints beneath the table with a line mapping lavaan’s factor names to
  the target’s, and the `method` attribute carries the target and that
  count. The help summarizes the simulation of Myers, Jin, Ahn, Celimli,
  and Zopluoglu (2015) and says that the intervals condition on a target
  fixed before the data were seen.

- **New
  [`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md)
  compares factor counts.** It fits the exploratory model with one
  factor, two, and so on (by default up to the largest count that keeps
  a degree of freedom) and sets beside each count the chi square test,
  RMSEA with its interval, CFI, TLI, and SRMR of that model (from
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md),
  under the same version policy),
  [`lavaan::lavTestLRT()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/lavaan/man/lavTestLRT.html)’s
  test of the previous count against it, the AIC, BIC, SABIC, and HBIC
  of
  [`sem_information_criteria()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_information_criteria.md)
  with the comparison
  [`compare_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/compare_sem.md)
  draws by a chosen criterion (BIC by default: each count’s gap from the
  lowest, its relative weight, and the log Bayes factor of the best
  count over it), the reduced eigenvalue at that rank with its parallel
  analysis reference
  ([`parallel_analysis()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/parallel_analysis.md),
  Horn, 1965), and Velicer’s (1976) average squared partial correlation
  after that many components (the MAP). A count whose model does not
  converge or is improper is a row that says so, with its fit withheld
  and the counts beyond it still fitted. The lines under the table name
  the counts with the lowest criteria, how far the eigenvalues exceed
  their reference, and where the MAP is smallest; no cutoff is applied
  and no count is chosen.
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)’s
  refusal of a fit without a proper solution now carries the class
  `dmar_efa_no_solution` and a `reason` (not converged, improper, or
  standard errors unavailable), with a message that says which.

- **[`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  takes its fit measures from the unrotated solution.** lavaan’s
  FIML-corrected (robust) RMSEA, CFI, and TLI of a rotated `efa` object
  depend on the rotation, since the rotated parameterization counts more
  free parameters than the model has: on six Holzinger and Swineford
  items the robust 95 percent RMSEA interval of one two-factor model was
  \[0, 0.075\] unrotated and \[0, 0.154\] under oblimin, with the same
  chi square statistic; the standard indices do not depend on it. The
  fit line and the `fit_measures` attribute now come from the unrotated
  fit of the same model, so every rotation reports the same fit, and
  [`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md)
  reports those values.

- **[`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  can return the point estimates alone.** With the new
  `point_estimates_only = TRUE` (the default `FALSE` gives the full
  analysis, unchanged) the table has the rows and the estimates of the
  full analysis, the determinacy, H, variance accounted for, and every
  fit measure included, with its standard errors, tests, and limits
  `NA`, because none of them is computed: lavaan is asked for no
  standard errors (`se = "none"`), the rotated fit is made without the
  test statistic DMAR never reads from it, and the delta method
  intervals of the standardized solution, the determinacy, and H are
  skipped. The fit measures, the robust statistic and FIML-corrected
  indices of MLR and the scaled and shifted statistic of WLSMV among
  them, come from the unrotated fit as before and are identical, and the
  RMSEA interval keeps its own level, `rmsea_conf_level`. A loading a
  target rotation attains exactly is recognized by its value and shown
  at its target, as in the full analysis. The input, target,
  convergence, proper-solution, and no maximum refusals are unchanged.
  The refusal of a solution without rotation-aware standard errors,
  which guards against a solution that is not identified at its
  estimates, is kept by inverting the information of the unrotated fit,
  the cheap expected information first (a failure confined to the
  rotation’s part of those errors is not detected); a FIML fit whose
  errors would need unavailable H1 information is not refused, since
  none are computed, and its fit measures are withheld as before. The
  display says that standard errors and intervals were not computed, and
  states no confidence level beside the RMSEA’s on the fit line, and the
  setting travels as the `point_estimates_only` attribute and a column
  of `tidy()` and `glance()`. The time saved is largest for a rotated
  solution: about a third on the nine classic Holzinger and Swineford
  tests under ML and MLR, more than half under WLSMV, and from 29 s to
  17 s for the rotated solution of 18 items with 410 patterns of missing
  values under MLR with FIML, where what remains is the unrotated fit’s
  robust statistic and FIML-corrected fit indices; an unrotated analysis
  saves little or nothing, so a program that fits both the rotated and
  the unrotated model saves on the rotated fit alone (45 s against 34 s
  there).

- **New
  [`factor_congruence()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_congruence.md)
  compares the factors of two solutions.** It takes two loading
  matrices,
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  tables, or single-group lavaan fits (such as
  `fa_confirmatory(output = "fit")`; the result tables of
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
  [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md), and
  [`cfa_2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_2.md) are
  refused with a pointer to that route), reads fits in the standardized
  metric, and aligns the items by name. The factors of `y` are paired
  one to one with those of `x` by the assignment that maximizes the sum
  of the absolute coefficients (the Hungarian method, with ties kept in
  the listed order), and a factor whose match is negative is reflected;
  `match = "order"` pairs them by position instead, signed. Each row
  gives the coefficient of a pair and the largest absolute coefficient
  of the row’s factor with any other factor of the other solution, a
  surplus factor of the larger solution has a row of its own, and the
  full matrix, the aligned loadings of `y`, and its reflected factor
  correlations are attributes. `loadings = "structure"` compares the
  structure loadings of
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  tables and lavaan fits, not of a matrix. The help describes
  Lorenzo-Seva and ten Berge’s (2006) study of how analysts judged
  similarity as a finding about the analysts, and the table applies no
  threshold. The coefficients agree with `psych::fa.congruence()` to
  1e-12, and
  [`procrustes_phi()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/procrustes_phi.md),
  the coefficient of one pair of vectors, links to it.

- [`parallel_analysis()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/parallel_analysis.md)
  uses the same fixed one-factor ML communality reduction for observed
  and reference correlation matrices. Normal and independently
  resampled-response references remain distinct, with ordered margins
  respected when requested. Reference quantile limits describe Monte
  Carlo error, not observed-eigenvalue sampling uncertainty or
  confidence in a factor count. The output counts failed and defined
  boundary reference fits. A complete-case reference size alongside a
  FIML correlation matrix is explicitly a benchmark, with no
  effective-sample- size or conservativeness guarantee.

- [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md),
  [`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md),
  and
  [`parallel_analysis()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/parallel_analysis.md)
  read `items` with a covariance matrix as they read it with raw data:
  `S` is reduced to the named rows and columns, in the order given,
  before its entries are checked. Naming six items of a nine-item `S`
  therefore analyzes exactly what `S[items, items]` would: a missing
  entry outside the six does not refuse the call, nor does a whole
  matrix that is indefinite (as one from pairwise deletion can be) while
  the six-item submatrix is positive definite. A name that is not an
  item of `S` is refused, with a message that lists the names not found.

- **[`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md)
  and
  [`parallel_analysis()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/parallel_analysis.md)
  fit complete ordered items with `missing` left out, as
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  does.** Such items were refused with the message meant for incomplete
  ordered items
  ([`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md)
  passed on its own default, `"fiml"`; a direct call of
  [`parallel_analysis()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/parallel_analysis.md)
  stopped with “Ordered parallel analysis requires explicit pairwise or
  listwise handling”), while `missing = "listwise"` ran. The three
  functions now resolve the default by one rule: with no value missing,
  leaving `missing` out analyzes the items as they stand,
  [`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md)
  uses that method for every fit, correlation, and parallel analysis,
  and the `method` attributes record `"listwise"`. On six four-category
  items (400 cases) under `estimator = "WLSMV"`, leaving `missing` out
  gives the table of `missing = "listwise"` exactly (chi square 46.972
  on 9 df for one factor). Ordered items with a value missing still
  require `"pairwise"` or `"listwise"`, and `"fiml"` or `"ml"` is
  refused for ordered items; every call that rule refuses is refused by
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  too, with the class `dmar_argument_invalid`, before anything is
  computed or any random number drawn.

- [`sem_sam()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_sam.md)
  provides local structural-after-measurement estimation for complete
  continuous data, using ML/twostep or MLR/twostep.robust. Independent
  measurement fits and derivatives of the corrected latent covariance
  reproduce the point estimates and normal or robust uncertainty,
  including lavaan’s optional finite-sample Gamma correction. This is
  numerical agreement for the documented scope, not a coverage
  calibration. Incomplete data, derived cross-stage effects, and other
  unverified models are refused with a pointer to joint latent SEM where
  appropriate.

### Estimation, Eligibility, and Inferential Records

- **[`dmar_metadata()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/dmar_metadata.md)
  is new, and refusals carry a class.** A program built on DMAR (SIEVER,
  a simulation runner) reads a result’s estimator, standard error
  method, test, missing data method, interval method, reported version
  and correction, cases and groups, two-stage row counts, auxiliary
  variables (the reliability family’s `aux` record and
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)’s
  two-stage record included), eligibility (eligible, or qualified by an
  unavailable H1 model or by a two-stage fit that could not be computed
  again with every case, with the text of the warning the function
  gave), and bootstrap counts from one list with fixed names, whatever
  family the table came from, instead of from attributes that differ by
  family. Refusals a program handles are classed: an unavailable
  unrestricted model (`dmar_h1_unavailable`, now the class of the error
  as well as of the qualifying warning; `inherits(cnd, "error")` tells
  them apart) and a two-stage fit that could not be computed again with
  every case (`dmar_two_stage_rows_unavailable`) can be caught by name,
  inherit `dmar_refusal`, and carry a `code` and their diagnostic or row
  counts, so an application need not match the wording of a message; the
  wording of these two did not change. The refusals of the SEM fit
  family are classed the same way: an inadmissible solution
  (`dmar_inadmissible`), a two-stage fit conditional on observed
  exogenous variables (`dmar_two_stage_fixed_x`), and the refusals of
  [`sem_exact_fit_bootstrap()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_exact_fit_bootstrap.md)
  (`dmar_exact_fit_bootstrap_scope`, `dmar_pattern_too_small`, and
  `dmar_transformation_undefined`), each with the fields the help of
  [`dmar_metadata()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/dmar_metadata.md)
  lists. The message of an inadmissible solution names what failed (the
  variable with a negative variance estimate, or the matrix that is not
  positive definite, with its group and level), and the two-stage
  refusal says on which rows to refit to keep the fit’s estimates (and,
  for a fit made with `conditional.x = TRUE`, to refit with
  `conditional.x = FALSE` as well). Every other error DMAR signals is a
  `dmar_refusal` with its own class as well; the help of
  [`dmar_metadata()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/dmar_metadata.md)
  lists them.

- **A misnamed item is refused with a class by
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md),
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
  [`measurement_invariance()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_invariance.md),
  [`measurement_alignment()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_alignment.md),
  and the functions that share their checks.**
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md),
  [`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md),
  and
  [`parallel_analysis()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/parallel_analysis.md)
  refuse `items` that cannot be read from the input (a name that is not
  a column of `data` or an item of `S`, a name given twice, a name that
  is `NA`, fewer than three items, or names that are not a character
  vector) with an error of class `dmar_items_invalid`, a `dmar_refusal`
  whose `reason` element names the check that failed (`"form"`,
  `"unknown"`, `"duplicate"`, `"count"`, or, for raw data whose column
  names repeat a name or, with `items = NULL`, that have a column
  without a name, `"data_names"`) and whose `items` element holds the
  names at issue. An item that the `factors` of
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
  name (and so those of
  [`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
  [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md),
  [`cfa_2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_2.md),
  [`fa_bifactor()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_bifactor.md),
  and
  [`fa_second_order()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_second_order.md)),
  or that the model of
  [`sem_sam()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_sam.md)
  names, and that the input lacks is the same mistake and is refused
  with the same class and the reason `"unknown"` (`"form"` for a name
  that is `NA`). So is an indicator that the `model` of
  [`measurement_invariance()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_invariance.md)
  names, whether as a named list of factors or as lavaan syntax, and the
  `items` of
  [`measurement_invariance()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_invariance.md)
  and
  [`measurement_alignment()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_alignment.md)
  are refused with the class and the reasons of
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)’s.
  The messages and the calls refused are unchanged, with two exceptions:
  [`measurement_invariance()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_invariance.md)
  now refuses an item named twice in `items` (see Changes to Earlier
  Results), with the message
  [`measurement_alignment()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_alignment.md)
  gives it (“‘items’ must not repeat an item.”); and in both functions
  an `items` that repeats a name and names fewer than three columns,
  such as `c("x1", "x1")`, is refused for the repeat, where it had been
  refused for the count.
  [`sem_sam()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_sam.md),
  new in this release, names an indicator its data lack (“Indicators not
  found in ‘data’: y7.”) rather than speaking of an `items` argument it
  does not have. The class is new, and a program catches the mistake by
  it rather than by the wording, which differs by function.

- **A rung of
  [`measurement_invariance()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_invariance.md)
  that lavaan’s optimizer does not converge on stops with an error that
  names it.** Through 1.0.x the call ended with lavaan’s error from its
  fit measures (“fit measures not available if model did not converge”),
  which named no rung. Each rung is now checked before anything is read
  from it, and one that did not converge stops with an error of class
  `dmar_not_converged`, the class
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
  gives such a fit, whose message names the rung and which carries it as
  `level`, with the lavaan code that reproduces the rung’s fit as
  `syntax` and `lavaan_call`. Three items whose correlations in one
  group have a negative product, with the factor scaled by a marker item
  (lavaan’s default), give such a rung.

- A sufficient affine-collapse diagnostic replaces the ordinary blanket
  FIML case-count refusal. It uses every row observing the candidate
  support and distinguishes dimension-guaranteed collapse from numerical
  affine instability. EM convergence alone cannot establish a finite
  global H1 maximum. Analytic alpha, observed-denominator omega, FMI,
  and two-stage methods require eligible unrestricted moments. Proper
  identified constrained FIML estimates with H0-based errors can remain
  available when H1 fails; unavailable fit indices and residual
  correlations are withheld, and the reason stays in print, `tidy()`,
  and `glance()`. A separate distinct-case bootstrap screen remains an
  explicit estimability policy. H1-dependent bootstrap points apply the
  likelihood screen again to the selected resample. Fixed/conditional-X
  model diagnostics screen responses only; conditional design rank and
  exact Y-on-X relations remain unassessed.

- The footers, warnings, and help of a fit by `estimator = "ULS"` state
  the multiplier lavaan uses to form the standard statistic from the ULS
  fit function, N - G for G groups, where they said N; the help’s sample
  size convention already had it. No value changed. The warning of a ULS
  fit tested by the standard statistic has the class
  `dmar_uls_standard_statistic`.

- Continuous ULS now withholds all ML-derived robust indices, including
  CFI/TLI/RNI, consistently in fit summaries and invariance ladders.
  Qualified scaled diagnostics may remain; common-units invariance does
  not establish validity of an ML correction outside its derivation.

- CFA uses estimator-matched SE defaults: standard for ML and
  Huber-White for MLR (DMAR 1.0.x passed `se = "standard"` under every
  estimator; see Changes to Earlier Results). Incompatible SE/test
  choices cannot silently change FIML to listwise deletion. Its RMSEA
  interval keeps lavaan’s 90 percent, as DMAR 1.0.0’s
  [`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
  [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md), and
  [`cfa_2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_2.md)
  reported it whatever `conf_level` was, and the new argument
  `rmsea_conf_level` sets it (see Every RMSEA Interval at 90 Percent by
  Default). A development version of 1.1.0 made the interval follow
  `conf_level`, .95 by default; that change, which no release carried,
  is withdrawn.

- Saturated models retain lavaan’s RMSEA = 0, CI \[0, 0\], and TLI = 1
  conventions. The explanation states that these are saturated-model
  descriptions without approximate-fit evidence or a fit-index SE;
  identified parameter SEs and intervals can still be meaningful.

- [`sem_fit_measures()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_fit_measures.md)
  corrects eligible two-stage fits for auxiliary-only cases, so
  estimates, SEs, tests, indices, and sample size use every case the
  first stage read. The correction is recorded rather than reporting a
  smaller sample size beside first-stage moments based on all rows.

- The bootstrap family requires at least half of attempted replications
  and at least two defined estimates for each target. AVE retains its
  additional 100-return minimum. Ineligible intervals are withheld while
  point estimates and counts remain available. Defined improper
  estimates are retained under the documented policy. These floors do
  not guarantee nominal coverage. Categorical omega now defaults to 20
  imputations inside each bootstrap replication; its separate
  point-estimate rule already uses at least 20. No new calibration of
  the 20-imputation default is claimed.

- Reliability sensitivity takes the width-target proportion, the widths,
  and the coverage over one denominator, the simulated studies that
  returned an interval; a study without one is counted in the
  `simulation` attribute (attempted, with an interval, without), where a
  binomial interval describes Monte Carlo uncertainty in the
  width-target proportion. (DMAR 1.0.0 took the proportions of intervals
  that missed the true value over all attempted studies; see the entry
  on the record of the simulation.)

- Simultaneous-interval sentences use only a matching
  multiplicity-adjusted p-value and explicitly name it, or explain that
  no matching p-value is available. Equivalence sentences say TOST
  p. Correlation and coefficient- of-variation intervals accept supplied
  tail areas when `conf_level` was omitted and refuse an explicitly
  inconsistent level; one-sided CV bounds respect the parameter’s zero
  boundary.

- The eight score columns of
  [`factor_scores()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_scores.md)
  carry the prefix `.derived_` (`.derived_regression`,
  `.derived_regression_se`, `.derived_regression_ci_lower`,
  `.derived_regression_ci_upper`, and the same four for
  `.derived_bartlett`), so that a score joined to the observed data
  cannot be taken for an observed variable or collide with one. The
  attribute `derived_columns` names them by what each holds. Valid
  regression conditional means are retained when a factor-disturbance
  relation with an observed conditioning variable invalidates Bartlett’s
  conditional unbiasedness; the Bartlett quantities are then unavailable
  with a reason. Ordered models outside the verified score likelihood
  retain their explicit refusals.

- Every indefinite supplied covariance matrix is refused after unit
  scaling. A general loading fixed or constrained to zero is treated
  like an omitted loading by the bifactor-index eligibility rule.
  General CFA/SEM can fit such a model, but the current bifactor indices
  do not apply.

- Welch simple effects retain their valid F tests and withhold the
  inherited partial-eta-squared interval: its estimand does not match
  the reported ordinary variance-ratio estimate. Parallel population
  plans require the supplied population to satisfy parallel-model
  restrictions. Congeneric complete-data plans below items + 1 are
  raised to that feasibility minimum before missing-information
  inflation, with an assurance-planning warning.

- **A factor analysis or structural equation model fit whose likelihood
  has no maximum stops.** lavaan lets an error variance fall below zero,
  and for some models and data the likelihood then has no maximum: it
  keeps rising, by less and less, as one item’s error variance falls
  without bound and its loading grows to match, and lavaan’s optimizer
  stops where its steps stop gaining and reports convergence, at a point
  its starting values and tolerance set rather than the data. When an
  error variance is negative, DMAR now fits the model again with that
  variance held further out (at ten times its estimate, or one model
  implied variance below it, whichever is further; with several, all of
  them together and then each alone), and when the log likelihood there
  is higher, or lower by no more than 1e-6 per case (a likelihood that
  flat leaves the estimate as much to where the optimizer stopped as a
  ridge does), it stops, for every output (`output = "fit"` included),
  with an error of class `dmar_no_maximum` (a `dmar_refusal`). The
  message names the function and the item, says what the fit further out
  found, says that DMAR fits the model with lavaan, the estimation
  engine, and to see lavaan for more details, where `bounds = "pos.var"`
  or a different model are the choices, and prints the lavaan code that
  reproduces the fit (the model syntax DMAR built, less the lines that
  define its indices, and the call, with a placeholder for the data that
  selects the items where lavaan would otherwise read every variable it
  is given); a model whose syntax would carry the message past the 8,170
  bytes R prints of an error has the call printed and the syntax left in
  the condition. The condition carries the syntax, the call, the items,
  their error variances, the two log likelihoods, the tolerance, and the
  number of cases. A finite negative estimate, at a maximum of the
  likelihood, is reported as before: the nine-test bifactor model of
  [`fa_bifactor()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_bifactor.md)‘s
  help gives visual perception an error variance of -41, and the
  likelihood falls on either side of it, while a fourth group factor on
  the Woody-McCall, revised paper form board, and flags tests sends the
  error variance of paper form board to -1163 under FIML, where the
  likelihood is still rising, and that model now stops. The check covers
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
  (with
  [`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
  [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md), and
  [`cfa_2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_2.md)),
  [`fa_bifactor()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_bifactor.md),
  [`fa_second_order()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_second_order.md),
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  (whose refusal is also a `dmar_efa_no_solution`, with the reason
  `"no maximum"`, which
  [`factor_count()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/factor_count.md)
  reports as that count’s status),
  [`measurement_invariance()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_invariance.md)
  (naming the rung and the group), the configural fit of
  [`measurement_alignment()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_alignment.md),
  and the single-factor fits of
  [`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md)
  and
  [`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md)
  (the tau-equivalent fit of
  [`reliability_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_alpha.md)
  has a maximum, since its equal loadings keep one item’s error variance
  from running off). It applies to maximum likelihood fits; least
  squares and WLSMV fits have no likelihood and are not checked. A
  solution with no negative error variance costs nothing more; one with
  a negative error variance costs a refit, or, with several, one with
  all of them held and then one for each until one shows a ridge (0.03 s
  for the nine-test model above, and 0.08 s for the model with the
  fourth group factor, whose own fit takes 5 s). Inside a bootstrap (the
  reliability family’s,
  [`ci_bifactor_indices()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_bifactor_indices.md)’s,
  and that of
  [`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md)
  on a fit), a replication with no maximum is set aside and counted
  among the replications that raised an error, under a message that
  names the item, and the run goes on. The engine fits each such
  replication a second time to recover its message, with the second fits
  spread over the same `ncpus` processes as the replications, and a fit
  that runs off is among the slowest lavaan makes: on one process, 100
  replications of the 15-test bifactor model of
  [`fa_bifactor()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_bifactor.md)’s
  help, 8 of them with no maximum, took 143 s, against 99 s without the
  check. The warning of
  [`fa_bifactor()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_bifactor.md)
  about an improper solution names sampling error, a model that does not
  describe the items, and a group factor the data barely separate from
  the general factor as the possible causes, where it named the last
  alone. The structural equation models DMAR fits with lavaan are
  checked the same way. The fit of the analysis model to the population
  moments, from which
  [`ss_aipe_composite_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_composite_sem.md),
  [`ss_power_composite_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_sem.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sem_path()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sem_path.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity.md)
  (to `supposed_cov_matrix`, and to `true_cov_matrix`, now fit before
  any replication is drawn) read their population values, stops the
  planner when it has no maximum, with the code that fits the model to
  the matrix given (or to `cov_sem(true_model)$sigma_theta`) and the
  model printed whole, its `:=` lines included, since they define the
  user’s own quantities. So does the lavaan fit from which
  [`mediation_mbco()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediation_mbco.md)
  starts its OpenMx fits. Its code fits the summary statistics directly
  when they are one group’s (a covariance matrix given as a data frame
  converted by [`as.matrix()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/matrix.html)); for
  several groups, or a model whose product terms the function writes
  into columns, it fits the data the function builds from them, which
  the message describes exactly, seed included, since the moments of a
  product column depend on the rows drawn; and a lavaan fit given as
  `model` is refused without code. The message names a different model
  as the choice, since the OpenMx model carries no bounds. A replication
  of those planners’ Monte Carlo with no maximum, which lavaan reports
  as converged where its optimizer stopped, is set aside as one that did
  not converge, and a fresh sample is drawn in its place.
  [`ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity.md)
  and
  [`sem_exact_fit_bootstrap()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_exact_fit_bootstrap.md)
  read only the chi square of a fit, and are not checked: along a ridge
  the likelihood levels off, so the chi square, unlike the estimates,
  does not depend on where the optimizer stopped (in 60 bootstrap
  samples of a factor with four weak indicators, the 7 that ran off had
  statistics of 0.37 to 3.96 that would move by 0.00005 to 0.0011
  further out), and setting such a fit aside would change the reference
  distribution, or refuse a population RMSEA that is determined. A
  bootstrap sample with no maximum therefore stays among the improper
  ones, counted or set aside as `improper` says. In a structural model,
  lavaan carries an observed variable that enters a regression as a
  latent variable of its own: an outcome, a covariate, or an indicator
  that also enters a regression (with a direct effect on it, for
  example). The variance of such a variable is not held and its loading
  is not moved, so a ridge on such an indicator, or on an outcome
  regressed on a latent variable, is not looked for; on the ridges of
  that kind tried, lavaan reported no convergence, where the check does
  not apply. A ridge on which lavaan reports no convergence, as it often
  does with a marker item fixing the scale, was already a replication
  that did not converge. The examples of these pages, none of whose fits
  has a negative error variance, take no longer: the check reads each
  fit’s parameter table, 5 to 15 microseconds a fit (21 fits in each
  composite planner’s examples, a fraction of a millisecond), and refits
  only a fit with a negative error variance, which in a Monte Carlo at a
  small N costs one refit for each replication that has one.

### Either Variance in the Denominator of Every Omega

- **[`reliability_omega_categorical()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega_categorical.md)
  gains a `denominator` argument.** `"observed"` (the default, and the
  only coefficient the function computed before) builds the variance of
  the summed categories from the unrestricted polychoric correlations,
  as Kelley and Pornprasertmanit (2016, Eq. 18) did; it is the
  categorical counterpart of robust omega. `"model_implied"` builds it
  from the latent-response correlations the fitted single-factor model
  reproduces, which is categorical omega as Green and Yang (2009)
  defined it: their appendix program takes “the reproduced (model-based)
  correlation matrix” as the input to the denominator. The help page had
  attributed the unrestricted denominator to Green and Yang’s Eq. 21; it
  now states which paper used which. Every interval method applies to
  both settings, and the bootstrap recomputes the coefficient with the
  chosen denominator on each replication.
  [`reliability()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability.md)
  forwards `denominator` for `type = "omega_categorical"` as it already
  did for `type = "omega"`. The model implied setting needs no
  unrestricted polychoric correlation, but its loadings rest on the
  correlations the data do determine. Those identify the loadings only
  when they connect every item to the others, directly or through other
  items, and include at least one cycle of an odd number of items (three
  items whose three correlations are all determined, for example). When
  they do not, the loadings are arbitrary. In 13 of 60 samples of 300
  from Green and Yang’s mixed-skew design (the help page’s example with
  `N <- 300` and seeds 1 to 60 in place of 113) they did not, and in 2
  of those lavaan’s start values gave loadings of opposite signs and a
  categorical omega of 0.05 and 0.09, against a population value of
  0.716. Both settings then stop with an error naming the undetermined
  pairs and either the blocks of items no determined correlation joins
  or, within one block, the two sets of items between which every
  determined correlation runs. A bootstrap replication or a completed
  data set in that state is set aside and counted as undetermined. The
  argument changes no existing result; what the observed setting now
  does with a correlation the data do not determine is under Changes to
  Earlier Results.

- **[`bifactor_indices()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bifactor_indices.md)
  gains a `denominator` argument.** The default, `"model_implied"`,
  divides by the variances the fitted bifactor model reproduces
  (Rodriguez, Reise, & Haviland, 2016), now including any residual
  covariances the model specifies (see Changes to Earlier Results);
  `"observed"` divides omega, omega_H, and omega_HS by the composite
  variances estimated from the data, the denominator of robust omega
  carried to the bifactor coefficients. ECV, PUC, and H do not depend on
  the setting. The observed setting requires a single-group fit. For a
  fit to ordered items both settings describe the sum of the latent
  responses behind the categories, not the summed categories; a new
  `metric` attribute (`"observed"` or `"latent_response"`) records
  which, and the printed line names it.

- **Every omega now names its denominator and reports its local
  dependence.** The printed tables of
  [`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md),
  [`reliability_omega_categorical()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega_categorical.md),
  and
  [`bifactor_indices()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bifactor_indices.md)
  state in one line how the total variance in the denominator was
  estimated, so a reader need not know the default to know which
  coefficient is on the page.
  [`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md)
  and
  [`reliability_omega_categorical()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega_categorical.md)
  also carry a `residual_cor` attribute (the residual correlations of
  the single-factor fit, the largest of them, the item pair it belongs
  to, and whether the fit is saturated) and print the largest under the
  table. The residual correlations come from a maximum likelihood fit
  whatever the interval method (the weighted least squares fit behind
  `ci_method = "adf"` has residuals of its own and is not used). With
  auxiliary variables, under FIML or two-stage estimation, the residual
  correlations are those of the items alone, under the items’ own names.
  With three items the single-factor model is saturated and a proper
  solution reproduces every correlation, so the attribute’s `saturated`
  element is `TRUE`, no pair is named, and the printed line says so. An
  observed denominator protects the denominator, not the numerator: a
  doublet or a method factor shared by a few same-signed items raises
  their loadings, and omega with them, under either setting while
  leaving the two denominators close. The residual correlations are
  where such structure shows, although when it sits on the items that
  dominate the factor the single factor absorbs it and the misfit
  appears among the other items. No row of any table changes; the
  additions are attributes and printed lines.

- **In a bootstrap, the model implied setting sets aside only the
  replications whose loadings are not identified or whose solution is
  improper.** A resample often leaves out the few respondents who
  determine a polychoric correlation, so a bootstrap meets undetermined
  correlations far more often than the sample does (see Changes to
  Earlier Results for the observed setting).
  `denominator = "model_implied"` needs no unrestricted polychoric
  correlation, so it sets aside a replication only when the correlations
  left determined do not identify the loadings or, as the observed
  setting does, when its solution is improper. That was 1 of 200 in a
  percentile bootstrap of the help page’s complete data, of 1,000
  respondents (`seed = 1`). In the 45 of the 60 samples of 300 above
  whose point estimate is identified and proper, a median of 42% of the
  replications was set aside (`B = 50`, `seed = 1`), and more than half
  in 15 of them.

- **Help pages name the denominator each paper used.**
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
  and [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md)
  described the categorical omega that
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
  reports for ordered factors as Green and Yang’s (2009); it is their
  assembly with the unrestricted polychoric denominator of Kelley and
  Pornprasertmanit (2016, Eq. 18), the default of
  [`reliability_omega_categorical()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega_categorical.md),
  and the pages and the message now say so. The example of
  [`reliability_omega_categorical()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega_categorical.md)
  now reproduces Green and Yang’s mixed-skew design and sets their
  coefficient beside the one Kelley and Pornprasertmanit recommended.

- \*\*The categorical omega assembly is checked against Green and Yang’s

  2009. population values.\*\* A new test reproduces ten entries of the
        nonlinear SEM column of their Table 1. Nine agree to the third
        decimal; the tenth (binary items, two negatively and two
        positively skewed, loadings of .8; published .591) computes as
        0.5904.

### One Bootstrap Engine for the Reliability Family

- **The reliability bootstrap refits by maximum likelihood.** Every
  replication of robust omega, of a bootstrap interval for the model
  implied omega, and of the model implied
  [`reliability_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_alpha.md)
  refit the single-factor model by robust maximum likelihood, whose
  estimates are those of maximum likelihood; only the standard errors
  and the test statistic differ, and a replication reads neither. The
  replications now refit by ML, with the same estimates to the last bit,
  so every interval is unchanged for a given seed, and the bootstrap is
  faster: the scaled test statistic had cost 1.3, 10, and 37 times an ML
  fit at 9, 24, and 40 items, and a 40-replication bootstrap of robust
  omega on 24 items now takes 1.5 s rather than 7.1 s. Robust omega also
  fit the model twice on every call, once for the estimate and once for
  the residual correlations, and now fits it once.

- **Every replication is counted where parallel workers keep the count,
  and the draws are returned.** The `bootstrap` attribute gains
  `improper_kept`, `not_converged`, `too_few_cases`, `improper_rule`,
  `caution`, `require_half`, `ncpus`, `t` (the estimate of every
  replication), and `status` (its fate: proper, improper, error,
  non_finite, undetermined, or not_converged), and the result gains the
  `B_used` attribute that the package’s other bootstraps carry. No
  element changes meaning; `not_converged` is zero for the reliability
  coefficients, whose replications still count a fit that did not
  converge among the non-finite ones, and is used by
  [`ci_bifactor_indices()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_bifactor_indices.md).
  Through 1.0.1 the counts were kept where a forked worker could not
  report them, so a session with `options(boot.parallel = "multicore")`
  lost every count.

- **`ncpus` spreads the replications over several processes.**
  [`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md),
  [`reliability_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_alpha.md),
  [`reliability_kr20()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_kr20.md),
  [`reliability_omega_categorical()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega_categorical.md),
  [`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md),
  and
  [`reliability()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability.md)
  gain `ncpus = 1L`: forked workers where the platform allows them and a
  socket cluster on Windows, with the jackknife behind a BCa
  acceleration on the same workers. boot draws every resample before any
  replication runs, so a given seed returns the same interval, counts,
  and draws whatever `ncpus` is.

- **`progress` follows a bootstrap and can stop it.**
  [`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md),
  [`reliability_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_alpha.md),
  [`reliability_kr20()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_kr20.md),
  [`reliability_omega_categorical()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega_categorical.md),
  [`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md),
  [`reliability()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability.md),
  and
  [`ci_bifactor_indices()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_bifactor_indices.md)
  gain `progress = NULL`, their last argument: a function that the
  bootstrap calls as `progress(done, total)`, with the replications
  attempted so far and `B`, after each replication when `ncpus = 1` and
  after each block of `ncpus * ceiling(B / (50 * ncpus))` replications
  (about a fiftieth of `B`) on several processes. An application that
  runs a long bootstrap, a Shiny app above all, can show how far it has
  gone and let its user stop it: when the callback returns `FALSE`, the
  bootstrap stops before the next replication or block with an error of
  class `dmar_bootstrap_cancelled` that carries `done` and `total`, and
  any other value is ignored. A BCa acceleration comes from the
  jackknife when fewer replications than cases return a value or the
  regression on the resampling frequencies fails, and while the
  jackknife runs the callback is called after each leave-one-out refit,
  or each block of them on several processes, with `done` and `total`
  both `B`, so a stop is honored there too, and `done` equal to `total`
  does not mean that the bootstrap has finished; the bootstrap then
  impute replications of categorical omega under `missing = "mi"` report
  the same way. An error inside the callback stops the call with an
  error of class `dmar_progress_error` that carries `done`, `total`, and
  the callback’s own condition, its class intact, as `parent`. The
  callback runs outside the random number stream, so a given seed
  returns the same interval, counts, and draws with or without it, and
  the default `NULL` runs the bootstrap exactly as before.
  [`?dmar_metadata`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/dmar_metadata.md)
  lists both classes beside the refusals.
  [`sem_exact_fit_bootstrap()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/sem_exact_fit_bootstrap.md)
  and
  [`average_variance_extracted()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/average_variance_extracted.md)
  have no `progress` argument in 1.1.0: their bootstraps do not run
  through this engine, so an application that calls them cannot follow
  or stop them this way.

- **`improper = c("keep", "drop")` for the single-factor coefficients.**
  [`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md),
  [`reliability_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_alpha.md),
  and
  [`reliability()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability.md)
  gain `improper`. A bootstrap replication whose solution was improper
  (a negative error variance) but still yielded a coefficient was kept
  and not counted; it is now counted, kept by default, and set aside
  under `"drop"`. Keeping is the default because setting such
  replications aside conditions the bootstrap distribution on
  admissibility and trims its upper tail; in a small coverage check
  (model implied one-factor omega, five items with loadings .95, .70,
  .60, .50, and .40, N = 60, 120 data sets per condition, B = 300),
  percentile intervals covered at .958 when they were kept and at .933
  when they were dropped, a difference near the Monte Carlo standard
  error of about .02. Under `"drop"` an improper point estimate stops
  when a bootstrap is requested. When the replications set aside and the
  improper ones kept reach the tail area (1 - C)/2 of B, the warning and
  the printed line add a caution that the limits depend on how they were
  treated. Categorical omega and H are not defined for an improper
  solution, so they set such replications aside, and both record
  `improper_rule = "drop"`.

- **Replications of three items with no single-factor solution are
  counted on their own.** The `bootstrap` attribute carries
  `no_solution`: the replications set aside because the correlations of
  three items had a product that was not positive, which no loadings
  reproduce. It is a subset of `improper`, reported under the status
  `"improper"`, and the warning and the printed line name these
  replications apart from the Heywood cases (“had no single-factor
  solution”).
  [`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md)
  from data counts them the same way, and its warning says that setting
  aside a Heywood case can trim the upper tail of the bootstrap
  distribution while one with no single-factor solution belongs on
  neither side. The element is zero for categorical omega, the bifactor
  intervals, and H from a fitted model, whose refits are not checked for
  it, as the help of
  [`reliability_omega_categorical()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega_categorical.md),
  [`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md),
  and
  [`ci_bifactor_indices()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_bifactor_indices.md)
  says; the categorical page defines `returned` and `non_finite` as
  [`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md)‘s
  page does. The warnings describe an improper replication by its
  criterion, an error variance below zero (a standardized loading past
  one; on the items’ own metric a loading above one is routine in a
  proper solution), and the bootstrap then impute warnings of
  categorical omega describe an improper replication or completed data
  set the same way. A replication with no single-factor solution is set
  aside under either rule: on the estimator’s scale it continues the top
  of the bootstrap distribution, since one loading, and omega with it,
  grows without bound toward that boundary, while its correlations point
  to low reliability, so it belongs on neither side. When some are set
  aside, the caution adds that the lower limit is likely too high. In a
  coverage check of the three-item estimator (three items of unit
