  [`randomization_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/randomization_test.md)
  and
  [`plot_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_smd.md)
  count the group sizes of raw data as integers
  ([`randomization_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/randomization_test.md)
  with [`sum()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/sum.html) of a logical vector,
  [`plot_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_smd.md)
  with [`length()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/length.html)), so they
  stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” for any data
  whose two group sizes have a product above 2^31 - 1 (46,341 scores in
  each group, or 100,000 and 21,475), whatever the type of the scores.
  The sizes are now multiplied as doubles, and the results are those for
  the same sizes given as doubles:
  `ci_smd_c(smd_c = .2, n_C = 50000L, n_E = 50000L)` gives the limits
  0.188 and 0.212, `convert_r_d(.2, n_1 = 50000L, n_2 = 50000L)` gives
  0.408, `ss_power_smd(.02, n_1 = 50000, n_2 = 50000)` gives the power
  .885,
  [`randomization_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/randomization_test.md)
  reports the standardized mean difference with its interval,
  [`plot_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_smd.md)
  draws the interval that
  [`ci_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_smd.md)
  gives for the sizes as doubles, and
  `ss_aipe_smd_sensitivity(true_smd = .1, specified_n_per_group = 50000L, width = .03, G = 3, seed = 1)`
  gives the table of the same call with `50000` (mean interval width
  0.0248). The specified-size paths of
  [`ss_power_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_reg_coef.md)
  and
  [`ss_power_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2.md)
  turned a size above 2^31 - 1 into NA (“NAs introduced by coercion to
  integer range”): in DMAR 1.0.0
  `ss_power_reg_coef(true_f2 = 1e-9, p = 3, specified_N = 3e9)`
  (`cohen_f2` in 1.0.x) returned NA for the power, and
  `ss_power_R2(true_R2 = 1e-9, p = 3, specified_N = 3e9)`
  (`population_R2` in 1.0.x) stopped with “missing value where
  TRUE/FALSE needed”. Such a size is now used as given: the first call
  gives the power .410, and the second .275.

- **[`krippendorff_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/krippendorff_alpha.md)
  gives alpha for 46,342 or more pairable values.** It formed N (N - 1),
  where N is the number of pairable values counted with
  [`length()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/length.html), as a product of
  integers, which becomes NA from N = 46,342 on (46,342 times 46,341 is
  2,147,534,622). Take 23,171 units rated twice on three nominal
  categories, drawn after `set.seed(7)` as
  `r1 <- sample(1:3, 23171, TRUE)` and
  `r2 <- ifelse(runif(23171) < .7, r1, sample(1:3, 23171, TRUE))`. In
  DMAR 1.0.0 `krippendorff_alpha(cbind(r1, r2))` summed the distances
  over all 1.07e9 pairs of values and then stopped with “missing value
  where TRUE/FALSE needed”, after the warning “NAs produced by integer
  overflow”. The product is now formed as a double, and the same call,
  after the same sum over pairs, gives alpha .698 (D_expected .667), the
  values from the frequencies of the ratings.

- **The Paule-Mandel estimate of `tau2` and the Q-profile interval for
  `tau2` no longer depend on the units of the effect sizes.**
  [`meta_es()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/meta_es.md),
  [`meta_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/meta_smd.md),
  [`meta_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/meta_r.md),
  and
  [`plot_forest()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_forest.md)
  with `method = "pm"` found the PM estimate, and every estimator found
  the limits for `tau2` and I2, by root searches that stopped within
  1.5e-8 of the root in the units of `tau2`, a distance larger than
  `tau2` for effect sizes in small units. For y = (-1, 0, 1) with
  sampling variances .01 the PM estimate is 0.99 and the interval 0.2611
  to 39.49; for the same effect sizes times 1e-6 (variances times 1e-12)
  the estimate, divided by 1e-12, was 10.1 and the interval 101 to 101.
  The searches are now made on `tau2` divided by the scale of the data,
  as the REML search already was, and stop at a distance relative to the
  root, so the results for effect sizes multiplied by c are those for
  the original ones times c squared (`tau2` and its limits) or c (the
  pooled estimate, its standard error, and the prediction limits). For
  the 12 simulated studies of the package’s tests the PM `tau2` was
  0.0431063198 and is 0.0431063219; metafor at its default tolerance
  gives 0.04310566, so a comparison with its default output can differ
  in the sixth significant digit.

- **[`ss_aipe_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_smd.md)
  no longer passes on the warnings of R’s
  [`pt()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/TDist.html) in its assurance step.**
  For a negative `true_smd` it asked
  [`pt()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/TDist.html) for the lower tail of a
  probability near 1 (15 warnings
  `full precision may not have been achieved in 'pnt{final}'` at
  `true_smd = -1`, `width = .5`, and `assurance = .90`). Each tail is
  now computed directly as a small probability, and those plans give no
  warning.

- **[`equivalence_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_smd.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_equivalence_smd_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_equivalence_smd_sensitivity.md)
  give their intervals when the product of the two group sizes passes
  2^31 - 1.** The product of the two group sizes, stored as integers,
  overflowed R’s integer range (“NAs produced by integer overflow”).
  [`equivalence_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_smd.md)
  with integer `n_1` and `n_2`, or with raw data, whose two sizes had a
  product above 2,147,483,647 (46,341 or more in each group, or 40,000
  and 60,000) returned `NA` for the *t* statistics, the *p*-values, the
  limits, and `equivalent`; it now returns them
  (`equivalence_smd(smd = .1, n_1 = 46341L, n_2 = 46341L, smd_lower = .2, smd_upper = .2)`
  gives the limits 0.089 and 0.111). The sensitivity function, whose
  sizes are integers, stopped there with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE
  needed” (at 54,112 per group, the plan for `width = .02` at a 90
  percent level) and now returns its table.

- **[`ss_aipe_equivalence_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_equivalence_smd.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_equivalence_smd_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_equivalence_smd_sensitivity.md)
  check their numeric arguments on entry.** A missing, not-a-number, or
  infinite `true_smd` or `supposed_smd`, a missing or vector-valued
  equivalence bound, a `specified_n_per_group` that is missing,
  fractional, or below 2, and a missing `width` are refused with a
  condition of class `dmar_argument_invalid` that names the argument.
  DMAR 1.0.0 stopped on most of these with R’s “missing value where
  TRUE/FALSE needed”, refused an infinite planning value as “Required n
  exceeded 1e6 per group; check inputs”, and truncated a per-group size
  of 10.7 to 10 without a word.

- **[`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md)
  with `fit` checks the covariance matrix of the estimates as the factor
  analysis tables do.** Where that matrix comes from an information
  matrix that is singular in the directions the fit’s equality
  constraints leave free, the standard error and limits are `NA`, with
  the warning of class `dmar_result_qualified` that
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
  gives for the same fit; a two-item factor uncorrelated in the sample
  with the other factor had `H` = .853 with a standard error of 533.8
  and the interval \[0, 1\], with no warning. Where lavaan computed no
  standard errors,
  [`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md)
  stopped with “argument is of length zero” and now returns the estimate
  with the same warning (the `vcov_basis` attribute is then `"none"`).

- **The check of the information matrix in
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
  [`fa_bifactor()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_bifactor.md),
  [`fa_second_order()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_second_order.md),
  and
  [`reliability_H()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_H.md)
  reads a fit with `ceq.simple = TRUE` correctly.** Parameters that
  share a label then share one free number and carry no equality
  constraint, and the check took the information of the unconstrained
  parameters for that of the model, so models identified by their labels
  (a two-item factor with equal loadings, two groups with loadings equal
  by label, a `group.equal` fit) were reported singular.

- **[`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
  and
  [`fa_bifactor()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_bifactor.md)
  with `output = "standardized"` and `se = "none"` return the
  standardized estimates,** with the `se`, `z`, `pvalue`, `ci.lower`,
  and `ci.upper` columns `NA`; they stopped with “missing value where
  TRUE/FALSE needed”.
  [`fa_second_order()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_second_order.md),
  which returned the estimates without those columns, has them too.

- **[`bifactor_indices()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bifactor_indices.md)
  no longer asks lavaan for the standard errors of the standardized
  solution, which it does not use,** so lavaan’s warning “Could not
  compute standard errors!” no longer reaches the caller beside the
  Heywood warning of an improper fit. The indices are unchanged.

- **[`htmt()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/htmt.md)
  refuses blocks that are not disjoint sets of distinct items under
  distinct names.** An item listed twice in a block, an item placed in
  two blocks, or two blocks under one name gave a ratio without a word:
  for nine simulated items whose blocks `A = x1, x2, x3` and
  `B = x4, x5, x6` give .615, listing `x1` twice in `A` gave .544,
  placing `x3` in both blocks .944, and naming both blocks `A` 1.533.
  These, and an item whose name belongs to two or more columns of
  `data`, are refused before anything is computed, with an error of
  class `dmar_htmt_blocks_invalid` whose `reason` element names the
  check (`"repeated"`, `"shared"`, `"construct_names"`, or
  `"data_names"`) and whose `blocks` and `items` elements name what is
  at issue. Disjoint blocks give the same ratios and bounds as before.

- **The standardized cluster randomized planners (`ss_aipe_crd_es_*()`)
  count and report the simulated data sets that give no usable interval,
  and pass on the warnings of their fits.** The counts, the reasons, and
  the first error message are in the new attribute `simulation` (also
  read with
  [`dmar_metadata()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/dmar_metadata.md))
  and on the printed line “Replications”; a warning of class
  `dmar_replications_without_interval` gives the counts when data sets
  failed, and a design at which no data set gave an interval, or at
  which an assurance cannot be reached, is refused with an error of
  class `dmar_computation_failed`, where the width had been `NaN` or the
  search had stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”. The
  planners wrapped their search in
  [`suppressWarnings()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/warning.html); each kind
  of warning a fit gives is now given once, as a warning of class
  `dmar_result_qualified` that counts the data sets that gave it. A fit
  of optimizer status 0 or 1 is used, and any other status counts as a
  failed data set. The models are built with `mxExpectationRAM()`,
  `mxFitFunctionML()`, and `mxFitFunctionAlgebra()` in place of the
  deprecated `mxRAMObjective()` and `mxAlgebraObjective()`, with
  identical limits, and the socket cluster used on Windows is stopped
  however the simulation ends.

- **The searches of the standardized cluster randomized planners end.**
  The search upward for the cluster size at a fixed number of clusters
  had no end when the width leveled off above the target. It now
  simulates cluster sizes up to 100 above the size the unstandardized
  difference needs (above its own start when that size is beyond
  100,000) and never above 500 (a search that would start above 500 is
  refused with `reason` `"cluster_size_beyond_reach"`, whose field
  `lower_bound` says whether the start is a lower bound on the size the
  target needs), and a width still above the target is refused with
  `reason` `"width_not_reached"`, the narrowest width found, and its
  Monte Carlo interval. Three designs in a row with no finite width end
  either search (`reason` `"no_finite_width"`), and a call simulates at
  most 500 designs (`reason` `"search_budget"`); each is an error of
  class `dmar_computation_failed`. The two planners over both sizes pick
  the first of tied widths or costs, where a tie stopped them with an
  error from `if()`.

- **The cluster randomized searches meet a budget or a width equal to
  the end of a bracket.** A cost or a width equal to the target at the
  end of a bracket of the coarse search stopped
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_budget(budget = 20000, cluster_size = 20, cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 1)`,
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_budget(budget = 10000, n_clusters = 10, cluster_cost = 0, individual_cost = 1)`,
  and the two width planners at the width of 1000 clusters of 20
  (0.1216020) and of 100 clusters of 1000 (0.3557016) with “‘from’ must
  be a finite number” in DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of
  1.1.0. Each now returns 1000, at a cost equal to the budget or a width
  equal to the target; their `ss_aipe_crd_es_*()` counterparts share the
  budget searches. In a grid of 480 budget searches the 51 (number of
  clusters) and 29 (cluster size) that stopped now return a size, and no
  other result changed; in 1,152 cluster size searches from a width, at
  targets that are not the width of a design, no result changed. A width
  equal to the target inside a bracket also meets it now (see “Changes
  to Earlier Results”).

- **[`ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd.md)
  returns a numeric `value` column.** The cluster size search gave the
  string “\> 100000” for a number of clusters that cannot reach the
  width, which made the whole column character whenever one of the
  numbers of clusters tried could not:
  `ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width(width = .5, cluster_cost = 10, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8)`
  returned the strings “80”, “7”, “0.499131775130474”, and “1360” in
  DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions of 1.1.0 (the development
  versions also “0.5”, the width asked for). The search gives `Inf`
  internally, and the plan is the same numbers (80 clusters of 7, budget
  1360), now numeric in the table and in `tidy()` and `glance()`: in 720
  calls the number of clusters, the cluster size, and the budget are
  identical, and the width differs only where the development versions
  returned strings, by at most 2.5e-15 relative. Given back as `width`,
  the width a plan reports now gives that plan:
  `ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width(width = 1, cluster_cost = 30, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .5, ...)`
  plans 20 clusters of 10 for a budget of 800, and the string
  “0.994337792651072” that DMAR 1.0.0 and the development versions
  reported for its width is below that width and, given back, gave 19
  clusters of 13 for 817. Every cluster randomized planner returns a
  numeric `value` column.
  [`ss_aipe_crd_n_individuals_fixed_width()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd.md)
  refuses a width no cluster size up to 100,000 reaches with `reason`
  `"width_not_reachable"` (class `dmar_argument_invalid`, as in the
  development versions), the width the interval falls toward as the
  clusters grow as `width_limit`, and whether a larger cluster size
  would reach it; the message said only that the target was “impossible
  to achieve”.
  [`ss_aipe_crd_es_n_individuals_fixed_width()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd_es.md)
  gives its refusal of a search whose unstandardized start is beyond
  100,000 the `reason` `"cluster_size_beyond_reach"`, with
  `start = Inf`.

- **The searches over both sizes no longer stop with an error from R.**
  `ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_budget(budget = 20000, cluster_cost = 1000, individual_cost = 1, pr_treat = .1, true_var_between = .2, true_var_within = .8)`
  stopped with “invalid ‘type’ (list) of argument” in DMAR 1.0.0 and the
  development versions of 1.1.0, because no number of clusters it tried
  was within the budget, and `pr_treat = .005` stopped with “wrong sign
  in ‘by’ argument”, because the floor of two clusters in each
  condition (400) was above the end of the search (200). Both are
  refused with `reason` `"budget_infeasible"` (20 clusters of 2 cost
  20,040; 400 cost 400,800). In 720 calls of the budget planner the 92
  that stopped this way are refused, and the 628 plans are identical.
  `ss_aipe_crd_es_both_fixed_budget(budget = 1000, cluster_cost = 5, individual_cost = 1, true_es = .5, true_icc = .9, pr_treat = .5, G = 2, seed = 113)`
  simulated one more cluster than the budget buys, with a cluster size
  of `NA`, and stopped with “invalid ‘times’ argument” in both; that
  design is no longer simulated, and the call returns 142 clusters of 2.

- **The documented variance pairs (between, ICC) and (within, ICC) plan
  in the six unstandardized cluster randomized planners.**
  `ss_aipe_crd_n_clusters_fixed_width(width = 1, cluster_size = 20, pr_treat = .5, true_var_between = .2, true_icc = .2)`
  and the same call with `true_var_within = .8, true_icc = .2` stopped
  with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” in DMAR 1.0.0 and the
  development versions of 1.1.0; both return 18 clusters, as the other
  pairs do. The variances are resolved once per call, where they had
  been resolved at every number of clusters tried; every call with
  consistent inputs gives the same plan (36 calls over the six planners
  and six pairs, identical but for the string rounding of
  [`ss_aipe_crd_both_fixed_width()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_crd.md)
  above).

- **[`mediation_mbco()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediation_mbco.md)
  refuses a joint hypothesis one of whose expressions adds no
  restriction to the others,** before any model is fit, with a condition
  of class `dmar_argument_invalid` (`arg = "hypotheses"`) whose
  `redundant` and `kept` elements name the expressions. The degrees of
  freedom of a joint test were the number of expressions, so a repeated
  expression, a multiple or combination of others, or one that is 0
  wherever the others are counted as a restriction: in the single
  mediator model fit to 100 simulated cases (seed 731),
  `hypotheses = list(h = c("a", "a"))` gave the statistic of `"a"`,
  4.980, with 2 degrees of freedom (*p* = .0829, where `"a"` gives *p* =
  .0256), and `c("a*b", "b")`, whose null set is that of `"b"`, gave *p*
  = .0316, where `"b"` gives .00858. The rank of the Jacobian of the
  constraints at the unrestricted estimates, and points of the null set
  of the other expressions found branch by branch, find such an
  expression. `c("a*b", "a*cp")`, whose null set is `a = 0` or
  `b = cp = 0`, is still tested with 2 degrees of freedom. See
  *Constraints that add no restriction* in
  [`?mediation_mbco`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediation_mbco.md).

- **[`mediation_mbco()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediation_mbco.md)
  fits badly scaled variables in a rescaled metric.** When the standard
  deviations of the observed variables differ by a factor of 1000 or
  more (the rule of lavaan’s `rescale_data` option), each variable is
  divided by a power of 2 near its standard deviation for the OpenMx
  fits, and every result is returned in the original metric; the
  divisors are in the new `"rescale"` attribute. The optimizers had
  stopped far from the maximum: with the seed-731 data, `x` multiplied
  by 1000, and `m` divided by 1000, the statistic for `"a"` was 1316.2
  and is 4.980, the least squares value, and that of the indirect effect
  7.56 and now 4.980.

- **[`mediation_mbco()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediation_mbco.md)
  fits the null model of a conditional indirect effect at a probe value
  branch by branch** (`(a0 + a1*w)*b` is 0 where `b = 0` or where
  `a0 + a1*w = 0`): in a first-stage moderated mediation of 300
  simulated cases (seed 3812) the statistic at a moderator value of 1
  was 37.294 and is 33.631, the smaller of the two branch statistics.
  When every branch fit is valid, the smallest is the constrained
  minimum and the constrained searches, which could end just off the
  null set, are not run.

- **[`mediation_mbco()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediation_mbco.md)
  reports the test of a total effect (and of other sums and differences
  of effects) where its null fit had failed** (reported as `NA` with a
  warning in 10 of 100 simulated data sets of 150 cases with every
  coefficient 0). A constraint without branches is now also started from
  the full-model estimates moved onto its null set.

- **[`?mediation_mbco`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediation_mbco.md)
  states the conditions under which the likelihood ratio statistic has
  its chi square reference,** and that the null hypothesis of no
  indirect effect is not regular where both coefficients are zero.
  There, in the single mediator model with observed variables, the test
  at the .05 level rejects with probability .05 squared, .0025, in large
  samples (between .0025 and .05 when the estimates are correlated), so
  it is conservative. The page gives this limit beside the rejection
  rates of .025 to .075 that Tofighi and Kelley (2020) report from
  simulations in which one coefficient of the indirect effect is zero,
  and says what each describes.

- **[`ss_power_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_reg_coef.md)
  and
  [`ss_power_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_rc.md)
  check `p` on every route:** a single whole number of at least 1.
  `p = 2.5` returned `necessary_N` = 47.5 (`true_f2 = .2`), `p = 0` and
  `p = -1` returned 47, and the route through `true_reg_coef_j` stopped
  with “argument is of length zero” when `p` was left out. Each is now
  refused with a condition of class `dmar_argument_invalid`
  (`arg = "p"`).

- **[`ss_power_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_reg_coef.md)
  and
  [`ss_power_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_rc.md)
  plan for a single predictor given through `true_cor_XX` and
  `true_cor_YX`.**
  `ss_power_reg_coef(true_cor_XX = matrix(1, 1, 1), true_cor_YX = .3, which_predictor = 1)`
  stopped with `'a' is 0-diml` and returns `necessary_N` = 93, the
  result of `true_f2 = .09 / .91` with `p = 1`. `which_predictor` must
  be a whole number from 1 to `p`, `true_cor_XX` a correlation matrix,
  and `true_cor_YX` possible with it (a squared multiple correlation
  below 1); each is checked by name.

- **[`ss_power_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_reg_coef.md)
  and
  [`ss_power_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_rc.md)
  refuse at once a sample size for an effect of 0 when `desired_power`
  is above `alpha_level`,** with a condition of class
  `dmar_effect_zero`, since the power is then `alpha_level` at every
  sample size; the search ran to N = 10,000,000 (about 40 seconds) and
  stopped with class `dmar_computation_failed`. An effect too small for
  any sample size up to 10,000,000 to reach `desired_power` is refused
  at once with that class. Both inherit `dmar_refusal`.

- **[`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md)
  plans for one predictor on the covariance structure path.**
  `true_cor_XX = matrix(1)` with `p = 1` stopped with “the condition has
  length \> 1” (and, with `true_reg_coef_j` given,
  `object 'b_j_tmp' not found`); it now returns the plan of the direct
  path (327 for a correlation of .4 and `width = .2`), and `p` and
  `which_predictor` follow from a 1 x 1 matrix.

- **[`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md)
  check a supplied `true_reg_coef_j` on the covariance structure path
  against the coefficient on the scale `true_sd_Y` and `true_sd_X`
  describe.** With `true_sd_Y = 2` and `true_sd_X = 1` the correct
  coefficient .681 was refused and the standardized .341 accepted. The
  plan is unchanged; the refusal now gives both values.

- **[`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md),
  [`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md),
  and [`ci_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_src.md)
  state the conditions of the function they call in their own argument
  names** (for example `true_std_reg_coef_j`, not `true_reg_coef_j`, in
  [`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md)).
  [`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md)
  refuses `true_sd_Y` or `true_sd_X` other than 1 itself, saying that it
  plans for the standardized coefficient and
  [`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md)
  for the unstandardized one; the refusal had spoken of
  ‘noncentral=TRUE’, which the user had not given.

- **[`ci_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_src.md)
  without a coefficient is refused by name,** where it stopped with
  “argument is of length zero”; it takes the coefficient from `t` with
  its standard error, from `t` with `R2_Y_X` and `R2_j_X_without_j`, or
  from the three squared multiple correlations. The warning that a
  standardized coefficient is unusually large applies beyond 1.1 in
  either direction, not only to positive values.
  [`ci_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_rc.md) and
  [`ci_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_reg_coef.md)
  take `reg_coef_j = NULL` by default, for the routes on which the other
  inputs determine the coefficient, and
  [`ci_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_rc.md)
  reports that coefficient between its limits.

- **[`ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity.md)
  refuses a missing `true_var_Y`** (with `noncentral = FALSE` it built a
  covariance matrix of the wrong size), a `which_predictor` outside 1 to
  `p`, and a `specified_N` that is not a whole number of at least
  `p + 2`.

- **[`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.md)
  differs from DMAR 1.0.0 when the variances of *Y* and of the targeted
  predictor differ.** For `true_var_Y = 4`, `true_cov_YX = c(.8, .6)`,
  unit predictor variances correlated .3, supposed correctly,
  `width = .3`, and `noncentral = FALSE`, DMAR 1.0.0 planned 610 (657
  with `assurance = .9`) and judged the intervals against .681; this
  release plans 156 (with `assurance = .9`, 181 by default and 171 with
  `assurance_method = "simulation"` and `seed = 1`) and judges them
  against .341. A call with one predictor and `specified_N`, which DMAR
  1.0.0 answered, changes as well: with `true_var_Y = 4`,
  `true_cov_YX = .8`, `true_cov_XX = matrix(1)`, and `specified_N = 100`
  it judged the intervals against .8, where this release judges them
  against .4. With equal variances of *Y* and of the targeted predictor
  (unit ones, or every variance 4), whatever the variances of the other
  predictors, and two or more predictors, the calls without `assurance`
  and those with `assurance` and the default `assurance_method` return
  the 1.0.0 table, to rounding error, with the same draws at the same
  sample size, plan a case below 1.0.0 (156 and 181 here, 157 and 182 in
  1.0.0; see Changes to Earlier Results).
  [`ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity.md)
  plan with the supposed standard deviations, as 1.0.x did (609 here
  without `assurance` and 672, the exact central plan, with
  `assurance = .9`, where 1.0.x planned 610 and 657), and need no such
  change; for their plans with one predictor see the next entry.

- **The regression sensitivity functions plan the calls DMAR 1.0.x
  refused.** In
  [`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.md)
  a noncentral plan (the default) from a supposed variance of *Y* or of
  the targeted predictor other than 1 was refused by DMAR 1.0.0 (“Since
  you’ve specified ‘noncentral=TRUE’, all variances should be one”); for
  `true_var_Y = 4` and `assurance = .9` this release plans 179 (176 with
  `assurance_method = "simulation"` and `seed = 1`). (DMAR 1.0.0
  answered a call in which only a predictor that is not targeted has a
  variance other than 1.) DMAR 1.0.0 also stopped on every call of
  [`ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity.md),
  [`ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.md)
  that planned the sample size with one predictor, for either interval
  and with or without `assurance` (“argument is of length zero”, or, for
  a noncentral plan from a supposed variance of *Y* other than 1, the
  refusal above). This release plans these calls: for `true_var_Y = 1`,
  `true_cov_YX = .4`, `true_cov_XX = matrix(1)`, `width = .3`,
  `noncentral = FALSE`, `assurance = .9`, and `seed = 1`,
  [`ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef_sensitivity.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc_sensitivity.md)
  plan 178 and
  [`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.md)
  171 (159 with `assurance_method = "simulation"`), and the noncentral
  plans are 172 (165 with `"simulation"`). With `true_var_Y = 4` and
  `true_cov_YX = .8`,
  [`ss_aipe_src_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src_sensitivity.md)
  plans the same sample sizes, and the central plans of the other two
  functions are 639.

- **The upper quantiles of the intervals and plans of a regression
  coefficient, a contrast, and a correlation are taken in the upper
  tail.**
  [`ci_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_reg_coef.md)
  with `noncentral = FALSE`,
  [`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md),
  [`ci_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_correlation.md),
  the central plans of
  [`ss_aipe_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md),
  [`ss_aipe_rc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md)
  and the exact central assurance step of the first two, the simulated
  central step of
  [`ss_aipe_src()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md)
  formed an upper quantile as `qt(1 - alpha, df)` or `qnorm(1 - alpha)`.
  1 - alpha rounds a small tail area away, and it is exactly 1 for a
  tail of 2^-54 or less, where the quantile is `Inf`. That is how
  [`ci_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c.md) and the
  central
  [`ci_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_reg_coef.md)
  returned an upper limit of `Inf`, and
  [`ci_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_correlation.md)
  a limit of 1 or -1, at a tail of 1e-20 in DMAR 1.0.0 and the
  development versions of 1.1.0. Each quantile is now
  `qt(alpha, df, lower.tail = FALSE)` (or the
  [`qnorm()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/Normal.html) counterpart), exact
  at any tail. A tail that small is now refused (see Calls That Are Now
  Refused); above the floor the change is in the last digits at the
  usual levels and in about the eighth or ninth significant digit near
  the floor (see Changes to Earlier Results).

- **The help of the regression coefficient planners describes what they
  plan for.** In
  [`?ss_aipe_reg_coef`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reg_coef.md),
  [`?ss_aipe_src`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_src.md),
  and
  [`?ss_aipe_rc`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rc.md),
  the plan without `assurance` was called the plan for the expected
  width. It is the plan for the width at the expected values of the two
  sample squared multiple correlations, which is not the mean width over
  samples, as Details already defined it. On the squared multiple
  correlations path, the noncentral and standardized assurance step was
  said to take the smallest probability over every value of the
  correlation of *Y* with the targeted predictor that the planning
  values allow, “so the sample size suffices whatever it is”. It takes
  the smallest over 21 equally spaced values across that range, an
  approximate minimum: between two of them the probability can be a
  little lower, and the plan a little short of the request. With *p* = 2
  the two ends are the only possible values. The help also said the
  simulated estimate rises with *N*. The search assumes that it does not
  decrease, which held in every set checked, although single simulated
  intervals were wider at *N* + 1 in 3,208 of 95 million comparisons. No
  result changes.

- **[`ss_aipe_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_R2.md)
  plans for an abbreviated `which_width`.** The function checked
  `which_width` with
  [`char.expand()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/char.expand.html) and
  discarded the expanded value, so an abbreviation matched none of the
  three plans and the function returned `NULL`. In DMAR 1.0.0,
  `ss_aipe_R2(true_R2 = .5, width = .15, which_width = "L", p = 5, random_predictors = FALSE)`
  (`population_R2` in 1.0.x) returned `NULL`, as did `"F"`, `"Fu"`,
  `"Lo"`, `"U"`, and `"Up"`. It now gives 117, the plan of `"Lower"`;
  `"F"` gives 264, the plan of `"Full"`, and `"Up"` gives 13, the plan
  of `"Upper"`. An abbreviation is expanded as
  [`match.arg()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/match.arg.html) expands it in
  the other planners whose `which_width` lists the three values.

- **[`cohen_f()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cohen_f.md)
  refuses a specification it cannot read as one.** It computes *f* from
  `means` with `var_within`, from `eta_squared`, or from `sd_means` with
  `sd_within`, and an argument of one of these given with an argument of
  another was ignored: in DMAR 1.0.x,
  `cohen_f(eta_squared = .10, mu = c(1, 2))` returned .333, the *f* of
  eta squared. Such a call, one half of a pair given alone,
  `n_per_group` without `means`, a vector where one number is needed,
  and a missing value among `means` are refused with a condition of
  class `dmar_argument_invalid` that names the arguments.

- **[`ci_srsnr()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_srsnr.md)
  with `means` refuses `df_1`, `df_2`, or `N` that disagree with the
  group sizes, and group sizes that are not whole numbers.** They were
  replaced without a word:
  `ci_srsnr(means = c(94, 91, 92, 83), var_within = 67.375, n_per_group = 6, N = 100)`
  ran with N = 24, and `n_per_group = c(7.5, 8, 9)` ran with 21.5
  denominator degrees of freedom. `var_within` or `n_per_group` without
  `means`, which was ignored, is refused, and the refusal of equal group
  means (an *F* of 0) names `means`, not `F_value`.

- **[`omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/omega_squared.md)
  returns a DMAR table** of class `dmar_anova_es`, as
  [`eta_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/eta_squared.md)
  does, so it prints with the package’s display and has `tidy()` and
  `glance()` methods; through 1.0.x it returned a plain `data.frame`.

- **[`omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/omega_squared.md)
  and
  [`ci_omega_squared()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_omega_squared.md)
  accept `F_value = 0`** and report 0; through 1.0.x they refused it.

- **[`plot_ci()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_ci.md)
  draws the estimates of
  [`ci_eta_squared_generalized()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_eta_squared_generalized.md),**
  where it plotted the midpoint of each interval.

- **[`ci_proportion()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_proportion.md)
  keeps every Wilson limit in \[0, 1\], with a lower limit of exactly 0
  at 0 successes and an upper limit of exactly 1 at N successes.** In
  floating point those limits came back a few units in the last place
  either side of 0 or 1 (as low as -5.6e-17, as high as 1 + 2.2e-16).
  Every other limit is unchanged. The Wald interval is not clamped.

- **[`ci_games_howell()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_games_howell.md)
  gives limits and a *p*-value for a pair whose Welch degrees of freedom
  fall below 2,** where R’s
  [`qtukey()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/Tukey.html) and
  [`ptukey()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/Tukey.html) return `NaN`. With
  groups a = (1.2, 2.9), b = (3.1, 5.5), and c = (4.0, 7.9, 6.1), the
  b - a pair (1.80 df) had `NA` limits and *p*-value and has \[-7.516,
  12.016\] and *p* = .4499. With two groups the interval and *p*-value
  equal those of `t.test(var.equal = FALSE)` below 2 df as well.
  [`cv_tukey_hsd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cv_tukey_hsd.md),
  [`ci_tukey_kramer()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_tukey_kramer.md),
  `contrast_test(adjust = "tukey")`, and
  `qbryant_paulson(n_covariates = 0)` likewise return the critical value
  below 2 error df (`cv_tukey_hsd(.05, df = 1.5, n_groups = 4)` is
  10.189), and a critical value R’s
  [`qtukey()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/Tukey.html) fails to find
  (`qtukey(.25, 51, 32)` stops with “convergence failed”) is computed as
  the root of the exact distribution function.

- **[`contrast_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/contrast_test.md)
  no longer returns `NA` standard errors when a group has a single
  observation,** whose variance is `NA` in R though its weight in the
  pooled error variance is zero. For 20 groups of which two have a
  second observation (2 error df), the standard error of the “2 - 1”
  contrast was `NA` and is 0.2008, from the residual mean square of the
  one-way fit.

- **[`format_p()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/format_p.md)
  refuses a `digits_p` that is not a whole number from 1 to 324,** with
  a condition of class `dmar_argument_invalid`;
  `format_p(.123456, digits_p = 3.9)` returned “0.123”. Its help page
  says that it formats and does not check its input. A refusal that
  names the value given shows it to 15 significant digits when 7 would
  show a different number (a `digits_p` of 1 + 1e-12 was named as “1”).

- **[`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md)
  judges contrast weights by their values.** It compared the sum of the
  positive weights with 1 by
  [`identical()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/identical.html), which also
  compares the storage type and every bit: `c_weights = c(1L, -1L)` or
  `-1:1` stopped with “Please use fractions to specify the contrast
  weights”, and `c(.7, .2, .1, -1)` was refused while
  `c(.1, .2, .7, -1)` was accepted.
  [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md),
  and
  [`ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_sensitivity.md)
  now apply one rule to the values of the weights (the positive values
  sum to 1 within 1e-8), with one set of messages, and weights given as
  text are refused with class `dmar_argument_invalid` (they stopped with
  “invalid ‘type’ (character) of argument”).

- **[`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md)
  with `assurance` plans a negative contrast with unequal tails as its
  magnitude with `alpha_lower` and `alpha_upper` exchanged,** since the
  [`ci_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_sc.md)
  interval at -*t* is the reflection of the interval at *t* with the
  tails exchanged. It kept the tails as given, so the interval could be
  too wide more often than the request allowed (see Changes to Earlier
  Results).

- **[`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md)
  plans wide targets and correlations near 1.** Its plan without
  `assurance` let the sample size fall below 2 per group, where the
  error degrees of freedom are 0 or below:
  `ss_aipe_sc_ancova(true_std_contrast = .5, true_cor = .5, divisor = "s_anova", c_weights = c(1, -1), width = 3.6)`
  did not return, and `width = 5` with `divisor = "s_ancova"`, or
  `true_cor = .999` with `divisor = "s_anova"` and `width = .5`, stopped
  with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”. The plan is now at least
  2 per group, and these give 2, 2, and 6, the smallest sample sizes
  that meet the widths (see Changes to Earlier Results).

- **[`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md)
  and
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md)
  find the plan without `assurance` by doubling a step and bisecting,**
  not by raising the sample size by one, so a narrow target no longer
  takes seconds or minutes, and a plan the 1.0.0 search did not finish,
  such as `width = 1e-5` (about 3e11 per group), is returned. The plans
  of
  [`ss_aipe_sc()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc.md)
  are unchanged:
  `ss_aipe_sc(true_std_contrast = .5, c_weights = c(1, -1), width = .01)`,
  316,921 per group, took 3 seconds and takes under a second.
  [`ss_aipe_sc_ancova()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sc_ancova.md)
  starts the search at 2 per group, and some of its plans are smaller
  (see Changes to Earlier Results).

- **[`ss_power_indirect_effect()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_indirect_effect.md)
  returns a sample size that attains `desired_power` in data drawn from
  the model it plans for.** It took the power of each path test with the
  noncentrality fixed at the population standard error, as if the sum of
  squares of X were N and the residual sum of squares of the mediator
  given X were its expectation, and took the joint significance power as
  the product of the two path powers. In a study both sums of squares
  vary from sample to sample (that of the mediator in every design,
  since the mediator is measured, and that of X when X is measured), and
  the two tests are not independent, since the residual sum of squares
  of the mediator is the error sum of squares of the test of *a* and the
  predictor sum of squares of the test of *b*. So the reported power was
  too high: its plan of 65 for paths of .39 and power .80 has a power of
  .7675. The power of each path test is now its noncentral *t* power
  averaged over the chi square distributions of those sums of squares,
  and the joint significance power is the probability that both tests
  reject, computed given the residual sum of squares of the mediator,
  given which the two tests are independent; the plan is 69, with power
  .8010. The new argument `random_predictors`, `TRUE` by default as in
  [`ss_power_R2_change()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_R2_change.md)
  and
  [`ci_R()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_correlation.md),
  makes X random (normal), as when it is measured; `FALSE` fixes X by
  design, with variance 1 computed with divisor N (two groups of equal
  size, for example). The mediator is random under either setting, and
  the setting is recorded in the `"random_predictors"` attribute. The
  help said that the tests validated the result against raw-data
  simulation; the test then allowed a relative error of 6 percent, and
  it now requires agreement within four Monte Carlo standard errors, at
  the plan and at one case fewer, for either test and either predictor
  model.

- **The Sobel power of
  [`ss_power_indirect_effect()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_indirect_effect.md)
  is the probability that the Sobel test rejects.** DMAR 1.0.x referred
  \|ab\| / se_ab, with population standard errors, to the normal
  distribution. The first-order Sobel statistic that
  [`mediate()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediate.md)
  uses is t_a t_b / sqrt(t_a^2 + t_b^2), in the *t* statistics of the
  two paths; it is not normal with unit variance, and the approximation
  erred in either direction: at N = 96 with paths of .39 it gave .8026
  where the power is .8818, so its plan for .80 was 96 where 84 suffice,
  and at N = 12 with paths of .6 and .5 and a direct effect of .2 it
  gave .3165 where the power is .1226. The power is now the probability
  that 1 / t_a^2 + 1 / t_b^2 is below 1 / z^2 under the joint sampling
  distribution of the two statistics.

  The probability is an integral over \|t_a\| that
  [`integrate()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/integrate.html) computes in
  pieces, and development versions of 1.1.0, which no release carried,
  computed it with three faults that are now fixed. First, they stopped
  with an error of class `dmar_computation_failed` whenever
  [`integrate()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/integrate.html) returned a
  piece with a roundoff status, as it does for pieces next to the
  critical value z that are worth almost nothing (less than 1e-45 in
  this call):
  `ss_power_indirect_effect(.2, .1, specified_N = 10, alpha_level = .999, method = "sobel")`
  stopped with “The power of the Sobel test at N = 10 could not be
  computed reliably: the numerical integral over the distribution of the
  path t statistics failed (roundoff error is detected in the
  extrapolation table).” and is .9983 (DMAR 1.0.x gave .9990; see
  Changes to Earlier Results). In a grid of 5,760 Sobel powers
  (`alpha_level` from .000001 to .99999, paths from .02 to .95, N from
  10 to 1,000,000, X random and fixed) they refused 664, at
  `alpha_level` .995 (two, both at N = 1,000,000), .998, .999, .9995,
  .9999, and .99999, and a path near 1 brought the refusal to ordinary
  levels:
  `ss_power_indirect_effect(.39, .999999, specified_N = 10, alpha_level = .5, method = "sobel")`
  was refused and is .7457. A piece with either roundoff status
  (“roundoff error was detected” or “roundoff error is detected in the
  extrapolation table”) is now accepted when its estimated absolute
  error is finite and at most its share of 1e-9 and its value is at
  least minus that share, so the power carries an estimated quadrature
  error below 1.2e-9; the largest such piece in the grid was worth
  2.9e-19. A piece returned “OK” is accepted whatever its error
  estimate, as before. A roundoff piece over its share is refused with
  class `dmar_computation_failed` and the message “… failed (`<status>`,
  with an estimated absolute error of `<e>` against a budget of `<b>`
  for this piece). The joint significance test (method
  =”joint_significance”) does not need this integral.”; every other
  status of [`integrate()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/integrate.html) is
  refused as before. Second, at `alpha_level` of .99999 and above, the
  lower end of the integral can round to just below z, where the
  integrand was NaN: 40 of the 664, among them
  `ss_power_indirect_effect(.95, .3, specified_N = 10, alpha_level = .99999, method = "sobel")`,
  stopped with “… failed (non-finite function value).” and the warning
  “NaNs produced”. The Sobel test cannot reject at \|t_a\| \<= z, so the
  integrand is now 0 there, and that call gives .999991. Third, with X
  random and \|a\| near 1, the density of \|t_a\| has a separate peak at
  each node of the distribution of the sum of squares of X, and
  [`integrate()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/integrate.html) stepped over
  some of them:
  `ss_power_indirect_effect(.999999, .5, specified_N = 10, alpha_level = .5, method = "sobel")`
  gave .3521 where the power is .5216, and the plan
  `ss_power_indirect_effect(.999999, .5, desired_power = .52, alpha_level = .5, method = "sobel")`
  stopped at ten million where it is 10. Once two neighboring peaks
  stand more than 2 standard deviations apart, which takes \|a\| above
  about .9, each peak gets pieces of its own. No call in the grid is now
  refused or warns, and none of 270 plans at `alpha_level` up to .99999
  is refused (126 were). In the grid of 5,760 the powers that both
  computed agree within 3e-15. In a second grid of 2,520 powers with X
  random (\|a\| from .85 to .999999, b from .02 to .999999, N from 10 to
  100,000, `alpha_level` from .001 to .999), of which they refused 130,
  the powers that both computed agree within 5e-14 at \|a\| up to .999;
  at \|a\| = .9999 they move by up to 2e-7, and at .99999 and .999999 by
  up to .23 and .97, and the plan
  `ss_power_indirect_effect(.99999, .2, desired_power = .80, method = "sobel")`
  moves from 9,418,685 to 9,418,684. The new values agree with
  independent integrals that share no code with the function to 3e-11 or
  better (`alpha_level` up to .999999, paths up to .999999), and with
  2,000,000-draw Monte Carlo estimates within 4 standard errors in 360
  settings with \|a\| from .9999 to .999999.

- **The Bryant-Paulson distribution with covariates is computed at large
  error df and with many covariates.** From about 4 x 10^7 error df with
  one covariate (5.6 x 10^7 with six, 10^8 with 30),
  [`pbryant_paulson()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bryant_paulson.md)
  returned about 0
  (`pbryant_paulson(3.7, n_covariates = 1, n_groups = 4, df = 1e8)` was
  5.6e-25, where the probability is .956), and
  [`qbryant_paulson()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/bryant_paulson.md),
  [`cv_bryant_paulson()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cv_bryant_paulson.md),
  and
  [`ci_c_ancova_bp()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova_bp.md)
  stopped with [`uniroot()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/uniroot.html)’s
  “f() values at end points not of opposite sign” or, at the edge of
  that range, returned a critical value that was too large
  (`qbryant_paulson(.95, n_covariates = 1, n_groups = 4, df = 4.09e7)`
  was 4.5327, where it is 3.6332). `df = Inf` stopped with “non-finite
  function value”. With 40 or more covariates the same failures began at
  smaller df: about 3 x 10^6 with 40 covariates, 10^6 with 150, 1.3 x
  10^5 with 200, and 1.6 x 10^4 with 300. At large df the weight of the
  integral over the covariate shrinkage factor lies within a few
  multiples of sqrt(p / df) of one end of its range, where the
  quadrature over the whole range did not find it, and with many
  covariates the factors of the weight overflowed and underflowed apart.
  The integral now stops where all but 1e-15 of the weight lies, the
  weight is computed on the log scale, and with `df = Inf` the functions
  return the studentized range at infinite df, as they do with no
  covariates.

- **The help of `seed` in the standardized cluster randomized planners,
  [`mediate()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediate.md),
  [`plot_mediation_mbco()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/plot_mediation_mbco.md),
  [`ci_eta_squared_generalized()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_eta_squared_generalized.md),
  [`mediation_mbco()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediation_mbco.md),
  [`ss_aipe_indirect_effect()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_indirect_effect.md),
  and
  [`measurement_alignment()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_alignment.md)
  says what `seed = NULL` does:** it draws from the current random
  number stream and advances it. The help said that it left the
  generator’s state unchanged.

- **Help pages state what the code computes and attribute claims to
  their sources.** Documentation only; no function, argument, output
  row, or value changed.
  [`?ci_src`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_src.md) and
  [`?ci_reg_coef`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_reg_coef.md)
  say that the standard error of a standardized coefficient treats the
  sample standard deviations as fixed (Kelley & Maxwell, 2003,
  pp. 315–316), so it is approximate, and give the coverage of the
  intervals in simulations;
  [`?ci_c_ancova_bp`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_c_ancova_bp.md)
  says how much wider the Bryant-Paulson intervals are than Tukey’s (84
  percent with three covariates and 2 error df at alpha = .05);
  [`?var_alpha`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_alpha.md)
  attributes the *N* - 1 form to van Zyl, Neudecker, and Nel

  2000. and the *N* - 2 form to Bonett (2003), as the rows now do; and
        [`?ss_aipe_pcm`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_pcm.md),
        [`?irt_grm`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/irt_grm.md),
        [`?irt_information`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/irt_information.md),
        [`?mr_cv`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_cv.md),
        [`?mr_smd`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mr_smd.md),
        [`?skewness`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/skewness.md),
        [`?kurtosis`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/kurtosis.md),
        [`?descriptives`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/descriptives.md),
        and the pages of four power functions define their arguments,
        columns, and formulas. Statements the code, the data, or the
        cited source do not bear out are corrected or attributed on the
        pages of
        [`correlations_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/correlations_test.md),
        [`ci_ratio_of_means()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_ratio_of_means.md),
        [`ci_ratio_of_means_paired()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_ratio_of_means_paired.md),
        [`ci_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_smd.md),
        [`expected_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/expected_smd.md),
        [`var_smd()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_smd.md),
        [`var_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/var_r.md),
        [`expected_r()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/expected_r.md),
        [`ci_proportion()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_proportion.md),
        [`krippendorff_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/krippendorff_alpha.md),
        [`gwet_ac()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/gwet_ac.md),
        [`equivalence_c()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/equivalence_c.md),
        [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
        [`obrien_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/obrien_test.md),
        [`manova_split_plot()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/manova_split_plot.md),
        [`welch_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/welch_t.md),
        [`summary_t_test()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/summary_t_test.md),
        [`randomization_test_paired()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/randomization_test_paired.md),
        `teacher_expectancy`, `prime_time_achievement`, and
        `holzinger_swineford`, and
        [`?DMAR`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/DMAR-package.md)
        and the pages of more than thirty functions and data sets
        describe the package without praise or unsupported claims
        (“modern”, “easy to use”, “the most general”, and the like).

- **Refusal messages state the requirement instead of the user’s
  error.**
  [`ci_reg_coef()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_reg_coef.md)
  said “You have not properly specified ‘alpha_lower’ correctly.” and
  says “‘alpha_lower’ must be between 0 and .5.”;
  [`convert_R2_f()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/convert_R2.md)
  and
  [`convert_f_R2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/convert_R2.md)
  say “Specify both ‘df_1’ and ‘df_2’, or omit both and specify ‘N’ and
  ‘p’.”; and
  [`reliability_alpha()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_alpha.md)
  and
  [`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md)
  say that DMAR offers no ADF interval under that treatment of missing
  data, rather than that none exists. The condition classes are
  unchanged.

- **The vignettes, the README, and DESCRIPTION are corrected.**
  Documentation only. Rd markup that pandoc left out of the HTML of four
  vignettes is Markdown now. The vignettes and the README no longer say
  that every `ci_*()` function inverts a noncentral distribution, that
  every plot shows a confidence interval and the sample size, or that
  every result is a data frame of `term` and `value` rows; their tables
  of argument names give the 1.1.0 names; they and the DESCRIPTION
  describe the package and MBESS in factual terms; and the README’s
  suggested citation gives the version as 1.1.0.

- **The refusals of
  [`ci_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_cv.md) name
  the argument at issue.** With `cv` and no `N`, the condition’s `arg`
  is `N`, the argument that is missing. `data` given together with `cv`
  is refused with “Give either ‘data’, or ‘cv’ with ‘N’, not both.”,
  where DMAR 1.0.0 asked for the sample size. A `mean` or an `sd` that
  is not a single finite number is refused by name;
  `ci_cv(mean = 5, sd = "a", N = 30)` (`n` in 1.0.x) stopped with
  “non-numeric argument to binary operator”. A sample mean that is not
  positive has one message, whether it was given as `mean` or computed
  from `data`, which states the value and that the interval requires a
  positive mean and a positive standard deviation; it no longer asks
  whether taking the absolute value of the mean makes sense.

### Changes to Earlier Results

- **[`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  plans on the expected value of the sample coefficient of variation
  again, as Kelley (2007) does.** The method (Kelley, 2007, p. 758)
  evaluates the width at E\[k \| kappa, N\] of the paper’s Equation 3 at
  each candidate sample size. DMAR 1.0.x evaluated it at the population
  value multiplied by (1 + 1/(4N)), the nearly unbiased estimate of
  Equation 4, which is above the population value where the expected
  value is below it. The cause is inherited: MBESS through 3.3.3
  computed Equation 3 inside `cv(unbiased = TRUE)`, which the planner
  called; [`cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cv.md) was
  later changed to the Equation 4 multiplier and the planner followed it
  without being edited. Of 34 expected-width conditions of the paper’s
  Table 1 the earlier value was the tabled one in 10 and one larger in
  24; of 16 conditions with assurance .99 it was one to three larger in
  all 16. The function now returns the tabled value in 39 of the 50 (24
  of the 34 and 15 of the 16), and 101 and 142 for the paper’s worked
  example (`true_cv = .25`, `width = .10`, `conf_level = .99`, without
  and with `assurance = .99`), where the paper gives 99 and 141 and DMAR
  1.0.x returned 100 and 142. The tables were computed with R’s
  approximation to the noncentral *t* distribution, and the function now
  plans for the exact interval of
  [`ci_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_cv.md) (see
  the entry on that change below). The help states how the returned
  sample size relates to the expected width itself.
  [`ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity.md),
  which plans through
  [`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  when no sample size is given, changes with it.

- **The population coefficient of variation in
  [`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  is the argument `true_cv`** (it was `C_of_V`), the name the data
  generating value has in
  [`ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity.md).
  `C_of_V` is not accepted. See Breaking Changes in 1.1.0.

- **[`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  with `assurance` is the published procedure of Kelley (2007), for any
  assurance strictly between 0 and 1.** Two rows of the tables of that
  article show a misprint. Table 1, assurance .80, width .125,
  coefficient of variation .40 prints 127, between 69 and 122 in its
  row; the procedure gives 93. Table 3, assurance .80, width .010 prints
  14,279; 28,321; 50,209; 38,120; and 82,817 for coefficients of
  variation of .30 to .50, which do not increase; the procedure gives
  14,279; 20,475; 28,321; 38,120; and 50,209 with R’s approximation to
  the noncentral *t* distribution, with which the tables were computed.
  How the plans of the exact distribution compare with the printed
  values is in the entry on the exact interval below. The help page
  describes the step as it is computed: the search is run for the value
  of the article’s Equation 3 at the quantile of the sample coefficient,
  and applies Equation 3 to that value again at each sample size. With
  R’s approximation this computation gives the printed value in 524 of
  the 528 assurance cells (the other four are the misprints), where the
  search for the quantile itself, as the article’s text words the step
  (p. 759), gives it in 365. The result has one row, `necessary_N`, with
  or without `assurance`, as in 1.0.x. `assurance` had to be above .50
  and may now be any probability strictly between 0 and 1; a value such
  as .50 asks that the realized interval be no wider than `width` in
  about half of the studies that could be run. A malformed `assurance`
  (a vector, a character string, `NA`) or one outside (0, 1) stops with
  one refusal, of class `dmar_assurance_invalid`, that states the value
  given, why neither 0 nor 1 is accepted, and what to give, where R’s
  own errors appeared. The procedure is a close approximation and not an
  exact search. With the exact distribution, in the 488 printed cells
  with an assurance and at most 5,000 cases, the probability that the
  realized interval is no wider than `width` at the returned sample size
  is .744 to .902 where .80 was requested (below .80 in 37 of 244) and
  .9916 to .9997 where .99 was requested, and away from the published
  tables it can fall below the request (.587 for a requested .60 with
  `true_cv = .22`, `width = .09`, and a 95 percent interval, where the
  function returns 57). The shortfall grows as the request falls toward
  .50: in 105 plans at 95 percent confidence the probability is below
  the request by at most .038 for .50, .036 for .55, .058 for .60, .032
  for .70, and .001 for .80, and by nothing for .90 and .99; and a
  request of .50 returns one fewer than the plan without `assurance` in
  12 of 15 plans (17 against 18 for `true_cv = .05` and `width = .0375`,
  where the probability at 17 is .462). The help gives these numbers,
  and
  [`ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity.md)
  estimates the probability for any plan by simulation.

- **[`ss_aipe_sm()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sm.md)
  takes any assurance strictly between 0 and 1.** The assurance step
  plans for the value that the sample standardized mean exceeds in
  magnitude with probability `1 - assurance`, the one-sample form of the
  procedure of Kelley and Rausch (2006, Equations 18 to 20 and 25 to
  31), and that value is defined for every probability in (0, 1). DMAR
  1.0.x refused an `assurance` at or below .50. A value such as .50 asks
  that the interval be no wider than `width` in about half of the
  studies that could be run, and a value below about one half returns a
  smaller sample size than the plan without `assurance`: for
  `true_sm = 1`, `width = 0.5`, and a 95 percent interval the function
  returns 93 without `assurance`, 87 at .20, 93 at .50, 100 at .80, and
  105 at .90, where the probability that the interval is no wider than
  0.5, from the noncentral *t* distribution, is .228, .519, .812, and
  .925. An `assurance` that is not `NULL` or a single number strictly
  between 0 and 1 stops with the refusal of class
  `dmar_assurance_invalid` that
  [`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  gives. No result for an `assurance` above .50 changes for this reason
  (the exact interval of
  [`ci_nc_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_nc_t.md)
  changes a few plans by one or two; see the entry on the AIPE planners
  built on
  [`ci_nc_t()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_nc_t.md)).

- **[`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  plans for the exact interval of
  [`ci_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_cv.md), so
  it no longer returns every value printed in Kelley (2007).** The
  noncentrality of the interval, the square root of N over the
  coefficient of variation, passes 37.62 whenever the interval is
  narrow, and the assurance step also takes the noncentral *t* quantile
  exactly where R’s [`qt()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/TDist.html) inverts
  [`pt()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/TDist.html) (see Exact Noncentral *t*
  and Studentized Range Distributions). The tables of Kelley (2007) were
  computed with R’s approximation. Apart from the four misprinted cells
  (127 in Table 1; 28,321, 50,209, and 82,817 in Table 3; see the entry
  above on
  [`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  with `assurance`), the function returns the printed value in 468 of
  788 cells (the procedure computed with the approximation gives all
  788), one to three fewer cases in 232, and one to three more in 88; it
  returns every printed value with a width of .125 or more at 90 and 95
  percent confidence and 9 of the 120 with a width of .075 or less at 99
  percent. The worked example of the article (`true_cv = .25`,
  `width = .10`, `conf_level = .99`) gives 101, and 142 with
  `assurance = .99`, where the article gives 99 and 141 and DMAR 1.0.x
  gave 100 and 142: at 99 the interval at the expected value of the
  sample coefficient is .1006 wide, and .0999 by the approximation. For
  `true_cv = .10`, `width = .10`, and 99 percent the plan is 20 (printed
  19); for `.05`, `.05`, and 99 percent, 19 (printed 21). The help
  page’s numbers on the assurance step are recomputed with the exact
  distribution (see the entry above on
  [`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  with `assurance`). The warning
  [`ss_aipe_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv.md)
  gave when its search passed a noncentrality of 37.62 is gone.

- **[`ci_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_cv.md) no
  longer warns when its upper limit is infinite, and the tail columns at
  that limit hold the requested areas.** DMAR 1.0.0 warned “The computed
  confidence interval does not have the same coverage as the specified
  confidence interval.” and reported `prob_less` 1 and `prob_greater` 0
  on the upper limit. The interval does have the stated coverage. The
  upper limit is infinite when the square root of N over the sample
  coefficient is at most the 1 - `alpha_upper` quantile of the central
  *t* distribution on N - 1 degrees of freedom, and the infinite limit
  is part of the exact interval: in the 19,975 of 20,000 normal samples
  with a positive mean, for a coefficient of variation of .8 and N = 6,
  the upper limit of the 95 percent interval was infinite in 31 percent
  and coverage was .952, and with .5 and N = 5 it was infinite in 9
  percent and coverage was .948. `ci_cv(cv = 1.2, N = 6)` returns 0.571
  and `Inf` without a warning, with `prob_less` .975 and `prob_greater`
  .025 on the upper limit. No limit changes. The functions that call
  [`ci_cv()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ci_cv.md) are
  quiet with it:
  `ss_aipe_cv(true_cv = .45, width = .10, conf_level = .99)` (`C_of_V`
  in 1.0.x), whose search starts at a sample size where the limit is
  infinite, gave the warning once in DMAR 1.0.0 and gives none, with the
  plan unchanged by this; and
  [`ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_cv_sensitivity.md)
  gives one warning of its own for the replications with an infinite
  limit (see the entry on the replications it summarizes).

- **A fit whose likelihood has no maximum now stops, where DMAR 1.0.x
  reported a table or stopped with an unrelated error.** When an error
  variance has run off below zero along a ridge of the likelihood, which
  is flat or still rising there, lavaan’s optimizer stops where its
  steps stop gaining and reports convergence, and DMAR 1.0.x reported
  that point’s estimates, omega, and fit rows, with a warning about a
  Heywood case.
  [`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
  [`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
  [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md),
  [`cfa_2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_2.md),
  [`measurement_invariance()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_invariance.md),
  and
  [`measurement_alignment()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_alignment.md),
  and the single-factor fits behind
  [`reliability_omega()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/reliability_omega.md),
  now stop instead, for every output, with an error of class
  `dmar_no_maximum` that prints the lavaan code of the fit (see “A
  factor analysis or structural equation model fit whose likelihood has
  no maximum stops” above). On three items whose correlations have a
  negative product (the sample of the reliability tests, population
  correlations .4, .3, and -.05, N = 300), DMAR 1.0.0’s
  [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md),
  which deleted incomplete cases listwise by default, returned the table
  of the point where lavaan stopped, with an error variance of -1899 and
  an omega of 442; `cfa_1(missing = "listwise")` now stops. With that
  sample as one group and a sample of 300 from a population in which
  three items correlate .5 as another, DMAR 1.0.0’s
  [`measurement_alignment()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_alignment.md)
  aligned a configural fit that had stopped with a loading of 21.8 and
  an error variance of -475 in the first group and gave the second a
  factor variance of 1282; it now stops.
  [`ss_aipe_reliability()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reliability.md)
  counts a simulated sample with no maximum as an interval wider than
  `width`, and
  [`ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_reliability_sensitivity.md)
  sets such a replication aside, whatever its error variances sum to;
  DMAR 1.0.x used the interval of the point where lavaan stopped. A
  bootstrap replication with no maximum, whose estimate DMAR 1.0.x used,
  is set aside and counted among the replications that raised an error.
  A finite negative error variance, at a maximum of the likelihood, is
  reported as before.
  [`ss_aipe_composite_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_composite_sem.md),
  [`ss_power_composite_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_sem.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sem_path()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sem_path.md),
  [`ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity.md),
  and
  [`mediation_mbco()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediation_mbco.md)
  stop the same way when the fit they read their result from has no
  maximum: a planner’s fit of the analysis model to the population
  moments, or the lavaan fit from which
  [`mediation_mbco()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediation_mbco.md)
  starts its OpenMx fits. DMAR 1.0.x went on from the point where lavaan
  stopped. Given a lavaan fit (`std.lv = TRUE`, `meanstructure = TRUE`)
  in which those three items measure a mediator between two other
  variables,
  [`mediation_mbco()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/mediation_mbco.md)
  reported an indirect effect of -0.0000008 with a likelihood ratio
  statistic of 0; and for a single factor with free loadings fit to
  their covariance matrix,
  [`ss_aipe_sem_path()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sem_path.md)
  stopped with R’s “incorrect number of dimensions” and the composite
  planners said that the loading “gives no sampling variability”, errors
  that did not name the cause. A replication of the Monte Carlo of
  [`ss_aipe_composite_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_composite_sem.md),
  [`ss_power_composite_sem()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_power_composite_sem.md),
  or
  [`ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity.md)
  with no maximum, which DMAR 1.0.x kept, is set aside as one that did
  not converge.
  [`ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_rmsea_sensitivity.md),
  which reads only the chi square of its fits, is not checked, and its
  results change only as its own entries below describe (its default
  level and how its intervals are formed).

- **[`ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sem_path_sensitivity.md)
  passes the arguments in `...` to every fit, and
  [`ss_aipe_sem_path()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sem_path.md)
  adjusts its own fit’s plan for assurance.** The arguments in `...` go
  to [`lavaan::sem()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/lavaan/man/sem.html). DMAR
  1.0.x passed them to the planning fit to `supposed_cov_matrix` alone,
  so the fit to `true_cov_matrix`, which gives the population value of
  the path, and the fit to each simulated sample used lavaan’s defaults:
  with `std.lv = TRUE`, the path of the help’s population was planned in
  the metric that argument sets, where it is 0.577, and simulated and
  covered in the metric of a marker item, where it is 0.5. With an
  `assurance`,
  [`ss_aipe_sem_path()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/ss_aipe_sem_path.md)
  adjusted a sample size it read from a second fit of the model made
  without `...`, so the plan under `std.lv = TRUE` was adjusted from the
  plan of the default metric; it now adjusts the plan of the fit it
  reports, with one population fit fewer. Results change only when `...`
  is used, and an argument such as `bounds = "pos.var"`, which the
  refusal of a fit with no maximum names as a choice, now reaches every
  fit.

- **[`measurement_invariance()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_invariance.md)
  refuses an item named twice in `items`.** DMAR 1.0.x built the model
  `f =~ y1 + y1 + y2 + y3` from `items = c("y1", "y1", "y2", "y3")`,
  which lavaan (0.7-3) reads as the three-item model
  `f =~ y1 + y2 + y3`, so the ladder described one item fewer than the
  call named. The call now stops with an error of class
  `dmar_items_invalid` (reason `"duplicate"`), as
  [`measurement_alignment()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/measurement_alignment.md)
  and
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  refuse such `items`. Only `items` is checked for a repeat, since DMAR
  writes the model from it. An indicator repeated in lavaan syntax given
  as `model` is read by lavaan as one indicator, as before, and a named
  list given as `model` that names an item twice is refused as before,
  without the class.

- **[`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
  [`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
  [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md), and
  [`cfa_2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_2.md) take
  the standard errors that match the estimator by default.** `se` now
  defaults to `NULL`, which gives Huber-White (robust) standard errors
  under `estimator = "MLR"` and `"robust.sem"` under `"WLSMV"`; DMAR
  1.0.x defaulted to `se = "standard"` and passed it to lavaan under
  every estimator but with ordered items, so its MLR standard errors
  were the normal theory ones beside a robust test (for the second
  loading of a verbal factor of three Holzinger and Swineford tests,
  0.249 then and 0.213 now). `se = "standard"` gives the 1.0.x standard
  errors (checked against DMAR 1.0.0’s
  [`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md):
  identical).

- **[`fa_confirmatory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md)
  fits by full information maximum likelihood by default**, as
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  does, and
  [`cfa_k()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_confirmatory.md),
  [`cfa_1()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_1.md), and
  [`cfa_2()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/cfa_2.md)
  follow it. `missing = "listwise"` gives the listwise deletion that
  DMAR 1.0.x applied by default, and
  [`fa_exploratory()`](https://yelleknek.github.io/DMAR/reference/fa_exploratory.md)
  accepts it as well. With incomplete items the default now uses every
  case with an observed item, so the estimates, their standard errors,
  and N change. With complete data the estimates are unchanged, and for
  `estimator = "ML"` so are the chi square, CFI, TLI, and RMSEA; the
  standard errors come from the observed information, which lavaan uses
  under FIML and Savalei (2010) recommends with incomplete data, rather
  than the expected information, and moved by at most about 2 percent on
  the two factors of the examples. The item intercepts (`nu` rows) join
  the table, and AIC and BIC count them. With `estimator = "MLR"` FIML
  on complete data leaves the standard errors as listwise deletion gives
  them (DMAR 1.0.x took other ones under MLR; see the entry on `se`
  below), and the robust CFI and RMSEA are the corrected version 3
